articles.title: We're losing the night sky as light pollution makes it 10% brighter every year
articles.text:
Editor's take: I've always wanted to capture an image of the Milky Way galaxy – or, at the very least, see it with my own eyes in real time. I've got the photography know-how to pull off what would be a frame-worthy shot of our galaxy, as well as the desire to make it happen, but the opportunity simply hasn't presented itself yet. And if the statistics are to be believed, I might never get to cross this one off my bucket list.
Man-made light pollution is the culprit, and it's not just from above. You've no doubt heard of the growing headache that orbiting satellites are causing astronomers trying to photograph the night skies. Compounding the matter is the modern amenity that is artificial light on the ground. Thanks to technologies like LED lighting, large cities and neighborhoods are brighter than ever.
And we're not just talking small numbers here. According to one report, the average night sky got brighter by 9.6% per year from 2011 to 2022. That equates to a roughly doubling of the sky's brightness every eight years. Another study notes that four out of five people live under light-polluted skies. Given those odds, it's likely that you've never even seen the night sky as it was intended.
As Tove Danovich with The Guardian highlights, access to a dark sky is about more than just stargazing. Light pollution can confuse nocturnal animals that use moonlight to navigate, and being in a brightly lit environment around the clock can throw off the circadian rhythm of most all living creatures – humans included.
Some communities are already taking steps to reduce ground-based light pollution. Flagstaff, Arizona, has rules in place to regulate how much light can be used at night, what type, and where it can legally shine. New York state is also considering similar restrictions. But as Danovich correctly notes, such restrictions do nothing to combat space-based light pollution sources like satellites designed to beam sunlight to Earth at night.
Indeed, it feels like darkness is quickly becoming a luxury.

articles.title: Gong adds auto-enrichment and event-driven agents to its revenue intelligence platform - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Gong adds auto-enrichment and event-driven agents to its revenue intelligence platform
Revenue intelligence startup Gong is expanding its platform with third-party account and contact data, deeper artificial intelligence analysis and tools for building agents that automatically execute sales workflows.
The company used its Gong Celebrate conference in Las Vegas today to launch Mission Callisto, a new feature of its Gong Enrich data enrichment platform that brings information from outside data providers into its Revenue Graph analytical and reporting engine. The release also adds deep research to Gong Assistant and expands dashboards beyond forecasting to track performance across sales, marketing and customer success.
Gong, the business name of Gong.io Ltd., said the updates address a common problem facing revenue teams: Customer conversations and sales activity provide useful context, but they don’t necessarily contain the current contact information and account details sellers need to reach prospects. Missing or outdated records can also limit what AI assistants and agents can access.
“Gong Enrich adds data that may not exist in either place,” co-founder and Chief Product Officer Eilon Reshef said, referring to its Revenue Graph and customer relationship management records. “By bringing information from multiple third-party data providers directly into Gong, teams can fill those gaps and give Gong’s AI and agents a more complete picture of every account and contact.”
Customers can connect to supported data providers and set the order in which Gong queries them. If a provider can’t supply the requested information, Gong moves to the next one on the list.
Customers can use existing subscriptions and credits and spend Gong Credits to fill in any gaps. Partners include ZenLeads, Inc., which does business as Apollo , LeadIQ Inc., Lusha Systems Inc., RocketReach LLC and ZoomInfo Technologies Inc.
Sellers can fill missing contact details with a click, while teams can automate enrichment when specified conditions occur. For example, a bounced email can trigger a search for updated information.
Administrators choose data partners, exclude selected geographies and decide whether incoming information fills empty CRM fields or replaces existing values. Gong also identifies the source for most contact details and allows that information to be passed into the CRM.
Those controls have limits. Reshef said Gong relies on providers’ representations about opt-out and suppression requirements, does not independently verify each contact’s opt-out status and does not guarantee every data point’s accuracy. Customers remain responsible for how they use the information, including outreach.
Prebuilt agents
Another change is the addition of automatic triggers to custom agents. Gong distinguishes Agent Builder, which creates workflows specific to a customer’s business, from Agent Studio, where customers configure Gong’s prebuilt agents.
“The biggest change is that those agents can now be event-driven rather than relying on someone to manually trigger them,” Reshef said.
For example, an agent could respond to a change in status of an enterprise deal by analyzing relevant calls against a company’s risk criteria, summarizing its findings and writing next steps to the CRM. Customers can define triggers, conditions and actions through a visual editor or natural-language instructions, then reuse company-specific expertise across agents.
Deep Mode targets strategic questions requiring broader investigation than Gong Assistant’s existing Quick Mode. For example, a revenue leader might ask what is driving enterprise deal risk during a quarter and what the team should change.
The feature can clarify the question’s scope, plan an investigation and examine deals, conversations, accounts and other signals over time. It might identify recurring security concerns in stalled deals and surface supporting conversations.
“Deep Mode is for bigger strategic questions that require broader analysis, synthesis across multiple signals, and a complete, sourced report,” Reshef said.
The dashboard expansion lets teams define metrics once in Gong Data Studio and reuse them across views. Other Assistant updates embed it in deal and account boards and allow users to create Gong Engage Flows through natural-language requests.
Gong Enrich, Deep Mode and the expanded dashboards are generally available. Automatically triggered custom agents and the other Assistant enhancements will roll out later this year.

articles.title: Samsung Introduces Galaxy Tab S12 Series
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Samsung Introduces Galaxy Tab S12 Series
Samsung Electronics today unveiled the Galaxy Tab S12 series—Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Tab S12+—delivering Samsung's most capable and versatile tablet experience yet. Packing breakthrough performance, long-lasting battery life, and the latest Galaxy AI into Galaxy Tab's signature ultra-thin design, the new lineup turns complex workflows into effortless, everyday achievements whether it's mastering skills, pursuing career goals, or exploring creative passions.
Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Tab S12+ feature immersive displays and come bundled with the ergonomically designed S Pen for effortless note-taking and precise editing. With easy access to professional-grade apps and versatile accessories, users can pursue their passions and progress toward their goals with ease. Combining portability with professional-grade power, the Galaxy Tab S12 series gives users instant access to powerful capabilities whenever inspiration strikes.
Jay Kim, Executive Vice President and Head of Customer Experience Office, Mobile eXperience (MX) Business at Samsung Electronics"The Galaxy Tab S12 series is designed for people who are constantly exploring new ideas, developing new skills, and bringing their ambitions to life. Built with industry-leading hardware, the Galaxy Tab S12 series pairs an expansive screen with the power of Galaxy AI—removing friction from complex tasks so users can stay focused on achieving impactful results."
Peak Performance in an Ultra-Thin Design
The Galaxy Tab S12 series combines powerful performance and long-lasting battery life into a thin and light design, making it easy for users to achieve more, wherever ambition takes them. At a remarkably slim 5.1 mm, Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is Samsung's thinnest Galaxy Tab, while delivering the most powerful performance of any Galaxy Tab to date, supporting productive use throughout the day. For example, users taking an online course alongside a full-time job can catch up on a lesson during the commute, then work through course exercises on the large screen at a café or library later in the day.Both models are built to go the distance, allowing users to keep going without losing momentum. On a single charge, the all-day battery lasts up to 23 hours on Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and up to 21 hours on Galaxy Tab S12+, supporting long stretches of productivity anywhere. When it is time to recharge, the battery goes from 0% to 100% in about 95 minutes with the 45 W adapter—minimizing downtime, so users can get back to what they were doing.
Beyond long-lasting battery life, the Galaxy Tab S12 series delivers the most powerful performance of any Galaxy Tab to date, keeping pace with even intensive tasks. The cutting-edge 3 nm processor delivers up to 61% faster NPU processing, 19% faster CPU performance, and 17% improved GPU power compared to Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra. In everyday use, that means users can take on more demanding tasks with increased speed and responsiveness. Whether rendering complex creative projects or watching a lecture while taking notes and asking AI for clarification—the experience stays responsive and fast with fewer interruptions to break their focus.
A newly designed 3D Vapor Chamber efficiently dissipates heat to support more reliable performance during demanding tasks, whether users are editing video or designing graphics for hours. Engineered for resilience and durability to withstand the elements and give users peace of mind, the Galaxy Tab S12 series also comes with IP68-rated water and dust resistance.
The Galaxy Tab S12 series comes with an expansive screen designed to help users think bigger and give ideas more room to unfold. Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra features a large 14.6-inch display, making it easy to explore complex topics and keep multiple perspectives in view. The Galaxy Tab S12+ features a larger 12.6-inch display and slimmer bezels than its predecessor, offering more screen space without sacrificing portability. Both models feature Dynamic AMOLED 2X displays reaching up to 1,600 nits of peak brightness—delivering clear, vivid visuals indoors, or out. The upgraded seamless Vision Booster now adjusts brightness in real time based on lighting conditions for comfortable viewing.Sound gets a major upgrade as well, with 4-channel spatial audio—twice as many channels as the previous generation—delivering a richer, more immersive experience whether users are streaming content, following a tutorial, or editing.
Making Everyday Tasks More Intuitive and Effortless
Building on an industry-leading hardware foundation, the Galaxy Tab S12 series turns its large screen into a flexible workspace that makes it easy to keep up with different tasks without missing a beat. Running Android 17 with One UI 9 and the latest Galaxy AI, it brings research, note-taking, creation, and AI assistance into one place, giving users more freedom to explore new ideas, capture what matters and put what they learn into practice.
Thanks to the Galaxy Tab S12 series' immersive screen, users can split the screen into up to three sections in Multi Window layout. For example, users can take notes in Samsung Notes on one side while playing a lecture and opening an AI assistant on the other. As key takeaways or questions come up, users can capture them with the S Pen directly in Samsung Notes, while Note Assist summarizes their notes - all without pausing the lecture.Both models come bundled with an ergonomic S Pen, offering precise, intuitive input for note-taking, annotating materials, and sketching concepts. For a more structured, professional workstation, the Pro Keyboard elevates productivity with a premium aluminium finish and a Galaxy AI Key that enables instant access to AI assistants, while the Book Cover Keyboard Slim delivers flexibility with comfortable viewing angles and an effortless typing experience.The Galaxy Tab S12 series helps users bring information together and get real-time support the moment curiosity strikes. The Galaxy Tab S12 series comes equipped with a six-month trial of Google AI Pro, providing expanded access to Google's most capable AI models from day one. Users can ask Gemini about anything unclear or dive deeper into subjects they want to explore the moment a question comes up. With Gemini Notebook, users can bring together notes, images, recordings, and files in one workspace and create summaries, podcasts, and even quizzes to make key information easier to understand.
As exploration expands into deeper research, Samsung Browser helps users stay focused without losing track of what they have already discovered. By understanding webpage content, context across multiple tabs, and browsing history, it can summarize information across open pages or surface a relevant source viewed days earlier - helping users spend less time searching through past tabs and more time capturing the key insights that matter most.A Complete Ecosystem Designed To Take Skills and Creativity Further
The Galaxy Tab S12 series gives users the ideal place to put knowledge into practice, bringing together professional-grade apps alongside benefits worth approximately $600 to help them take their skills further.
Adobe Photoshop16 comes preloaded on the Galaxy Tab S12 series—a first for Android tablets—bringing pro-grade image editing and design to the tablet. The interface is optimized for tablets, and S Pen support makes it more intuitive to move ideas from hand to screen. Photoshop includes AI-powered features including AI Assistant and generative AI features powered by Adobe Firefly like Generative Fill and Image to Video, helping creatives edit faster and effortlessly. Exclusively for the Galaxy Tab S12 series, users receive four months of free access to the Photoshop mobile plan.
Notability, newly preloaded on Galaxy Tab, helps users capture their ideas, organize notes, and build knowledge more efficiently with S Pen optimization and AI-driven study tools with a six-month free trial, plus 20% off the first subscription.
Goodnotes delivers clean note-taking and organization with one year of free access and LumaFusion enables professional-grade video editing, offered at a 66% discount. And Notion supports flexible writing, planning, and organization with one month of its Plus plan free. Clip Studio Paint22 brings precision drawing and painting tools for digital art with a six-month trial and 20% off the first subscription.
In addition to these apps, users can explore a broader range of options that support different needs. MyScript Math instantly solves handwritten equations and shows the steps behind each one, while MyScript Notes summarizes handwritten notes into study materials with built-in AI tools to explain concepts or generate quizzes. Noteshelf offers customizable layouts for capturing and organizing ideas, while ArcSite converts rough field sketches into precise CAD drawings.
Availability
The Galaxy Tab S12 series will be available starting Oct. 7 in select markets and offered in two colors, Gray and Silver.
Built for lasting and confident use, Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Galaxy Tab S12+ support up to seven times of OS upgrades and security updates.
For added peace of mind, Samsung Care+ offers comprehensive coverage tailored to users' device needs, including fast repairs for accidental damage, extended warranty, and certified expert support available both at home and abroad. Additionally, Galaxy mobile phone users running One UI 9 can easily check the Samsung Care+ status of their Galaxy Tab and enroll through the Warranty and care menu in the Settings. It provides quick access to warranty information, self-diagnostics, repair requests, and remote support for connected devices—all directly from the mobile phone.

articles.title: I tried Peloton's redesigned Tread Vision and its AI feedback features, and asked top execs why it's still 'immense value' despite high prices
articles.text:
Could a treadmill make you a better runner than an Apple Watch? Peloton CPO Nick Caldwell and CMO Megan Imbres believe the Peloton Tread Vision's AI cameras offer 'much higher accuracy' than wearables
I tried the new features out for myself
Peloton is name that remains synonymous with stationary exercise equipment, despite the company's ups and downs. It experienced huge highs as Covid forced people to exercise indoors, and became a market leader in the best treadmills and exercise bikes, even if it was never quite able to recapture the zeitgeist position it once held as restrictions lifted and people returned to their gyms.
Six years on, the premium exercise equipment company shows no sign of slowing down: its slickly-produced live and recorded classes feature instructors who are treated like celebrities in their own right, and its algorithmic, addictive content meshes with its high-end machinery to make for a 'magic formula' which keeps Peloton power users addicted to indoor cardio.
Now Peloton has announced a trio of new treadmills that will launch starting October 1: the Peloton Tread Flex, the Tread Vision, and the Tread Vision Plus.
Let's start with the Peloton Tread Flex. Costing $2,195 / £1,999 / AU$3,499, it's Peloton's cheapest treadmill, and its cheapest product so far, although it won't be available in regions outside the US until spring 2027. It's designed for smaller spaces and smaller budgets, and it's also Peloton's first folding treadmill, with four caster wheels to help you tow it around in its upright configuration without needing tools.
"We've put a lot of work into that," Nick Caldwell, Peloton's Chief Product Officer, tells me when I meet him and Chief Marketing Officer Megan Imbres at Peloton HQ in London. "It's 46% of the footprint of our Tread Vision base platform, and also super quiet... You're getting great value with the capability to do folding and flex, and you're going to get a ton of new software features with this as well."
Some of those software features include the great-looking ReRun feature, which extracts and replicates the elevation profile of real-world routes, like parts of the New York City Marathon, and replicates them on the Tread. The Tread will respond by adjusting the gradient automatically to replicate the route, and show you your progress on a virtual map. Not only is this cool in its own right, it also allows runners hoping to tackle popular races around the world an opportunity to dry-run those iconic courses.
"Out of the box, we'll have some built-in ones," says Imbres. "We'll take the New York City Marathon and break it up into five digestible chunks... so you can get dialed-in training for the course." Imbres adds that runners will be able to upload GPX files from their outdoor runs and replicate them on the treadmill, too.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Next up is the Tread Vision, a more powerful non-folding, AI-powered model starting at $3,495 / £2,999 / AU$4,999. It features a new cushioning system underneath the tread for more comfort and energy return, and a redesigned button system with jump-up and jump-down options alongside the old dial system. But the real advancement is the Movement Tracking Camera.
"We've created a new form feedback system for runners", Caldwell tells me. "This is using vertical displacement to a) count your steps, give you a cadence figure, and b) it'll tell you whether or not your form is correct, and whether your running efficiency is being maximized".
Covering stats like vertical oscillation (how much you bounce while you run) as well as cadence, the system will give you a Running Efficiency Score, as well as personalized AI-powered feedback. We've seen similar features in products like the Peloton Guide, and incorporated into earlier Cross Training labelled devices, but here Peloton has applied it to a treadmill.
"We've already seen this improved folks who are trying to do marathon prep, and things like that," adds Caldwell, indicating that it's more accurate than similar running efficiency-based metrics from wearables such as the best Garmin watches.
Finally, we have the Tread+ Vision, priced at $6,695, with pricing for other regions TBC. This treadmill also features Sled Mode, a Hyrox-style workout that has you grip two vertical bars and replicate a sled-pushing exercise against variable levels of resistance.
"There is one other competitor that has this on the market, that treadmill costs $15,000," says Caldwell. "I know this thing isn't cheap, but, like, you know, for around seven grand US, you're getting an immense value in the form of the highest-quality energy return service, and now Sled Mode."
With all these treadmills, you get Peloton IQ features such as the new ReRun functionality and an IQ Pace Target, which uses AI to calculate times for you to aim to achieve for various distance. These features are also coming to historic treadmills too.
"The only thing that is gated is the Run Analysis because it uses that Computer Vision camera," says Imbres. "Our philosophy is if the hardware allows it, to give it to everyone."
You also naturally get access to Peloton's smorgasbord of live and historic classes, depending on your subscription tier. Heart rate zone-specific workouts are a new addition to the roster, allowing people to connect heart rate monitors and wearables from Garmin, Apple, Google and now Whoop, alongside new running, walking and hiking workouts.
Seeing the Vision
Seeing as we were at Peloton HQ, I had the opportunity to have a quick go on the Tread Vision to try some of the new running tools for myself. The cameras were quick to set up, putting in some information such as my height and capturing my body in vertical orientation as a phone camera does.
During a brief 10-minute test run, I can attest to feeling as though there has been some improvement of the energy return of the belt compared to my experience with the previous model. The belt was nice and spacious, and using the jump-up and jump-down buttons as opposed to, or in conjunction with, the dial was helpful when following the class's cadence as dictated by the instructor. No more spinning the dial too far and trying to course-correct during a class.
After that short test, I ended up with a fairly pedestrian Running Efficiency Score of 66, viewable in the Peloton app, with individual scores for specific metrics, and some apparently genuinely helpful advice on working on my vertical oscillation. However, given the brief nature of the trial, I imagine the feature would become more accurate with longer workouts — at least, that's my excuse.
I'm looking forward to trying all three new treadmills over a longer test period — stay tuned.

articles.title: WSL Containers est disponible pour tous et vient marcher sur les plates-bandes de Docker Desktop
articles.text:
Microsoft généralise WSL Containers, son environnement intégré pour construire et exécuter des conteneurs Linux sous Windows. Une évolution qui rapproche encore WSL des usages jusqu’ici couverts par des outils comme Docker Desktop.
Quelques mois après son arrivée en préversion, WSL Containers est désormais disponible pour tout le monde. Microsoft en profite pour étoffer la gestion des conteneurs, assouplir les réglages réseau et de stockage et donner aux applications Windows un accès direct à ces environnements Linux grâce à une nouvelle API. Elles peuvent ainsi s’appuyer sur des conteneurs pour exécuter localement des charges d’IA ou des composants cloud-native.
WSL s’émancipe un peu plus de Docker Desktop
Les conteneurs Linux tournent depuis longtemps sous Windows, mais WSL n’en assumait jusqu’ici qu’une partie. Docker Desktop s’appuie par exemple sur WSL 2 pour disposer du noyau Linux nécessaire à leur exécution, puis fournit son propre moteur et ses outils de gestion. Les développeurs qui préfèrent directement travailler depuis Linux peuvent aussi installer Docker ou Podman dans leur distribution WSL.
Avec WSL Containers, Microsoft intègre désormais une partie de ces fonctions directement à WSL et les rend accessibles depuis Windows au moyen de wslc.exe. La commande permet de construire et lancer des conteneurs, de leur associer des volumes ou de gérer leur réseau sans ouvrir au préalable une distribution Linux ni installer Docker pour les opérations les plus courantes.
Depuis la préversion, l’outil s’est enrichi du redémarrage des conteneurs, de la copie de fichiers, des contrôles d’état, d’un flux d’événements permettant de suivre leur activité et du choix de l’emplacement utilisé pour leur stockage. VS Code peut déjà utiliser WSL Containers pour ses Dev Containers, Aspire le reconnaît comme environnement d’exécution et l’extension Containers de Microsoft permet d’administrer les conteneurs depuis l’éditeur.
Il faudra en revanche encore attendre pour profiter de Compose. Microsoft en a fait la priorité des prochaines versions et veut laisser WSL Containers lire les fichiers compose.yaml existants, sans conversion ni syntaxe propre à WSL. Les projets répartis entre plusieurs conteneurs pourraient alors réutiliser leurs configurations actuelles sans les adapter à WSL.
Une API pour rapprocher les applications Windows de Linux
La ligne de commande n’est pas le seul moyen de gérer WSL Containers. Microsoft fournit également une API grâce à laquelle une application Windows peut créer et piloter elle-même un conteneur Linux.
Un moteur d’IA local peut ainsi tourner sous Linux, avec les bibliothèques et dépendances prévues pour cet environnement, tout en étant sollicité depuis une application Windows. Même chose pour les composants cloud-native déjà conçus pour fonctionner en conteneurs, qui peuvent être exécutés localement sans être réécrits pour Windows.

articles.title: CD Projekt Red recommande de désactiver une option graphique dans The Witcher 3
articles.text:
Depuis ce mardi 29 septembre, il est possible de se replonger dans The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt grâce à une édition Remastered, gratuite pour tous les propriétaires du jeu. Le succès est au rendez-vous (plus de 120 000 joueurs connectés en même temps sur Steam le jour de la sortie, un record pour le jeu), mais cette nouvelle version arrive avec son lot de bugs, dont certains ont déjà été identifiés par CD Projekt Red.
Dans un message publié sur X ce mercredi 30 septembre, le support technique de l’entreprise polonaise partage un conseil pour les joueuses et les joueurs PC : « Nous avons identifié un problème lié à Nvidia HairWorks susceptible d’affecter significativement les performances. Nous vous recommandons de désactiver ce paramètre en attendant qu’il soit corrigé dans une mise à jour. » CD Projekt Red n’a pas précisé quand le correctif sera lancé.
Nvidia HairWorks est (encore) un problème dans The Witcher 3
« HairWorks affecte significativement les performances depuis environ 11 ans », ironise l’internaute Ermin Hamidovic, en réponse au communiqué de CD Projekt Red. Dès la sortie du jeu, en mai 2015, CD Projekt Red prévenait que HairWorks risquait de mal tourner sur les cartes graphiques AMD, faute de pouvoir optimiser le code de Nvidia pour elles, et conseillait déjà de désactiver l’option. Onze ans plus tard, rien n’a changé.
Dans une vidéo YouTube publiée ce mercredi 30 septembre, une chute de 52 % du nombre d’images par seconde est mesurée sur un PC équipé d’une RTX 5070, une carte graphique de milieu de gamme chez Nvidia. Sur Reddit, l’internaute HYKoalaFanBoy n’a pas attendu CD Projekt Red pour partager le même conseil. Ce mardi 29 septembre, il écrivait : « Désactiver HairWorks sur Geralt après la mise à jour m’a donné un énorme gain de FPS, passant d’environ 70 à environ 120. On dirait bien que HairWorks restera à jamais la bête noire de l’optimisation de ce jeu. »
Le cloud ne règle rien : sur GeForce Now, avec l’offre la plus haut de gamme et sa RTX 5080, un joueur de notre entourage a relevé des chutes de 15 à 20 images par seconde avec HairWorks activé.
HairWorks est une technologie développée par Nvidia qui vise à afficher des cheveux, des pelages et des fourrures plus réalistes, avec une simulation physique en temps réel et une modélisation fine de milliers de brins (cheveux ou poils). En temps normal, le rendu est bluffant, mais calculer autant de brins à la fois coûte cher : même un PC puissant peut constater un gros impact sur le framerate. Dans la version Remastered, le résultat n’est même plus bluffant : DSOGaming note que, HairWorks activé avec le ray tracing, les cheveux de Geralt prennent un aspect plastique.

articles.title: Karnataka government first scheme: Up to Rs 25 lakh for startup pilots
articles.text:
Karnataka government first scheme: Up to Rs 25 lakh for startup pilots
Karnataka’s Government First initiative will give 100 startups up to Rs 25 lakh each to pilot and validate solutions with government departments.
Karnataka is giving startups a new route to test, validate and potentially sell their solutions to the government, with its ‘Government First’ initiative offering up to Rs 25 lakh per startup for pilot deployments.
Under the initiative, up to 100 startups will receive support over three years, with a total allocation of Rs 25 crore. Government First has been approved under the ELEVATE programme of the Karnataka Startup Policy 2025–30 and will be implemented by the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS).
Rather than functioning only as a buyer, Karnataka wants government departments to become early customers for new technologies. Startups will get an opportunity to put their products through real-world testing, while departments can evaluate solutions before considering wider adoption.
From government problems to startup pilots
Government departments can identify specific problems and invite startups to develop solutions. Startups can also approach departments proactively with products or ideas that address government requirements.
A third route involves piloting selected solutions in live government environments.
Applications will be processed through quarterly cycles, with proposals received during each cycle evaluated together. Shortlisted solutions will be assessed for factors including innovation, technical feasibility, scalability and relevance to government use cases.
Once a pilot begins, the concerned department will provide access to the required infrastructure and support. It will also monitor implementation, offer domain-specific guidance and assess how the solution performs under real operating conditions.
Evaluation will cover performance, usability, cost-effectiveness, scalability and measurable impact.
Solutions that deliver the expected outcomes can then move towards government procurement and wider adoption. For products that are already deployment-ready, the guidelines also allow consideration for direct procurement.
Eligibility, funding and benefits
Startups registered in Karnataka can apply if they are less than 10 years old and have an annual turnover of no more than Rs 200 crore in any financial year since incorporation.
Their products, processes or services must demonstrate innovation or scalability and meet applicable technical, regulatory and sector-specific requirements.
Solutions must also have a Technology Readiness Level of at least 7, meaning they have been validated in an operational environment and are ready for real-world testing.
The programme covers physical goods, specialised services and end-to-end solutions. Areas listed in the guidelines include IT, AI, data analytics, consulting, design, logistics, hardware and other technology-enabled solutions for government challenges.
Of the Rs 25 crore allocation, Rs 23.75 crore has been earmarked for startup assistance and Rs 1.25 crore for administrative and operational expenses. Each selected startup can receive up to Rs 25 lakh for pilot deployment and validation.
Payment terms are also structured around implementation. Startups will receive 25% when the work order is issued, with the remaining 75% released after the user department provides a completion certificate. Intellectual property will remain with the startup unless another arrangement is mutually agreed upon.
Proposals will be reviewed by committees comprising domain experts and government representatives.
Their assessment will cover technical feasibility, innovation, product readiness, scalability, integration capability and socioeconomic impact.
A successful solution can also move beyond its first deployment. Where relevant, products can be adopted by multiple departments, while larger government challenges can be addressed by combining solutions from different startups.
Karnataka also plans to publish key programme information through a public dashboard, including work orders, implementation details and case studies. An annual report will track startups engaged, work-order values and programme outcomes.
For startups, Government First creates a path that goes beyond grant funding: government problem, startup solution, live pilot, validation, procurement, wider adoption. It gives young companies a chance to establish their technology in a real public-sector setting while giving departments a structured way to assess new solutions before scaling them.

articles.title: Spider-Man : après Spider-Noir, Amazon prépare une série sur les clones de Peter Parker
articles.text:
Spider-Man : après Spider-Noir, Amazon prépare une série sur les clones de Peter Parker
Amazon serait sur le point de commander pour Prime Video une série tirée de la Saga du Clones de Marvel Comics, mettant en scène deux clones de Spider-Man.
L'univers de l'homme-araignée est plus vivant que jamais ! Alors que Spider-Man : Brand New Day a battu tous les records au box-office mondial, et que Spider-Noir a prouvé qu'il était possible de porter le super-héros avec brio sur petit écran, une autre série Spider-Man pour la plateforme de streaming Prime Video serait en passe de recevoir le feu vert, comme l'a dévoilé le site Deadline.
Spidey et ses doubles
Basée sur la Saga du Clone, une série de comics publiée d'abord dans les années 70 avant de connaître un second arc plus mémorable entre 1994 et 1996, cette future série racontera les aventures de deux clones de l'homme-araignée : Ben Reilly et Kaine Parker.
L'histoire est celle du professeur Miles Warren, alias Le Chacal, qui crée un clone de Peter Parker. Celui-ci prend par la suite le nom de Ben Reilly est sa propre identité super-héroïque : Scarlet Spider. Kaine est lui un autre clone imparfait et souffrant de graves problèmes physiques.
Si les détails sur ce projet sont encore peu nombreux, les bruits de couleurs indiquent que la série suivra Ben et Kaine alors qu'ils essaient de comprendre leur nature tout en affrontant d'autres clones maléfiques. Des rumeurs disent même que les personnages pourraient tout à fait voir leurs origines modifiées.
Nous savons toutefois que cette nouvelle série est écrite par Kelvin Yu, créateur du show American de Chine sorti en 2023 sur Disney+. Si l'information est confirmée dans les prochaines semaines, et que le projet reçoit bien le feu vert de la part d'Amazon, la série prendra le relais de Spider-Noir, annulée après une saison.
Pour rappel, Sony et Amazon ont signé un accord pour développer l'univers de Spider-Man à la télévision. Outre Spider-Noir, un projet de show sur la super-héroine Silk a été longtemps dans les tuyaux avant d'etre annulée.
Cette potentielle série sur la Saga du Clone fait donc partie de ce deal, et devrait être produite par les habitués Amy Pascal, Phil Lord et Christopher Miller pour le service de streaming Prime Video. Les Numériques vous tiendra informé dès qu'il y a une officialisation.

articles.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger tenía una finca valorada en más de medio millón. Terminó formando parte de una ruta natural
articles.text:
Cuando pienso en Arnold Schwarzenegger mi mente lo imagina como el T-800 de Terminator. A mí me cuesta sacar al actor fuera de los entornos peliculeros, pero su vida va mucho más allá de personajes apocalípticos. En el mundo real, y aparte de gobernar California, Schwarzenegger hizo una contribución importante para salvar un entorno natural de ese preciso estado.
La propiedad. Corría 2016, y Schwarzenegger se juntó con Betty Weider, culturista y empresaria, para donar cerca de 16 hectáreas de una finca ubicada en Zuma Canyon, California. Esa parcela terminó integrándose en el Backbone Trail, una extensa ruta de senderismo que serpentea por los patrajes naturales de las montañas de Santa Mónica. No fue una donación cualquiera: la finca se había tasado en más de 500.000 dólares, unos 440.000 euros sin contar la inflación.
Con el terreno donado, la ruta pudo cruzar por Zuma Canyon y abrir así el entorno natural a cualquiera que se calce unas botas de senderismo (o una bicicleta, que buena parte de la senda es apta para BTT). Como destaca el Servicio de Parques Nacionales (NPS), el diseño final del Backbone Trail es el resultado de más de cuatro décadas de colaboración entre organismos públicos, privados, activistas y mecenas. Como nuestro Schwarzy.
Pumas, reptiles y un santuario biológico. Los Ángeles es una ciudad gigantesca, de esas donde el único bosque está hecho de hormigón. Cuesta imaginar que esté pegada a un paraje natural donde habitan todo tipo de especies animales y vegetales, pero así es. Por Santa Mónica puedes pasear y encontrarte un puma, poca broma.
Los animales amenazados necesitan amplio espacio libre y que este no se vea interrumpido por autopistas, edificios y otras construcciones. La creación de un sendero como el Backbone Trail no solo aportó una vía para pasear y disfrutar de la naturaleza, también otorgó refugio a todo tipo de especies autóctonas. Como los propios pumas, coyotes, ciervos, multitud de aves y reptiles.
Más de 40 años para acabar el proyecto. La historia del Backbone Trail comenzó mucho antes de que se implicaran Arnold Schwarzenegger y Betty Weider. Según detalló el NPS en 2016, hacer realidad la ruta necesitó más de 40 años de gestiones. En los años sesenta, las montañas de Santa Mónica estaban salpicadas de ranchos privados, campos de golf y urbanizaciones. Hubo que negociar los terrenos finca a finca.
En conjunto, se adquirieron más de 180 parcelas con un coste que terminó superando los 100 millones de dólares (unos 88 millones de euros al cambio actual, sin contar la inflación). Dicho coste se sufragó mediante fondos locales y programas federales, además de con donaciones como las de Schwarzenegger y Weider. Hoy en día es una ruta con una longitud de 67 millas (casi 108 kilómetros). El tramo del Backbone Trail junto a Zuma Canyon recibe más de 10.000 visitantes al año.
Un activista medioambiental. Durante su mandato como gobernador de California entre 2003 y 2011, Schwarzenegger hizo del medioambiente uno de los ejes de su agenda. En 2006 promulgó la Global Warming Solutions Act, una normativa que fijó metas estrictas para la emisión de gases de efecto invernadero. Esto sentó las bases legislativas de California en materia de cambio climático.
Tras abandonar la política, el actor continuó vinculado a las causas medioambientales: cofundó la organización R20 (Regions of Climate Action) para orientar a los gobiernos hacia planes sostenibles y promovió la creación del USC Schwarzenegger Institute en 2012. Permanecerá para siempre en mi memoria como Terminator, pero en su trayectoria confluyen el cine, la política y la filantropía. Su donación de suelo en 2016 es una de las huellas más tangibles.

articles.title: Android dit non à l'Union européenne : Google refuse d'ouvrir l'OS à ChatGPT et Claude
articles.text:
Depuis le 16 juillet, deux décisions de la Commission européenne imposent à Google d’ouvrir Android aux assistants IA concurrents et de partager ses données de recherche, au titre du DMA, le règlement européen sur les marchés numériques. Ce mardi 29 septembre, l’entreprise a annoncé contester les deux textes devant le Tribunal de l’Union européenne, à Luxembourg. Le recours décidera de votre liberté de remplacer Gemini par l’assistant de votre choix.
ChatGPT au bouton, Claude à la voix : l’Android que Bruxelles exige
La décision Android, adoptée après six mois d’instruction, contraint Google à ouvrir onze fonctions du système aux assistants concurrents. Un appui long sur le bouton d’accueil pourra réveiller un autre service que Gemini, et chaque éditeur pourra définir son propre mot d’activation, l’équivalent du « Hey Google » maison. Les assistants tiers obtiendront aussi l’accès au contexte de vos applications, à l’automatisation d’actions à l’écran, aux modèles embarqués comme Gemini Nano et à l’exécution en arrière-plan. L’essentiel doit arriver avec Android 18, au plus tard le 1er août 2027 ; l’écoute simultanée de plusieurs mots d’activation attendra Android 19, à l’été 2028. Les accès les plus sensibles passeront par un programme de certification, dont les conditions définitives sont attendues pour le 1er mai 2027.
Google refuse d’ouvrir ces portes et met la sécurité en avant. Confier à des applications tierces un micro toujours actif, la lecture de l’écran et des automatisations système reviendrait, d’après ses équipes, à « saper le modèle de sécurité fondamental d’Android ». La firme brandit aussi le risque d’injection de commandes : des instructions cachées dans une page ou un document, qui détournent un agent IA sans que son propriétaire ne s’aperçoive de rien.
Vos recherches, l’autre trésor que Google ne veut pas céder
La seconde décision touche à plus intime encore : vos requêtes. À partir de janvier 2027, Google devra fournir aux moteurs concurrents, chatbots IA compris, ses données de recherche anonymisées (requêtes, clics, classements), à prix encadré, dès lors que le demandeur dépasse 50 000 utilisateurs européens par mois. L’entreprise plaide que ces données racontent nos vies, « des préoccupations de santé à l’intimité », et qu’un partage mal protégé causerait un « préjudice irréparable » à la vie privée des utilisateurs.
Bruxelles oppose ses garde-fous : anonymisation des données, consentement explicite de l’utilisateur pour les accès sensibles, conservation limitée à treize mois et audits indépendants imposés aux bénéficiaires. Le 23 juillet, la Commission a déjà infligé 890 millions d’euros d’amende à Google pour deux manquements distincts au même règlement. Ignorer les décisions de juillet exposerait cette fois l’entreprise à des sanctions pouvant atteindre 10 % de son chiffre d’affaires mondial.
En attendant les juges, rien ne bouge sur votre écran : Gemini reste seul à décrocher quand vous pressez le bouton, et le calendrier fixé par Bruxelles n’a pas varié à ce stade. Si la Commission tient bon, votre Android devra faire de la place aux assistants rivaux d’ici à l’été 2027. Si Google l’emporte, l’assistant de votre fidèle téléphone restera ce qu’il est aujourd’hui : préinstallé, exclusif et non négociable.

articles.title: Jeeves raises $110M to scale stablecoin-native banking platform for global payments - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Jeeves raises $110M to scale stablecoin-native banking platform for global payments
Jeeves Inc., a stablecoin-focused banking platform for global enterprises, announced Tuesday it has raised $110 million in equity funding to launch a cryptocurrency wallet with payouts across 190 countries.
The crypto-focused venture capital and investment firm CoinFund led the round. Additional participants included AllianceBernstein, Andreessen Horowitz, Coinbase Ventures, CRV, GIC, Global PayTech Ventures, ParaFi, Vista, Wintermute, Y Combinator, and others.
Jeeves touts itself as a stablecoin-native banking platform, meaning it uses cryptocurrency tokens pegged to a local currency, such as United States dollars, to avoid the volatility common to other cryptocurrency tokens while keeping the benefits of rapid transactions. The company says its platform lets global enterprises save time and money by using its service to power corporate cards, accounts payable and treasury payments, spend management and agentic workflows.
“We built Jeeves as a banking platform on stablecoin rails because that’s the only way to give companies the same speed and cost structure moving money between São Paulo and Berlin that they get transacting within one country,” said founder and Chief Executive Dileep Thazhmon. “That is what a stablecoin-native banking platform for global business actually looks like.”
Current Jeeves customers include industry leaders such as BMW, H & M Hennes & Mauritz AB, Lululemon Athletica Inc. and Burger King Corp.
This funding round comes as Jeeves has surpassed $5 billion in annualized total platform volume across its card and payment products. The stablecoin market is one of the fastest-growing parts of that volume, the company said. Eight months ago, stablecoin-settled activity on the platform was effectively zero, and now it represents $1.5 billion in annualized revenue.
Jeeves began in 2019 as a traditional financial technology company, solving multi-country expense tracking and corporate card needs using traditional banking infrastructure. In late 2025, the company officially began pivoting to stablecoin-backed solutions to bypass slow, expensive traditional cross-border correspondent banking networks.
The stablecoin market is worth around $290 to $300 billion today, with Tether Holdings Ltd. and Circle Internet Group Inc. issuing most of the tokens. Valuations differ depending on what counts as a stablecoin, with Forbes putting the market cap near $292 billion and a recent TokenPost report putting it near $306 billion. A supermajority, around 98%, of all stablecoins are pegged to USD.
The company is currently expanding its stablecoin card offering from 25 to 35 countries, including Argentina, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Guatemala, Panama, Peru, Paraguay and Uruguay. The expansion will cover nearly every market in Central and South America. Combined with its current coverage across North America, the United Kingdom and Europe, Jeeves will gain broader global reach.
Alongside this, the company is launching a proprietary stablecoin wallet with instant payouts in 190 countries, a global artificial intelligence spend-tracking solution and an accounts receivable module.

articles.title: Apple lanzaría más dispositivos durante el año y este sería el plan de John Ternus para lograrlo
articles.text:
John Ternus, el nuevo director ejecutivo de Apple, prepara una reorganización que busca terminar con la dependencia de la compañía a sus tradicionales eventos de primavera y otoño. Según un reporte de Bloomberg, el sucesor de Tim Cook quiere que la empresa lance dispositivos con mayor frecuencia a lo largo del año, en lugar de concentrar casi todas las novedades en septiembre.
El cambio de estrategia responde a la necesidad de competir en la era de la inteligencia artificial, un terreno en el que Apple llegó tarde.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo sería el nuevo calendario de lanzamientos de Apple
El plan contempla romper con la coreografía que Apple siguió durante años: septiembre para el iPhone y el Apple Watch, la primavera para renovaciones de iPad y Mac, y octubre para completar la temporada con nuevas computadoras.
La idea de Ternus es que, si un producto está terminado, la compañía lo presente sin esperar a la siguiente ventana comercial. Eso permitiría distribuir la atención mediática durante todo el año y evitar que demasiadas novedades compitan entre sí en pocas semanas.
Los primeros indicios de este cambio llegarían a comienzos de 2027, cuando se esperan los anuncios de los iPhone 18, 18e y el modelo Air 2. En septiembre, Apple ya había presentado únicamente los modelos Pro y Pro Max de la serie 18, junto al iPhone Duo, el primer teléfono plegable de la marca. Ese desdoblamiento funciona como indicio de la estrategia que impulsa el nuevo CEO.
PUBLICIDAD
El plegable llegó además en el primer evento encabezado por Ternus, de cara al vigésimo aniversario del iPhone que se cumplirá el año próximo. Para esa fecha, la compañía también planea lanzar sus primeras gafas inteligentes y unos AirPods con cámara, con lanzamientos escalonados durante el año que impulsarían los ingresos de sus divisiones de hardware y servicios.
Cómo sería el esquema de trabajo para lograr este ritmo de lanzamiento
Para lograr esa velocidad, Ternus no solo busca mover fechas de presentación. También pretende reducir los puestos de mando intermedio y acercar a los ingenieros directamente a los altos ejecutivos, con menos capas de gestión y decisiones más rápidas.
En su primer memo interno como máximo responsable de Apple, recogido por MacRumors, Ternus prometió a los empleados una semana “fenomenal” de lanzamientos. El mensaje llegó el 1 de septiembre de 2026, día en el que asumió oficialmente el mando tras Tim Cook.
PUBLICIDAD
En una presentación interna, el CEO defendió la idea de que Apple debe conseguir más resultados con menos empleados, según una diapositiva sobre el crecimiento de la plantilla mostrada a sus equipos. Esa filosofía ya se tradujo en recortes: directores y gestores de programas de ingeniería recibieron varias semanas para encontrar otra posición dentro de la compañía o abandonarla.
Los ajustes alcanzaron también áreas como Siri, Vision Pro, el software de inteligencia artificial y Fitness+, divisiones que ya habían sufrido bajas desde que comenzó la reestructuración a inicios de 2025.
Cómo afectaría este plan a los gastos y la calidad de Apple
La aceleración de los lanzamientos tiene una segunda lectura vinculada al dinero. Con el crecimiento del negocio de servicios en desaceleración, la dirección pidió reducir el gasto en marketing y limitar los incrementos presupuestarios previstos para 2027.
PUBLICIDAD
La consecuencia es una compañía que intenta aumentar el ritmo de entrega de productos mientras mantiene presupuestos más contenidos y reorganiza su estructura interna, algo que contrasta con la lógica habitual de invertir más recursos para producir más.
Empleados consultados advirtieron que modificar prácticas de desarrollo tan arraigadas podría tomar años, según Bloomberg. Reducir la burocracia puede permitir que los equipos de ingeniería trabajen con mayor agilidad, pero aumentar el número de lanzamientos mientras se limitan las contrataciones también abre una duda sobre hasta dónde puede acelerar Apple sin afectar la calidad de sus productos.
Esa tensión entre velocidad y nivel de acabado, uno de los rasgos que históricamente distinguió a los productos de la compañía, quedará expuesta con mayor claridad cuando avance el cronograma de lanzamientos previsto para 2027.

articles.title: Promoção relâmpago: Galaxy Buds 3 FE com ANC despenca 56% com cupom • Tecnoblog

Promoção relâmpago: Galaxy Buds 3 FE com ANC despenca 56% com cupom
Galaxy Buds 3 FE têm bateria de longa duração e suportam a suíte Galaxy AI; fones de ouvido da Samsung saem 56% mais baratos no Pix com cupom no Mercado Livre
Os Galaxy Buds 3 FE estão saindo por R$ 485 no Pix com cupom SITE60 no Mercado Livre. Os fones de ouvido wireless da Samsung, que trazem ANC, bateria de longa duração e funções do Galaxy AI, atingem o menor preço já visto pelo Achados, com desconto de 56% sobre o original de R$ 1.099.
Mas seja rápido: o cupom está em modo de “contagem regressiva” e deve esgotar em breve.
Os Galaxy Buds 3 FE contam com o recurso de cancelamento ativo de ruído (ANC), que filtra sons externos e melhora a experiência ao ouvir música em qualquer lugar (sons importantes, como de trânsito, ainda passam por motivos de segurança). O Modo Ambiente capta conversas sem precisar remover os fones.
Os recursos de Inteligência Artificial da suíte Galaxy AI incluem o Modo Intérprete, que traduz conversas em tempo real; o usuário escuta a voz da outra pessoa em seu idioma, e o celular Galaxy pareado (recurso exclusivo) exibe as respostas traduzidas, sendo uma ótima função em viagens ao exterior.
O suporte ao Google Gemini habilita um dos melhores fones da Samsung a realizar consultas aos fones diretamente ou a outro dispositivo Galaxy pareado, incluindo smartwatches. É possível criar lembretes, iniciar atividades físicas ou receber respostas sobre diversas dúvidas.
Outros recursos dos Galaxy Buds 3 FE incluem o áudio 360, que oferece maior imersão, e um equalizador de áudio personalizável. O design ergonômico com hastes longas facilita os controles por gestos, ao oferecer uma maior área de contato.
As baterias dos fones, quando combinadas à do case de transporte, resistem a até 30 horas com o ANC desligado, e cerca de 6 horas com o recurso ligado, segundo a fabricante. Assim, você pode ouvir suas músicas e podcasts sem se preocupar com tomadas e powerbanks.
Os Galaxy Buds 3 FE (R$ 485 no Pix com cupom SITE60) possuem certificação IP54, que confere proteção moderada contra água, suor e poeira. Não perca essa oferta relâmpago e leve os fones da Samsung para casa no precinho.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon AI model, but you can't use it yet
articles.text:
Google promised Gemini 3.5 Pro in June, but it spent the summer trotting out smaller Flash models. Now, Google is ready to take on the frontier again with Gemini 4 Argon. The company claims this new AI offers industry-leading performance in coding, knowledge work, and cybersecurity, but you aren’t allowed to use it yet.
While most of us will have to wait to test Gemini 4, Google says engineers inside the company are already using the new model extensively. Argon reportedly used “fleet-wide telemetry data” to help Google save 300 TiB of memory across its data centers. Meanwhile, Argon agents have been working to migrate C/C++ codebases to Rust across Google, including thousands of lines in the core re2 and libgav1 libraries and more than 800,000 lines in the Fuchsia OS Zircon kernel.
Google has also come armed with a raft of benchmarks to back up its claims. On the software engineering DeepSWE v1.1 benchmark, Gemini 4 Argon hits 77.9 percent, which is higher than GPT-6 Astra, Fable 5.1, and Opus 5.5. Google promises similar power across a range of long-horizon tasks, pointing to Argon’s industry-leading score in the economic analysis Vals Index test.
This model is still in limited testing, but Google has announced API pricing. For a limited time, Argon will offer rates of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, and cached input tokens will be discounted 95 percent. The company has also confirmed that Gemini 4 Argon will support a much higher output limit of 1 million tokens. That’s up from 64,000 tokens in previous Gemini models. Google says this allows users to complete more daunting tasks in a single step.

articles.title: QNAP Launches QSW-M5218 Series L3 Lite Managed 25 GbE Switches
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
QNAP Launches QSW-M5218 Series L3 Lite Managed 25 GbE Switches
QNAP Systems, Inc., a leading computing, networking, and storage solution innovator, today announced the new QSW-M5218 Series L3 Lite managed switches, including the QSW-M5218-6F12T and the PoE-capable QSW-M5218P-6F12T. Aimed at SMBs and applications that demand high-speed network infrastructure—such as AV over IP transmission—the series features twelve 10GbE RJ45 ports and six 25GbE SFP28 uplink ports, with a switching capacity of up to 540 Gbps. By combining L3 Lite routing, MC-LAG high availability, and IEEE 1588v2 PTP precise time synchronization, it helps enterprises overcome core network bandwidth bottlenecks and build a stable, high-performance IT infrastructure with a seamless upgrade path.
As NAS devices, servers, and workstations move to 10GbE, traditional 1G/2.5G ports and a single 10G uplink are increasingly becoming performance bottlenecks. The QSW-M5218 Series uses high-density 10GbE interfaces to connect high-speed NAS, virtualization servers, and multimedia workstations, while its 25GbE SFP28 ports act as a high-bandwidth backbone that aggregates traffic into the enterprise core—delivering up to 2.5 times the per-port uplink bandwidth of 10G. At the endpoints, existing Cat 6a copper cabling can be reused without the need to lay new fiber, streamlining core network upgrades.High-speed connectivity alone is not enough. Enterprises that need both 25GbE high-speed uplinks and inter-subnet routing have traditionally had to deploy complex, costly L3 core switches. The QSW-M5218 Series is the ideal solution, designed around a core philosophy: the simplicity and low barrier to entry of near-L2 deployment, combined with the L3 routing capabilities every enterprise needs. Compared with L2 managed switches that offer only VLAN/QoS, the QSW-M5218 Series has built-in L3 Lite, handling IPv4 / IPv6 static routing, a DHCP server, and inter-VLAN routing locally to offload the core router and cut latency. And compared with L3 Full models that add OSPF/BGP dynamic routing, it significantly reduces costs, making it a perfect fit for the real-world needs of SMBs and multi-segment environments.
Ruby Chan, Product Manager at QNAP"As 10GbE moves out of the core server room and onto the work floor, the real bottleneck shifts from the endpoints to the uplinks and power. The QSW-M5218 Series brings 25GbE uplinks, L3 Lite routing, MC-LAG redundancy, and PoE power delivery together in a single switch, letting enterprises build a stable, scalable, and easy-to-manage high-speed backbone with a leaner investment."
Key Features

				QNAP QSW-M5218-6F12T, 				QSW-M5218P-6F12T

Enterprises that need both 25GbE high-speed uplinks and inter-subnet routing have traditionally had to deploy complex, costly L3 core switches. The QSW-M5218 Series is the ideal solution, designed around a core philosophy: the simplicity and low barrier to entry of near-L2 deployment, combined with the L3 routing capabilities every enterprise needs. Compared with L2 managed switches that offer only VLAN/QoS, the QSW-M5218 Series has built-in L3 Lite, handling IPv4 / IPv6 static routing, a DHCP server, and inter-VLAN routing locally to offload the core router and cut latency. And compared with L3 Full models that add OSPF/BGP dynamic routing, it significantly reduces costs, making it a perfect fit for the real-world needs of SMBs and multi-segment environments.
Ruby Chan, Product Manager at QNAP"As 10GbE moves out of the core server room and onto the work floor, the real bottleneck shifts from the endpoints to the uplinks and power. The QSW-M5218 Series brings 25GbE uplinks, L3 Lite routing, MC-LAG redundancy, and PoE power delivery together in a single switch, letting enterprises build a stable, scalable, and easy-to-manage high-speed backbone with a leaner investment."
- L3 Lite Advanced Routing to Ease the Core Load: Built-in IPv4 / IPv6 dual stack, DNS, static routing, DHCP server, SNTP, and inter-VLAN routing let the switch map inter-segment traffic paths locally, improving internal network efficiency and reducing the load on the core router.
- MC-LAG High Availability and LACP: Multi-Chassis Link Aggregation (MC-LAG) consolidates the links between multiple switches into a single logical connection, so the network keeps running even if some physical links fail. Paired with QNAP NAS High Availability (HA), it provides dual-layer protection across the storage and network layers, while Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) support increases throughput and connection reliability.
- Hardware-Level PTP and IGMP Snooping for Professional AV Synchronization: Support for IEEE 1588v2 PTP and Transparent Clock provides sub-microsecond time synchronization at the hardware level and compensates for switching latency. Together with IGMP Snooping, which precisely manages multiple multicast streams and prevents surplus traffic from saturating bandwidth, media servers, NAS, and video walls stay in frame-accurate synchronization in AVoIP environments.
- PoE Model for Leaner Cabling (QSW-M5218P-6F12T): The PoE version supplies up to 90 W per port and a total power budget of 470 W, fully powering as many as 12 PoE+ (30 W) wireless access points or IP surveillance cameras, and can also drive high-power devices such as Wi-Fi 7 access points and PTZ cameras—with no need for extra power cabling or separate power injectors. VLAN isolation and 25GbE uplinks keep the backbone free of congestion when high-speed wireless traffic converges.
- Built-in Cybersecurity Ecosystem: Integrates with ADRA NDR X Network Detection and Response on QNAP NAS to proactively detect and isolate ransomware and abnormal traffic, and supports the QNAP Airgap+ isolated backup solution to reduce the risk of the backup environment being compromised in a network attack.
- QSS Pro Intelligent Management and AMIZcloud Centralized Cloud Control: Featuring an intuitive web GUI, QSS Pro (QNAP Switch System Pro) simplifies L2/L3 Lite management and online firmware updates. Through the AMIZcloud cloud platform, it can monitor switches across multiple sites with no additional hardware or software, enabling remote IT troubleshooting while lowering operating costs.
- QSW-M5218-6F12T: 12x 10GbE RJ45 ports, 6x 25GbE SFP28 uplink ports, and a switching capacity of up to 540 Gbps, with L3 Lite managed features.
- QSW-M5218P-6F12T: 12x 10GbE RJ45 PoE ports, 6x 25GbE SFP28 uplink ports, and a switching capacity of up to 540 Gbps, with PoE++ (IEEE 802.3bt) power delivery of up to 90 W per port and a total power budget of 470 W, plus L3 Lite managed features.

articles.title: 'A good option for future-proofing' - why this mesh Wi-Fi system from Devolo is a great value upgrade
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Devolo’s app could be more straightforward for first-time users, but the BE6500 mesh system remains good value for money. Its 6.0GHz option provides strong performance for newer computers and mobile devices, whilst also offering a 5.0GHz option for older devices.
Reasons to buy
- +Competitive price
- +Two options for dual-band Wi-Fi
- +Fast, reliable Wi-Fi for larger homes
Reasons to avoid
- -Ease of use could be improved
- -Many features require the use of a web browser
- -No tri-band support
Why you can trust TechRadar
Devolo WiFi 7 Mesh BE6500: one-minute review
Devolo is best known for its range of PowerLine adaptors and range extenders but, as the name suggests, its new WiFi 7 Mesh BE6500 steps up to provide a full mesh Wi-Fi system for homes that need to extend their Wi-Fi coverage beyond the range of a single conventional router.
Wi-Fi 7 has been around for a few years now, but high-end tri-band routers that support the 2.4GHz, 5.0GHz and 6.0GHz frequency bands are still quite expensive.
So, like a number of Wi-Fi 7 routers and mesh systems that we’ve seen recently, the BE6500 keeps its price down by offering just dual-band Wi-Fi instead. However, it takes a slightly different approach from many of its dual-band rivals by giving you a choice about which frequency bands you can use.
You can opt to use the 2.4GHz and 5.0GHz bands together to ensure compatibility with older devices that only support Wi-Fi 5 or 6. Alternatively, you can switch to using 2.4GHz and the faster 6.0GHz band for newer computers and mobile devices that support Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7.
That’s a good option for future-proofing your home network, as it will let you use the BE6500 with older computers and mobile devices while still providing an upgrade path for newer devices you may buy in the future.
Devolo Wi-Fi 7 Mesh BE6500: Price & release date
- Released in May 2026
- Available in EU and UK
- Three-pack costs £369.99/€399.90
Devolo products are widely available within the UK and Europe, but the company doesn’t currently operate in the US.
The Wi-Fi 7 Mesh BE6500 is available as a two-pack containing two BE6500 routers for £249.99/€269.90. Devolo doesn’t quote the precise area covered by that two-pack option, merely saying that it is suitable for ‘small-to-medium’ homes.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
However, I tested the three-pack option for ‘larger’ homes, which costs £369.99/€399.90. If required, you can further extend your mesh network by buying additional BE6500 routers, costing £129.99/€149.90 each. Those prices are very competitive when compared to rivals in a similar price range, such as Amazon’s Eero 7 and the Netgear Orbi 373, which only support dual-band Wi-Fi 7 on the 2.4GHz and 5.0GHz bands.
- Value score: 4/5
Devolo Wi-Fi 7 Mesh BE6500: Specs
| Wi-Fi Support  | Wi-Fi 7 (2.4GHz, 5.0GHz, 6.0GHz)  | 
| Wi-Fi Speed  | Upto 6.5Gbps (using 6.0GHz)  | 
| Ports  | 1x 2.5Gbit WAN/LAN, 3x 1Gbit LAN  | 
| Processor  | Qualcomm quad-core @ 1.5GHz  | 
| Dimensions  | 175 x 118 x 72mm  | 
Devolo Wi-Fi 7 Mesh BE6500: Design
- Compact design
- Four Ethernet ports per router
- Setup is a bit fussy
The BE6500 routers are neatly designed, with each plain white unit standing 175mm high, 118mm wide and 72mm deep, so they will fit comfortably onto any convenient table or shelf.
The routers look identical, with four Ethernet ports located on the side, including a 2.5Gbps port for high-speed broadband connections and three 1Gb ports to provide a local (LAN) connection for devices, such as a games console or PC, that may work better with a lag-free wired connection.
However, one of the routers is labelled as the ‘Controller’, and this router will need to be connected to your existing broadband router or modem in order to use its internet connection.
Setting up the Controller router is fairly straightforward, as Devolo’s Home Network app for iOS/Android allows you to simply scan a QR code to connect to the Controller. However, adding the other two routers – referred to as ‘Extensions’ – requires a little more effort.
The app tells you to plug both of the Extension routers into a mains power supply close to the Controller, but it can only connect one Extension to your network at a time. This means that you have to go through the process of connecting the first Extension to your network, and then unplug it so that you can move it to another location, and then repeat the same process for the second Extension.
We’ve seen other mesh Wi-Fi systems that can automatically connect multiple routers in order to create your new network for you, so Devolo could do more to simplify the initial set-up process.
- Design score: 4/5
Devolo Wi-Fi 7 Mesh BE6500: Features
- App is a bit confusing
- Some features are enabled via a browser
The setup process was also unclear how to choose the frequency bands that are used for your new network.
The app doesn’t ask which frequencies you would like to use, but after randomly tapping buttons within the app for a while I did find a mention of the fact that the network was using the 2.4GHz and 5.0GHz bands.
However, there was no option within the app to switch to the 6.0GHz band instead, so I had to connect a laptop to the Devolo network using the default 2.4GHz and 5.0GHz bands, and then use a web browser to view more detailed network settings.
And, again, after some more random button tapping, I did find an option that allowed me to switch to using the 2.4GHz and 6.0GHz bands instead. The browser interface also includes other features, such as a QoS option – Quality Of Service – that allows you to prioritise tasks such as gaming or streaming video.
That’s not a very user-friendly approach though, and may well be confusing for people who aren’t used to configuring their network via a web browser interface, so Devolo needs to make its app more straightforward for new users.
- Features score: 4/5
Devolo Wi-Fi 7 Mesh BE6500: Performance
Ookla Speed Test – 2.4GHz+5.0GHz (download/upload)
Within 5ft, no obstructions: 150Mbps/150Mbps
Within 30ft, three partition walls: 150Mbps/150Mbps
Ookla Speed Test – 2.4GHz+6.0GHz (download/upload)
Within 5ft, no obstructions: 150Mbps/150Mbps
Within 30ft, three partition walls: 150Mbps/150Mbps
20GB Steam Download - 2.4GHz+5.0GHz
Within 5ft, no obstructions: 150Mbps
Within 30ft, three partition walls: 150Mbps
20GB Steam Download - 2.4GHz+6.0GHz
Within 5ft, no obstructions: 150Mbps
Within 30ft, three partition walls: 150Mbps
The BE6500 could certainly be more user-friendly, but I can’t fault its performance, and the three-pack system that I tested worked a treat for tackling the Wi-Fi deadspot that I have in an office towards the back of my building.
Devices in the same room as my normal broadband router can generally achieve the full 150Mbps available with my office broadband service both for Steam downloads and the Ookla Speed Test.
My aging router struggles to reach that back office though, so I have to rely on PowerLine adaptors to provide a more reliable wired network connection.
I placed one of the BE6500 Extension routers in that office, with the second placed roughly halfway between the back office and the main Controller router. Steam downloads did slow down a little initially, when using the 2.4GHz and 5.0GHz bands, dipping to 130Mbps as I walked along the corridor with my laptop, but quickly recovered to hit 150Mbps once more.
That pattern was repeated with the Ookla Speed Test as well. Performance was even better when I switched to using the 2.4GHz and 6.0GHz bands, with the BE6500 trio maintaining a smooth 150Mbps throughout my tests.
Some people might prefer a true tri-band router or mesh system that allows you to use the 2.4GHz, 5.0GHz and 6.0GHz bands simultaneously. That will be more expensive though, and if you need an affordable Wi-Fi upgrade that can cover a larger home with reliable Wi-Fi, then the BE6500 is good value for money.
- Performance score: 4/5
Should I buy the Devolo Wi-Fi 7 Mesh BE6500?
| Devolo Wi-Fi 7 Mesh BE6500 scorecard |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attribute  | Notes  | Score  | 
|---|---|---|
| Features  | Dual-band Wi-Fi 7, with support for 2.4GHz + 5.0GHz, or 2.4GHz + 6.0GHz | 4/5  | 
| Performance  | A mid-range option, but fast enough for most domestic broadband services | 4/5 | 
| Design  | Compact and neatly designed, with four Ethernet ports | 4/5  | 
| Value  | A reliable performer at a competitive price | 4/5  | 
Buy it if…
You need a long-range network
A conventional router is probably fine for smaller homes with one or two bedrooms, but larger homes may benefit from a mesh Wi-Fi system that uses two or three routers to cover a wider area.
You want an upgrade path
You have two options with the BE6500, with its 5.0GHz network providing compatibility for older devices, or you can step up to a 6.0GHz network for newer computers and mobile devices.
You don't need top speed
Tri-band routers and mesh systems can be very expensive, but the versatile dual-band options available with the BE6500 provide good performance while still keeping the price down. 
Don’t buy it if…
You're on a budget
The BE6500 is competitively priced, but many homes will still get good performance from a router or mesh system that supports Wi-Fi 6 or Wi-Fi 6E.
You're a complete beginner
The Devolo app is fairly basic, and many features require the use of a web browser interface, which may be confusing for less experienced users.
Also consider
Netgear Orbi 373
The Orbi 373 only supports dual-band Wi-Fi 7 using the 2.4GHz and 5.0GHz bands, but it performs well, and the Orbi app is very straightforward and easy to use.
Amazon Eero 7
The Eero 7 is a modest dual-band performer with a modest set of features, but it’s competitively priced and easy to use, with the backing of the Amazon name behind it.

articles.title: Meta's Muse AI agent accused of accessing sensitive user data on iPhone and Mac without permission — agent shocks reporter by referring to confidential messages it wasn't granted access to
articles.text:
Meta's Muse AI agent accused of accessing sensitive user data on iPhone and Mac without permission — agent shocks reporter by referring to confidential messages it wasn't granted access to
Meta says Muse won't access data you tell it to ignore, but that doesn't appear to be true.
Meta's Muse is the hottest new AI agent in town right now after the company announced it earlier this month. But despite having been well-received by those who have put the agent through its paces since then, it now appears Muse might not be as private as Meta claims. The company has said that Muse was "built from the ground up to be a safe, secure, private, and widely available personal AI agent." But according to one report, Muse has been caught digging through thousands of personal messages without being given permission to do so.
Inc's Jason Aten has been putting Muse through its paces on two devices: a Mac mini and an iPhone. He says that he uses the Mac mini specifically as a place to test new agents like Muse, and once installed, he set about asking it to do some simple tasks. The agent said that it would be able to help him come up with new article ideas, which sounds just like something a journalist might want. But then Muse went rogue, suggesting a piece based on information it shouldn't have.
According to Aten, he was in conversation with a podcast cohost about the new iPhone 18 Pro and his decision to stick with last year's model. The conversation was in text form via the Messages app. That's when Muse popped up to suggest that the topic of discussion would make a good article. It offered to do some additional research on the subject, too. The problem was that Muse was never given permission to read Aten's messages.
When asked how it learned about the conversation, Muse claimed that the Mac version of the app was able to read incoming notifications. It then provided that context to the Meta iPhone app, which is where Muse made the article recommendation.
There had so far been no suggestion that this was possible, let alone something Muse was actually doing. Muse claimed that it wasn't reading Aten's actual messages, and that it didn't have access to chat histories. But Aten wasn't convinced.
After digging further, Aten was able to identify that Muse was indeed syncing a local Messages database. In fact, it was in the process of syncing all the way to row 187,462 of that database — suggesting Muse did have access to chat histories despite its protestations.
This, of course, is an issue. Aten confirmed that he didn't give Muse full disk access permissions on his Mac, something that should be required for the Messages database to be readable by the agent. Worse, David Singleton, the CEO of Meta Superintelligence Labs, responded to the situation with a thread of social media posts appearing to blame Aten for the situation.

articles.title: Plus de 19 000 films : la justice française s'en prend à l'hébergeur OVH pour bloquer deux sites pirates
articles.text:
Le tribunal judiciaire de Paris a ordonné à OVH, dans un jugement du 17 septembre 2026, d’empêcher l’accès depuis la France à deux sites pirates de films et de séries hébergés sur son infrastructure. La mesure, réclamée par Columbia Pictures, Disney, Netflix, Universal et deux autres sociétés américaines, doit être en place au plus tard 15 jours après la signification du jugement. Elle durera 18 mois, aux frais de l’hébergeur.
C’est l’hébergeur qui est visé ici, et non les fournisseurs d’accès à internet (Orange, SFR, Free, Bouygues Telecom), cibles habituelles de ce type de demande. L’information a d’abord été relayée par Univers Freebox. Le texte du jugement permet d’en préciser la portée.
Un blocage fondé sur l’article L. 336-2
Les studios ont assigné OVH le 4 juin 2026 selon la procédure accélérée au fond, sur la base de l’article L. 336-2 du code de la propriété intellectuelle. Ce texte permet au juge d’ordonner des mesures à l’encontre de « toute personne susceptible de contribuer à y remédier ». Avec l’accord des parties, l’affaire a été jugée sans audience.
Les deux sites concernés s’appellent « tekfullfilmizle » et « fullhdfilmizlesene ». Des agents assermentés de l’ALPA ont constaté qu’ils s’adressent à un public francophone. Le premier donnait accès sans autorisation à 2 611 films et 175 séries, le second à 19 738 films. Sur un échantillon de 15 liens vérifiés à la main pour chaque site, 14 renvoyaient vers des œuvres contrefaisantes, soit un taux annoncé de 93,33 % pour chacun, avec une marge d’erreur annoncée d’environ 3,4 %.
Le tribunal relève aussi que ces sites n’affichent aucune des mentions légales exigées par la loi pour la confiance dans l’économie numérique et qu’ils sont intégralement anonymisés via plusieurs prestataires. Pour les juges, cela tend à montrer que leurs exploitants connaissent le caractère illicite des liens, et cela rend difficile de les poursuivre directement.
Ce que doit faire OVH, et ce qu’il n’a pas à faire
OVH doit empêcher l’accès depuis le territoire français, outre-mer compris, aux noms de domaine et sous-domaines listés dans une annexe du jugement. Le moyen est laissé à son choix. OVH doit informer les studios dès que le blocage est en place, et ces derniers doivent lui signaler les domaines qui disparaissent, pour éviter des coûts inutiles.
Si les sites changent de nom de domaine ou de chemin d’accès, les studios pourront revenir devant le tribunal, en procédure accélérée au fond ou en référé, pour faire actualiser la mesure. Le jugement est exécutoire malgré un éventuel appel.
Les demandeurs voulaient davantage : un délai de cinq jours, la possibilité de suspendre les services d’hébergement des exploitants, un rappel du rôle de l’Arcom pour les sites miroirs et 15 000 euros de frais de justice. Le tribunal a retenu 15 jours et le blocage des noms de domaine. Il n’a pas repris la mention de l’Arcom dans son dispositif, et il a rejeté les demandes financières des deux côtés, OVH réclamant de son côté 5 000 euros. Chaque partie garde ses dépens.
Ce que disait OVH
OVH contestait le caractère contrefaisant des deux sites, jugeait les mesures disproportionnées et s’opposait à un blocage étendu à toute autre adresse IP. Le tribunal a estimé les constats de l’ALPA suffisamment probants. Il rappelle qu’il doit ménager un équilibre entre le droit d’auteur, la liberté d’entreprise des intermédiaires et la liberté d’information, en citant deux arrêts de la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne, et il écarte tout contrôle général et sans limite de durée.
Une question reste ouverte
Le jugement demande à OVH d’empêcher l’accès aux deux sites depuis la France « par tout moyen efficace », en citant notamment le blocage des noms de domaine. Les studios réclamaient aussi la possibilité de suspendre les services d’hébergement des exploitants, une option que le dispositif ne reprend pas expressément. Il vise par ailleurs des « abonnés » d’un contrat souscrit en France, une notion qui pourrait renvoyer plus naturellement aux fournisseurs d’accès qu’à un hébergeur. Comment OVH, qui héberge les serveurs, mettra concrètement le blocage en œuvre n’est pas précisé par la décision.
