articles.title: AirPods 5 : Apple améliore enfin la réparabilité de ses écouteurs
articles.text:
Depuis les premiers AirPods en 2016, iFixit n'a jamais accordé autre chose qu'un zéro pointé à la gamme. Avec la cinquième génération, ce score bouge pour la toute première fois.
iFixit, spécialiste de la réparation électronique, vient de passer les AirPods 5 au crible dans une nouvelle vidéo. Si les écouteurs sans fil d’Apple restent particulièrement difficiles à réparer, pour la première fois depuis le lancement de la gamme, ils décrochent une note supérieure à zéro en matière de réparabilité. La différence est minime, avec un score de 2/10, mais aucune génération précédente n’avait réussi à franchir ce seuil.
AirPods 5 : les batteries peuvent enfin être remplacées
Batteries collées, connexions soudées, boîtiers impossibles à ouvrir sans les endommager : depuis 2016, les différentes générations d’AirPods se heurtent au même problème lorsqu’il s’agit de réparation. La note de 0 sur 10 attribuée par iFixit était devenue une constante. Les AirPods 5 font enfin exception à la règle, grâce à une seule modification : les batteries intégrées dans chaque écouteur peuvent désormais être retirées et remplacées sans nécessairement détruire l’appareil.
Cette modification suffit à faire passer les AirPods 5 à 2/10 chez iFixit, soit deux points de plus que toutes les générations précédentes. Le score reste évidemment très faible, mais il est une première pour la gamme. L’opération nécessite néanmoins de solides compétences en réparation et s’adresse plutôt à un professionnel expérimenté ou à un utilisateur particulièrement aguerri. Pour le grand public, la manipulation reste donc loin d’être évidente.
La batterie s’améliore, mais le reste demeure difficile à réparer
Comme le montre iFixit dans sa vidéo, aller plus loin dans les entrailles des écouteurs reste malheureusement impossible sans les endommager. Le boîtier de charge n’a quant à lui bénéficié d’aucune amélioration et demeure aussi difficile à ouvrir que ses prédécesseurs.
iFixit précise également que les batteries gauche et droite ne sont pas interchangeables. Leur polarité est en effet inversée et leurs points de contact diffèrent légèrement, ce qui empêche d’utiliser la batterie d’un écouteur pour remplacer celle de l’autre. La réparation nécessite donc les bonnes pièces pour chaque côté.
Le démontage permet aussi à iFixit de montrer l’intérieur des écouteurs grâce à ses scanners CT. La puce H2, les microphones MEMS et les batteries sont littéralement empilés dans quelques centimètres cubes. Pas étonnant, dans ces conditions, que le moindre démontage supplémentaire tourne rapidement à la casse. La batterie gagne donc un peu en réparabilité, mais pour le reste, les AirPods 5 restent conçus comme leurs prédécesseurs.

articles.title: PlayStation Plus : les 3 jeux offerts en octobre 2026
articles.text:
Sony a dévoilé ce mercredi 30 septembre la liste des jeux offerts à tous les abonnés PlayStation Plus en octobre. On rappelle le principe : il est possible de les ajouter gratuitement à sa bibliothèque et on peut y jouer tant que l’abonnement est actif.
L’abonnement PlayStation Plus est obligatoire pour jouer en ligne à la plupart des jeux sur PS4 et sur PS5. Il existe trois formules : Essential (9,99 € par mois), Extra (15,99 € par mois) et Premium (18,99 € par mois).
Les jeux dans le PS Plus en octobre 2026
Trois jeux seront offerts à partir du mardi 6 octobre avec toutes les formules de l’abonnement PlayStation Plus :
- F1 25 (PS5)
- Hunt: Showdown 1896 (PS5)
- Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 (PS4, PS5)
Vous pourrez les ajouter à votre bibliothèque jusqu’au lundi 2 novembre.
F1 25
Vous n’avez pas envie que Kimi Antonelli devienne champion du monde ? Vous voulez que Fernando Alonso obtienne enfin une nouvelle victoire ? Vous rêvez d’un huitième titre de Lewis Hamilton, désormais chez Ferrari ? Cette simulation officielle peut réaliser vos fantasmes.
Le jeu offert reproduit toutefois la saison 2025. Pour celle en cours, marquée par le nouveau règlement, il faudra acheter l’extension.
Hunt: Showdown 1896
Relancé en 2024 sous ce nom, l’extraction-shooter de Crytek (un jeu de tir où il faut ressortir vivant avec son butin) se déroule dans des contrées reculées, où sévit un mal ancestral. Seul ou en équipe de trois au maximum, il faudra traquer des monstres pour toucher leur prime, puis s’échapper avant que les chasseurs adverses ne vous tombent dessus.
Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2
La célèbre saga Earth Defense Force, où l’on combat des monstres, adopte un style visuel cubique. Mais l’objectif n’a pas changé et on peut y jouer jusqu’à quatre en coopération en ligne, ou à deux en écran partagé.

articles.title: Flipkart metrics reveal D2C brands scaling nationwide through non-metro demand
articles.text:
Flipkart metrics reveal D2C brands scaling nationwide through non-metro demand
Data shows brands like Kapiva, Open Secret, and Plum are driving over half their growth from Tier II and III markets by leveraging real-time search trends and multi-speed delivery options.
Direct-to-consumer brands across India are fundamentally shifting how they grow. Rather than relying solely on their own websites, companies are using marketplace platforms like Flipkart to handle everything from regional distribution to product development.
Looking at customer data shared by Flipkart during a round table discussion, it becomes clear that demand for wellness, skincare, and healthy food extends well beyond India’s major metropolitan hubs. Take Ayurvedic brand Kapiva, for example—roughly 66% of its sales on the platform come directly from Tier III cities, with over 70% of its Gen Z shoppers living in Tier II and III markets. A similar story plays out in beauty: non-metro regions account for over half the total category demand on Flipkart and generate two-thirds of all beauty search queries. For skincare brand Plum and healthy snacking company Open Secret, tapping into this nationwide logistics network has made reaching smaller towns far more predictable.
Platform search behavior and customer demographics are also replacing traditional focus groups when it comes to product strategy. Gen Z now makes up nearly 60% of beauty buyers on Flipkart, and more than 60% of these young shoppers start their search with specific ingredients like vitamin C or niacinamide rather than looking for a brand name. That intent-focused browsing aligns with big year-over-year surges in targeted skincare, including a 123% jump in face wash sales, a 120% increase in gel moisturizers, and over 80% growth in face serums.
Over in wellness, Gen Z makes up half of all Apple Cider Vinegar buyers and over 40% of buyers for products like Virgin Coconut Oil and Amla juice.
When it comes to sales performance, brands balance two very different retail moments: massive holiday events and ultra-fast daily fulfillment. Open Secret, which now gets about 30% of its revenue through Flipkart and has grown 3x on the platform over four years, sees its daily order volume jump 5x to 7x during Big Billion Days. During the same event, Kapiva experiences up to a 9x spike in demand for Shilajit on opening day alone, pushing its overall festive revenue 50% above normal periods.
At the same time, immediate delivery options like Flipkart Minutes are changing how people buy everyday essentials. Most quick-commerce orders come from targeted searches rather than passive browsing, with top categories including snacks, dry fruits, cooking ghee, and daily skincare. Off the back of these quick-delivery options, Plum expects its festive sales in the category to double year-over-year.""

articles.title: Comment l'Europe encadre les microtransactions de Valorant et Call of Duty — Frandroid
articles.text:
La moitié de la population européenne joue aux jeux vidéo et une grosse partie est régulièrement incitée à dépenser de la monnaie virtuelle pour améliorer son expérience. Que ce soit pour changer son apparence, acquérir des objets ou progresser plus facilement dans le jeu, le prix de ces Minecoin, V-Bucks ou Robux devrait être « clair et transparent », a tranché l’Union européenne.
Comme le remarque le Figaro, la Commission européenne vient d’ouvrir une enquête contre des éditeurs de jeu soupçonnés de pratique abusive liée à l’utilisation de monnaies virtuelles dans leurs jeux.
Des règles strictes pour faciliter les transactions
L’enquête vise des gros noms du secteur, comme Minecraft, Valorant, Call of Duty Mobile ou Candy Crush. Par ricochet, ce sont aussi leurs studios qui sont visés, parmi lesquels on trouve Ubisoft, King.com, Riot Games ou Activision. Pas du menu fretin, donc.
Il n’est pas question de bannir complètement les systèmes de microtransaction, mais plutôt de les rendre moins opaques pour les joueurs et joueuses. Selon les règles dictées par Bruxelles, le prix réel des microtransactions devrait, par exemple, être affiché, la pression pour acheter des éléments pour progresser devrait disparaître et des protections pour éviter d’inciter les enfants à la dépense devraient être mises en place.
Cela fait suite à une discussion ouverte depuis 2024 avec des éditeurs de jeu qui n’a mené nulle part selon le Bureau européen de protection des consommateurs (BEUC). « Personne ne devrait avoir besoin d’une calculatrice pour savoir combien il ou elle dépense dans un jeu vidéo. Les vrais prix doivent être affichés clairement et il est nécessaire de mettre fin aux pratiques trompeuses qui masquent les coûts et incitent les joueurs et joueuses à dépenser davantage », a déclaré Agustín Reyna, directeur du BEUC.
Des changements à venir
En France, c’est la DGCCRF qui pourrait hériter du pouvoir de pénaliser les entreprises qui continuent à brouiller les pistes avec des montages douteux basés sur des monnaies virtuelles. « Pendant trop longtemps, le secteur du jeu vidéo a bénéficié d’une forme de complaisance, voire d’aveuglement, de la part des autorités. Comme si les règles élémentaires de protection des consommateurs cessaient de s’appliquer dès lors qu’il s’agissait d’un univers numérique ou d’un loisir. Cette époque doit prendre fin », a rajouté la présidente de Que Choisir Ensemble.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Fortnite : Epic contourne Apple et Google pour proposer des V-Bucks moins chers
            
Si ces changements ne devaient pas arriver partout du jour au lendemain, les résultats de l’enquête ouverte contre les gros studios visés devraient rapidement inciter tous les autres à rentrer dans le rang.

articles.title: De 600.000 a 10 millones de coches: China fabrica tantos coches que ya no hay barcos suficientes para sacarlos del país
articles.text:
China está construyendo más coches de los que puede transportar por barco, y eso es una realidad. Los buques que funcionan a modo de gigantescos garajes flotantes (los conocidos como Ro-Ro) están muy solicitados. De hecho, se solicitan con muchísima antelación, y eso ha disparado enormemente los precios de flete.
Saturación. Las exportaciones son ahora la vía de escape de China para una industria repleta de marcas y escasa de compradores en su propio país. La escasez ya está rediseñando la forma en que los coches cruzan los océanos y también está empujando a los fabricantes de coches chinos a comprar sus propias flotas.
En cifras. Según el grupo de investigación Mobility Global, China exportó algo menos de 600.000 coches y furgonetas en 2019. El grupo prevé hasta 10 millones este año. El corredor marítimo Clarksons afirma que la tarifa media anual de flete para un gran transportador de coches alcanzó los 70.000 dólares al día en junio, frente a los 42.500 dólares de finales del año pasado. Y es que las tarifas para el envío de coches se encuentran ahora en el doble de sus niveles prepandémicos, según declaraba al Wall Street Journal Andreas Enger, CEO de la naviera noruega Höegh Autoliners.
Por qué ahora. Las empresas encargaron miles de millones de dólares en nuevos buques de transporte de coches entre 2022 y 2025, por lo que se suponía que las tarifas bajarían a medida que llegaran esos barcos. Wallenius Wilhelmsen, el mayor operador de transporte de automóviles, cuenta que la flota mundial ha crecido alrededor de un 40 % y que todavía no es suficiente. Este crecimiento ha venido impulsado precisamente por las exportaciones procedentes de China.
UN VISTAZO A...
Tras el impulso. Los fabricantes de coches chinos están mirando al extranjero porque en casa la situación se está volviendo más difícil:
- Más de 100 marcas nacionales compiten por un mercado que se está reduciendo. La Agencia Internacional de la Energía informaba que las ventas de coches en China cayeron más de un 20 % en el primer semestre de 2026.
- Tu Le, director general de Sino Auto Insights, contaba al WSJ que las exportaciones funcionan como una “válvula de liberación de presión”, señalando además que, en Alemania, una marca china no tiene a 20 compatriotas luchando por la misma venta.
- Hay una grandísima demanda de coches chinos desde el extranjero, pues la Asociación de Constructores Europeos de Automóviles informaba en su momento que BYD había conseguido más del doble de matriculaciones en la UE durante el primer semestre de 2026, y las de SAIC subieron un 19 %.
Contenedores. Eric Dessupoiu, de Ceva Logistics, contaba al WSJ que los fabricantes de automóviles prefieren los transportadores de coches porque embarcar y desembarcar los vehículos conduciéndolos es más barato y seguro para los coches, pero quienes no tienen alternativa utilizan contenedores. Kristoffersen afirmó que hasta cuatro millones de vehículos al año salen de China en contenedores u otras alternativas a los buques Ro-Ro. Un contenedor de 40 pies suele almacenar de dos a cuatro coches, según CarNewsChina. Empresas como Maersk y MSC prestan ahora sus servicios directamente a los fabricantes de automóviles, según comenta Christoph Seitz de DP World.
Flat racks. Desde CarNewsChina comparten que Leapmotor, respaldada por Stellantis, ha utilizado sistemas flat-rack, que asegura los coches en bastidores metálicos cargados en buques de carga convencionales. El medio afirma que más de 1.800 vehículos han ido a Brasil de esta manera. Según el medio, la empresa también ha adaptado buques multipropósito para el transporte de pasta de papel con bastidores plegables que pueden llevar más de 1.000 coches por viaje, apilados en hasta ocho niveles. Así que donde se puedan meter coches, se meten.
El problema es que los contenedores y los bastidores añaden más pasos durante el trayecto, ya que los coches deben llevarse a una instalación cerca del puerto, cargarse, levantarse con grúa y repetir el proceso en el destino.
El siguiente paso: poseer los barcos. El ejemplo más claro lo tenemos en BYD, que está tratando el transporte marítimo como parte de su negocio. Y es que tal y como comparten desde CarNewsChina, el fabricante completó una flota de ocho barcos en septiembre de 2025, con buques con capacidad para 7.200 o 9.000 coches cada uno. Por otro lado, el medio marítimo New Ships contaba que BYD había encargado 10 transportadores más con capacidad de hasta 9.200 coches. Con esto, BYD tendría capacidad suficiente para transportar más de 130.000 vehículos a través de sus 18 buques. El medio calcula que esto elevaría la capacidad anual de exportación de BYD de 1 millón a unos 2,5 millones de coches.

articles.title: The iPhone Duo is reportedly facing production challenges with low yields and quality concerns
articles.text:
Bottom line: After years of rumors and speculation, Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to go on sale next month, but getting enough of them into customers' hands could prove the harder part. Foxconn, the contract manufacturer responsible for producing the device, is reportedly facing severe production constraints that could limit early output, raising the prospect of tight supply for what is now Apple's most expensive iPhone.
According to an insider quoted by Chinese outlet Jiemian News, final assembly yields for the iPhone Duo were only slightly above 60% as of September 17. It could take Foxconn another six months to a year to raise yields to more mature levels while maintaining Apple's exacting quality standards.
The insider added that Foxconn has been continuously adjusting equipment, assembly processes, and production settings as it tries to bring yields up to acceptable levels. Suppliers are also reportedly lobbying Apple to ease certain quality requirements to speed up production and meet expected demand.
What makes matters worse is that the problems extend well beyond Foxconn. According to the report, several suppliers are also experiencing production issues, with Samsung Display singled out as one of the worst affected. The company is reportedly struggling with low yields for its foldable OLED panels and hinges, largely due to last-minute design changes by Apple.
Another supply chain source claimed that Apple's total production target for the iPhone Duo in 2026 is between six and eight million units, much lower than the 20 to 30 million units an iPhone Pro or Pro Max typically ships over its full product cycle. A separate source reportedly said Apple's sales guidance for the iPhone Duo is in excess of five million units.
According to a separate report from MyDrivers, several suppliers have told Apple it might have to choose between yield and output, as the entire iPhone Duo manufacturing ecosystem is facing serious production issues. The report, however, did not reveal the identities of any of the suppliers urging Apple to lower its quality standards to meet output targets.
The sources explained that ramping up production under the current constraints might improve output, but at the cost of yield, with the number of defective units expected to skyrocket, especially if Apple is unwilling to compromise on quality. Higher output would therefore result in higher scrap costs, which may not be in Apple's best interest.
Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo earlier this month at its 'Surprise and Shine' event in Cupertino, California. The device starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, lower than the $2,500+ range some analysts had predicted, and similar to the $2,099 asking price of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.

articles.title: Google finds vulnerability disclosures doubled as AI changes which flaws get discovered - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google finds vulnerability disclosures doubled as AI changes which flaws get discovered
A new report out today from Google LLC’s Google Threat Intelligence Group finds that monthly software vulnerability disclosures doubled between January and August.
Not surprisingly, artificial intelligence is changing which flaws get discovered as well, and GTIG said half of those turned up by AI agents allow remote code execution.
August’s count of 10,740 vulnerability disclosures was more than twice January’s 5,045. GTIG cautioned that raw totals can overstate the threat, because automated identifier assignment in open-source ecosystems inflates them. Flaws with “Linux Kernel” in their descriptions accounted for about 5,000 records this year without producing a single zero-day exploited in the wild. High-risk disclosures on GTIG’s own scale rose 167% over the same months to 350 in August, and 128 of those came from Oracle Corp.’s quarterly patch release and Linux kernel network driver advisories.
By GTIG’s count, attackers exploited 141 newly disclosed vulnerabilities in the wild between January and August, more than the 127 recorded across all of 2025. Measured against disclosure volume the number is small, at about one flaw in 431, and the report notes that a single vendor’s disclosure cycle or one busy campaign can move the monthly figure.
Zero-day exploitation has averaged 11 a month so far this year against eight in 2025, with most months landing between eight and 12 until August brought 22. Zero-days, new vulnerabilities that haven’t been patched, still made up 62% of the 141 exploited flaws. Most of the growth, GTIG suggests, has come from n-days, meaning flaws that attackers go after once they are public and usually already patched.
Attackers may be using large language models to compare product versions and patches, the report says, so they can turn known flaws into working exploits quickly. Exploited high-risk flaws numbered 75 this year, up from 28 in all of 2025.
The report then turns to the vulnerabilities AI itself is finding. GTIG believes public data undercounts them, since vulnerability databases carry no standard tag for AI-assisted discovery. Large cloud and software-as-a-service providers also fix many AI-surfaced bugs in production without ever requesting an identifier, because those identifiers are normally reserved for software that customers have to patch themselves.
Among the vulnerabilities GTIG identified as likely AI discoveries, 58% fell in the moderate tier of its risk scale. Bugs found by people and conventional scanners land there about half as often, and 69% of those rate as low-risk. Researchers tend to aim their agents at critical infrastructure and sensitive privilege boundaries on purpose, and GTIG thinks that choice likely explains much of the gap.
Remote code execution shows up in only 26% of all other disclosures, and the report says AI’s higher rate likely stems from how well agents pick out memory corruption and logic bypasses deep in C and C++ code that static analyzers tend to miss.
GTIG treats confirmed attacks on AI-found flaws as an early indicator for now. The example it cites to show the risk is “not purely theoretical” is CVE-2026-1731. The bug lets an unauthenticated attacker inject operating system commands into BeyondTrust Corp.’s Privileged Remote Access and Remote Support products, and a research agent from Hacktron AI Inc. found it autonomously.
Within four days of disclosure in February, GTIG saw one threat cluster exploiting the flaw, and five more had joined within a week. The attackers went on to escalate privileges and steal data, and payloads they dropped included SNOWLIGHT and SPARKRAT malware plus cryptocurrency miners.
The report’s final section covers flaws in AI software. Of the 2,076 such disclosures GTIG has tracked since the start of 2025, more than 1,500 came this year. Agent orchestration frameworks such as Flowise and Langflow account for roughly half.
Visual workflow builders of that kind often include nodes that execute code, and attackers can reach them with prompt injection or a crafted workflow file. Inference and serving software such as vLLM, Ollama and LiteLLM drew 212 disclosures, and GTIG traced nearly a quarter of them to unauthenticated application programming interface endpoints or server-side request forgery.
GTIG has not yet observed zero-day exploitation of AI infrastructure. Only a handful of disclosed flaws have been exploited in the wild, among them a command injection bug in LiteLLM’s Model Context Protocol server preview endpoints and two in Langflow. In July, Sysdig Inc. documented an autonomous ransomware attack that broke in through the older of the Langflow flaws.
The Google unit expects discovery and exploitation to keep climbing over the short to medium term. Exploitation remains concentrated on perimeter appliances and exposed enterprise services, according to the report.
Its advice to organizations is to drop unprioritized mass patching and let threat intelligence decide what gets fixed first, with targeted defenses at the edge. Software vendors should run agentic AI code review before code ships, the report argues, naming Google’s own CodeMender as one option. If that becomes standard practice, growth in public disclosures could eventually slow, GTIG said.

articles.title: Freidora de aire vs horno microondas: cuál electrodoméstico consume más energía
articles.text:
Muchas familias se preguntan qué electrodoméstico consume más energía, la freidora de aire o el horno microondas, cuando buscan reducir el gasto eléctrico sin cambiar sus hábitos de cocina. La respuesta depende del plato, la cantidad de comida y, sobre todo, del tiempo de uso.
Los dos electrodomésticos concentran la cocción en espacios pequeños y suelen requerir menos electricidad que un horno convencional. Sin embargo, el microondas suele imponerse en preparaciones rápidas, mientras que la freidora de aire resulta más adecuada cuando se busca dorar o lograr una superficie crujiente.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué aparato requiere menor potencia eléctrica
El microondas suele operar con una potencia de entre 900 W y 1.500 W, según los datos del Instituto para la Diversificación y Ahorro de la Energía (IDAE). Aunque la cifra puede parecer elevada, el aparato necesita pocos minutos para recalentar, descongelar o cocinar determinados alimentos.
Por su parte, la freidora de aire suele situarse entre los 1.000 W y 1.800 W. Por esa razón, puede demandar más potencia que un microondas, aunque su consumo final depende de cuánto tiempo permanece encendida. Una freidora usada durante pocos minutos puede gastar menos que otro aparato con menor potencia que funciona durante más tiempo.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué el microondas suele ser la opción más eficiente para ahorrar
El microondas calienta los alimentos con rapidez y evita el largo período de calentamiento previo que requieren otros aparatos. Endesa señala que, en algunos platos, el ahorro frente a una cocina convencional puede alcanzar el 75%, por la menor duración de la preparación.
Su mejor rendimiento aparece en tareas concretas: recalentar comidas, descongelar alimentos y cocinar verduras al vapor; y cortar los ingredientes en porciones pequeñas reduce el tiempo de cocción. Otra alternativa consiste en apagar el electrodoméstico unos minutos antes de terminar, para que el calor acumulado complete el proceso.
Cuánta energía puede consumir una freidora de aire al año
Una freidora de aire de 1.000 W, utilizada 15 minutos por día, puede consumir cerca de 90 kWh al año, según Endesa. Esa cifra permite dimensionar su gasto anual, aunque puede variar según la potencia del modelo, la temperatura elegida y la frecuencia de uso.
PUBLICIDAD
El aparato aprovecha un compartimiento reducido y un sistema de circulación de aire caliente. Esto permite acortar los tiempos frente a un horno de gran tamaño y, en muchos casos, elimina la necesidad de precalentarlo. Por ese motivo, puede ser una alternativa de menor gasto para porciones pequeñas o medianas.
Para qué comidas conviene usar cada electrodoméstico
El microondas tiene límites en recetas que requieren una corteza dorada, una masa horneada o una textura crujiente. No suele ser la opción indicada para repostería compleja ni para preparaciones que dependen de una cocción seca y uniforme en la superficie.
En cambio, la freidora de aire ofrece mejores resultados en papas, pollo, croquetas y otros alimentos que necesitan dorarse. Su funcionamiento se asemeja al de un horno de convección compacto.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, para cocinar grandes cantidades puede ser insuficiente y obligar a realizar varias tandas, lo que aumenta el consumo y el tiempo total.
Qué hábitos permiten ahorrar recursos sin comprar otro electrodoméstico
El ahorro no depende solo del aparato elegido. Apagar el horno unos minutos antes de finalizar la cocción permite aprovechar el calor residual. Tapar las ollas reduce el tiempo necesario para hervir agua y ayuda a conservar la temperatura durante la preparación.
Asimismo, evitar el precalentamiento cuando la receta no lo exige puede reducir el gasto inicial. En platos de cocción prolongada, como algunos asados, es posible incorporar los alimentos desde el comienzo. Para descongelar, el microondas suele demandar menos energía que el horno o el uso de agua caliente.

articles.title: Galaxy S25 Ultra registra queda abrupta de preço e tem 59% OFF na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy S25 Ultra registra queda abrupta de preço e tem 59% OFF na Amazon
Galaxy S25 Ultra (256 GB) traz câmera de 200 MP, corpo de titânio e desempenho de sobra; celular premium da Samsung tem preço mais baixo com pagamento no Pix
O Galaxy S25 Ultra de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 4.958 no Pix na Amazon. O celular premium da Samsung com câmera de 200 MP que filma em 8K, corpo de titânio e chip Snapdragon de ponta, recebe desconto de 59% sobre o preço original de R$ 11.999 e fica bem abaixo da média recente.
Um dos destaques do Galaxy S25 Ultra é seu kit traseiro de câmeras, que filma em 8K a até 30 fps. Ele traz wide de 200 MP com OIS, ultrawide de 50 MP e telefotos de 10 MP e 50 MP com zoom óptico de 3x e 5x, respectivamente. A frontal de 12 MP tira ótimas selfies e por sua vez filma em 4K a 60 fps.
Outro destaque é seu corpo de titânio ultrarresistente, enquanto o sucessor S26 Ultra usa alumínio na construção. O vidro Gorilla Armor 2 reveste o gadget de 2025 de ambos os lados e resiste a arranhões e pancadas, e a certificação IP68 confere proteção em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua tela AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,9″ possui taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de até 2.600 nits, sendo capaz de reproduzir cores excelentes com alta fluidez em apps e games, além de garantir visibilidade confortável em qualquer ambiente.
O chip Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite e 12 GB de RAM dão ao S25 Ultra grande poder de fogo para rodar apps pesados em multitarefa, games e soluções do Galaxy AI localmente. Os 256 GB de armazenamento permitem guardar uma quantidade adequada de vídeos e fotos.
Sua bateria de 5.000 mAh resiste a até 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a fabricante. O suporte ao carregamento rápido de 45 W via USB-C e de 15 W sem fio garante o uso por tempo prolongado, ideal para usuários com agendas corridas.
O Galaxy S25 Ultra de 256 GB (R$ 4.958 no Pix) foi atualizado para o Android 16 e é elegível a mais seis updates do sistema operacional. O celular da Samsung possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.

articles.title: iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop review: Strong gaming value and extras
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The iBuyPower Slate is a well-executed mid-range gaming desktop that pairs attractive styling, thoughtful extras, and strong RTX 5070-powered gaming performance. While its Ryzen 7 7700X3D isn't as capable in productivity workloads as Intel-based competitors, gamers looking for a capable 1080p and 1440p machine with quality included peripherals will find plenty to like.
Reasons to buy
- +Strong gaming performance
- +Attractive tempered glass case with RGB lighting
- +Quality included mechanical keyboard and mouse
- +360 mm liquid cooler with integrated status display
Reasons to avoid
- -Productivity performance trails similarly-priced Intel systems
- -Cooling fans can get loud under CPU-heavy workloads
- -RGB software lacks per-component control
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
The $1,999 iBuyPower Slate arrives with a formula that's hard to argue with: an RTX 5070, a Ryzen 7 7700X3D, a 360mm liquid cooler, and a tempered-glass chassis with plenty of RGB lighting. It even goes beyond expectations by including gaming peripherals that don't feel like afterthoughts.
But in an increasingly competitive mid-range desktop market, attractive extras and gaming prowess alone aren't always enough. The question is whether the Slate's gaming-first focus justifies its price when rivals offer stronger all-around performance for similar money.
Design of the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
There’s no mistaking the Slate for anything but a gaming machine. It’s designed to be seen inside and out, with a full-view tempered glass side panel. The front panel’s triangle glass partially shows off a trio of 120 mm RGB fans. The tower sits firmly in mid-tower territory, at 8.7 x 19.3 x 19.5 inches.
The mesh covering the rest of the front and top permits airflow and should do a decent job of blocking dust, though the case’s only removable air filter is under the bottom-mounted power supply.
Inside, the Slate’s blacked-out interior offers an RGB light strip running along the power supply compartment and up the front panel. Additional lighting comes from the two memory DIMMs. The GPU, an Asus Dual RTX 5070 in our review unit, lacks illumination. The lighting can be controlled via the Hyte Nexus app, though not on a per-component basis. (See the Software section later in this review.)
iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop Specifications
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D | 
| Motherboard | ASRock B560M-CX R2.0 | 
| Memory | 32GB DDR5-5200 (2x 16GB) | 
| Graphics | Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 (Asus Dual Gaming OC; 12GB GDDR7, 2,542 MHz boost clock) | 
| Storage | 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD (Patriot P410) | 
| Networking | RZ616 Wi-Fi 6E | 
| Front Ports | USB-C 3.2, 2x USB-A 3.2, headphone and microphone jacks | 
| Rear Ports | USB-C 3.2 (10 Gbps), USB-A 3.2 (10 Gbps), 2x USB-A 3.2 (5 Gbps), 4x USB 2.0, Ethernet, HDMI, audio jacks | 
| Power Supply | 750 watts, non-modular | 
| Cooling | 360 mm liquid (iBuyPower) | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 Home | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 8.7 x 19.3 x 19.5 inches (221 x 490 x 495 mm) | 
| Price (as configured) | $1,999.99 | 
Ports and Upgradeability on the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
Mid-tower desktops tend to include lots of ports, and iBuyPower’s Slate doesn’t disappoint. The top-mounted front connectivity includes one USB-C and two USB-A (all 5 Gbps) plus separate headphone and microphone jacks. The positioning of these ports works best if the desktop is placed on the floor; it’s less ideal on a desk.
Rear connectivity on the ASRock B650M-CX motherboard includes one USB-C 3.2 (10 Gbps), one USB-A 3.2 (10 Gbps), two USB-A 3.2 (5 Gbps), four USB 2.0, Ethernet, HDMI, and audio jacks. Though there are no truly high-speed ports, they aren’t expected outside of high-end towers with pricier motherboards. The desktop also includes Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth – the antennas must be connected as shown here for meaningful range.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The side panels come off with a tug at the top rear, hinging outward and away. Seven 120 mm fans – three front, three on the top-mounted 360 mm CPU cooling radiator, and one rear – provide plentiful airflow. Cabling is reasonably tidy, though the bundle of unused cables from the non-modular 750-watt power supply is a bit of a mess.
The CPU cooler is more than a basic model, with an LED screen showing CPU temperature, frequency, and load. The display can’t be customized, though it can be toggled off in the Hyte Nexus app.
The Slate’s expansion options include one open PCIe x16 slot and four DIMM slots, two of which are unpopulated. The motherboard offers two M.2 2280 drive slots. There are two 2.5-inch drive sleds behind the motherboard, but no room for a 3.5-inch drive.
Gaming and Graphics on the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
We are testing the iBuyPower Slate with a Ryzen 7 7700X3D processor, GeForce RTX 5070 GPU, and 32GB of RAM.
Playing 007 First Light, at 3840 x 2160 with High settings and DLSS enabled, I observed between 60 and 70 frames per second (FPS) in outdoor scenes and closer to 80 FPS indoors. Using DLSS was required for smooth gameplay, as I saw roughly half the FPS without it.
Our comparison desktops include the Asus ROG G700 (Core Ultra 7 265KF, RTX 5070, $2,029.99 when reviewed) and the CyberPowerPC Gaming Desktop GXi3800BSTV2 (Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, RTX 5070, $2,309.99), both mid-tower systems with the same GPU but Intel processors.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
At 1080p, iBuyPower’s Slate proved competitive overall, matching the Asus and CyberPowerPC in Shadow of the Tomb Raider (Highest settings), Cyberpunk 2077 (Ray Tracing Ultra), and Black Myth: Wukong (Cinematic). However, its Ryzen 7 7700X3D paid dividends in Far Cry 6 (Ultra), where its 185 FPS was well ahead of the Asus (110 FPS) and CyberPowerPC (141 FPS). It led by a similar amount in Red Dead Redemption 2, with 145 FPS against the Asus’ 120 FPS and the CyberPowerPC’s 126 FPS.
The Slate generally didn’t differentiate itself from the other desktops at the 4K resolution, an expected result since that resolution is almost always GPU-limited and these systems all rely on an RTX 5070. The exception was Far Cry 6, where the Slate’s 97 FPS greatly outperformed the 80 and 81 FPS produced by the Asus and CyberPowerPC, respectively.
Overall, despite its Ryzen 7 7700X3D not being nearly as powerful for general use as the Core Ultra 7 265K and Core Ultra 7 270K Plus featured in our competing systems, it can outperform both chips in games.
We stress-test gaming desktops running 15 loops of the Metro: Exodus benchmark at RTX settings. The iBuyPower desktop posted highly stable performance, averaging 145.7 FPS across all runs with less than a one frame variance across all runs. The Ryzen 7 7700X3D’s average temperature was 43 degrees Celsius and its average clock was 4.29 GHz. The RTX 5070 ran at 64 C and had an average core clock of 2.64 GHz.
I noticed a decent amount of fan noise from the Slate particularly when the CPU was stressed, causing the triple-fan CPU cooler to quickly ramp up to high speed. The fan noise was hardly noticeable for daily use and was relatively low while gaming as well.
Productivity Performance on the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
We tested the iBuyPower Slate gaming desktop featuring a Ryzen 7 7700X3D processor, 32GB of dual-channel DDR5-5200 RAM, and a 1TB PCIe 4.0 solid-state drive (a Patriot P410 as tested).
Productivity performance isn’t a strong point for this Slate configuration. Though its Ryzen 7 7700X3D remains potent for gaming, its previous generation eight-core architecture is outmuscled by the Core Ultra 7 K-class chips in both the Asus and CyberPowerPC systems, particularly the latter with its refreshed Core Ultra 7 270K Plus. The delta was significant: iBuyPower's system scored 14,222 in Geekbench multi-core versus 22,485 for CyberPowerPC, and took 3:35 to complete our 4K to 1080p Handbrake transcoding test versus just 2:03 for the Asus and 1:45 for the CyberPowerPC. The iBuyPower system does, however, include a decent storage drive, proving competitive in our 25GB file transfer test.
Despite the Slate’s performance delta versus the Core Ultra 7 systems, this PC is still highly capable for daily productivity and moderate content creation, such as video editing. Only those squeezing every last drop of performance out of their CPU will find it compelling to go with a more powerful chip than the Ryzen 7 7700X3D.
Keyboard and Mouse with the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
The Slate includes much better than average peripherals. The mechanical keyboard is the standout. Though not stated in the specs, it feels like it uses linear switches favored by gamers for their predictability. It felt rock solid in my testing and wasn’t overly loud. The keyboard supports RGB backlighting, though not per-key – the lighting can be set in the included Hyte Nexus app for various colors and patterns. You can also control the lighting through keyboard shortcuts – Fn+Ctrl cycles colors, Fn+Left/Right arrows alter brightness, Fn+Space Bar disables lighting, and Fn+Alt cycles through 16 backlighting patterns, such as breathing, pulsing, and steady. It’s also nice to see that the keyboard uses a detachable USB-C cable.
The mouse is also better than average, though it’s only for right handers. The standard buttons offer a solid feel, with two side buttons and a notched scroll wheel. The DPI button behind the scroll wheel switches between 1,200, 2,400, 3,500, 5,500, and 7,200 DPI, which are visually indicated by the DPI button illuminating in red, blue, green, purple, and yellow, respectively. The mouse fits my medium-size hand well. It’s internally backlit in RGB color, which can be configured in Hyte Nexus or toggled through 10 modes pressing the button on the underside. Patterns include color streaming, steady, and breathing, to name a few.
Software and Warranty on the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop
Besides the usual preinstalled Windows 11 apps, iBuyPower only preloads one app – Hyte Nexus. It provides basic component temperature and frequency monitoring, but its real focus is RGB lighting control.
The menu is confusing – there are tiles for different components, such as the case, but these have no effect since the particular case used in the Slate isn’t recognized. Instead, all the action happens in the Lighting section. Many preset lighting recipes are included, such as Rainbow, Aurora, Ice, Fireplace, and Forest, which even apply to the keyboard and mouse. There are also options for screen mirroring, audio visualization, and static colors. You can save your settings in profiles.
That said, there’s no way to control lighting on a per-component basis – colors and patterns apply to all components at once since they are all connected to ARGB header 1. Confusingly, the app lets you change settings for the other headers, but this has no effect since nothing is connected to them. If the app indicated that those headers aren’t connected, this would have been more straightforward. The Slate nonetheless allows a decent amount of lighting customization despite lacking an advanced lighting controller, which would have increased the cost.
iBuyPower covers the Slate with a one-year parts and labor warranty.
iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop Configurations
We tested the iBuyPower Slate Gaming Desktop with a Ryzen 7 7700X3D processor, GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card, 32GB (2x 16GB) of DDR5-5200 RAM, and a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD. A mechanical backlit gaming keyboard and mouse are included in the box.
Best Buy offers several other variations of the Slate. A $1,679.99 starter model included a Core i7-14700F and RTX 5060 while a $1,799.99 model stepped up to a Core Ultra 7 265F and RTX 5060 Ti. Above our test model, a $2,299.99 variant included a Ryzen 9 9900X3D, while a range-topping $2,999.99 model offered a Ryzen 9 7900X, an RTX 5080, and a 2TB SSD.
Bottom Line
iBuyPower’s Slate gets the mid-tier gaming desktop formula almost exactly right. Visually, its RGB lighting is attractive and reasonably configurable even if it lacks per-component control, and its RTX 5070 and Ryzen 7 7700X3D comfortably power through today’s games at 1080p and 1440p, with 4K possible using dialed-down visual quality or DLSS. iBuyPower goes above expectations by including a liquid CPU cooler with a built-in screen and by including a mechanical RGB keyboard and gaming mouse.
Where the Slate stumbles, as least in our reviewed configuration, is processing power. Though the Ryzen 7 7700X3D remains potent for gaming, it’s outclassed by Core Ultra 7 K-class chips for general use, which can be had in systems costing similar money. But for pure gamers, this Slate is a standup performer.
Charles Jefferies is a freelance reviewer for Tom’s Hardware US. He covers laptop and desktop PCs, especially gaming models.

articles.title: VPNs dodge a bullet — New US piracy bill targets ISPs but leaves VPNs alone
articles.text:
VPNs dodge a bullet — New US piracy bill targets ISPs but leaves VPNs alone
The newly introduced DEFEND IP Act targets broadband providers and DNS resolvers to fight overseas piracy, but explicitly excludes virtual private networks
- The DEFEND IP Act is a new bicameral site-blocking bill targeting ISPs, DNS
- The bill explicitly exempts VPNs from carrying out blocking orders
- It allows copyright holders to seek court orders to block foreign platforms
Last week, privacy advocates raised alarms about a US bill that could force virtual private networks to act as piracy blocklists. Now, a newly introduced competing proposal has taken a decidedly different approach — leaving the best VPN providers completely off the hook.
Senator Thom Tillis and Representative Zoe Lofgren have jointly introduced the DEFEND IP Act (Deterring Extraterritorial Foreign Exploitation of Networks Damaging Intellectual Property). The bicameral bill merges two previous legislative drafts into a single proposal aimed at giving copyright holders the power to compel intermediaries to block foreign pirate sites.
However, Representative Darrell Issa's competing American Copyright Protection Act (ACPA) included VPNs in its scope. According to an analysis by TorrentFreak, the newly introduced DEFEND IP Act explicitly leaves them out.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
How the DEFEND IP Act spares VPNs
Under the DEFEND IP Act, court-ordered blocking would apply to broadband providers with at least 50,000 subscribers and public DNS resolvers generating over $100 million in annual revenue. This high financial threshold easily captures tech giants like Google and Cloudflare.
Yet, the proposed legislation specifically carves out an exemption for virtual private network (VPN) tools. The bill's text excludes "an entity that exclusively provides virtual private network services or similar service [sic] that encrypt and route user traffic through intermediary servers."
While the word "exclusively" leaves some room for interpretation when it comes to cybersecurity companies that bundle their VPNs with other features like antivirus software, the legislative intent to shield core VPN operations is clear.
If passed, the DEFEND IP Act would establish a two-step legal process. First, a federal court must formally classify a website as a "foreign digital piracy site." To qualify, the platform must be primarily designed for copyright infringement or intentionally marketed as a piracy destination.
Once designated, rightsholders can return to a judge to request a formal blocking order. The court would then determine if the block is "technically feasible and effective." These blocking orders would remain valid for a year, can be renewed, and apply directly to live streaming events, meaning a rogue sports broadcasting site could be blocked before a match even starts.
Digital rights advocates push back
Despite the explicit VPN exemption, digital rights groups remain staunchly opposed to the broader concept of site-blocking. Public Knowledge, an advocacy group that also opposes the competing ACPA bill, has strongly criticized the DEFEND IP Act.
"For the second time in as many weeks, rightsholders have convinced Congress to build out an expansive infrastructure for censorship rather than go after the root of the problem: operators of overseas piracy websites," Public Knowledge wrote in response to the proposal.
The group also warned of the technical consequences of the bill's DNS scope, adding: "Let us repeat: Applying blocking orders to global DNS resolvers causes global blocks."
With the current congressional term ending in January, time is running out for either proposal to become law. Both Representative Issa and Senator Tillis are leaving Congress at the end of the term, meaning neither will be around to reintroduce their respective bills next year.
For now, however, privacy-conscious internet users can breathe a sigh of relief knowing that their VPNs are excluded from this latest legislative push.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Rene Millman is a seasoned technology journalist whose work has appeared in The Guardian, the Financial Times, Computer Weekly, and IT Pro. With over two decades of experience as a reporter and editor, he specializes in making complex topics like cybersecurity, VPNs, and enterprise software accessible and engaging.

articles.title: Reddit is putting more limits on Old.Reddit.com
articles.text:
Soon, Reddit won’t let people use Old.Reddit.com unless they have used the site while logged in within the previous six months.
In July, Reddit started requiring that users be logged in to access Old Reddit. This new requirement is an effort to reduce Reddit’s biggest source of scraping and automated traffic, the company says.
Today, the social media platform announced additional upcoming restrictions on Old Reddit. A Reddit post from an employee, known as “judy-funnie” on the platform, says that “in the next few months, we’ll further limit access for logged-in users to only those who have used Old Reddit in the last six months (which covers the vast majority of all Old Reddit users).”
There is an exception for moderators, who will still be able to view Old Reddit regardless of when they last used it, as long as they are logged in.
“This helps keep Old Reddit available for the people who rely on it while reducing automated abuse,” the post says.
Today’s post claimed that forcing users to log in to use Old Reddit “helped reduce scraping and automated abuse.” But further restrictions on the site, which many longtime Reddit users prefer over regular Reddit for its look, layout, homepage feed, and familiarity, have people concerned that Reddit will shutter Old Reddit one day.
I asked Reddit if it has plans to shut down Old Reddit, and spokesperson Rosa Kim told me via email:
As [Reddit CEO Steve Huffman previously] confirmed, Reddit is continuing to work on the future of Old Reddit. This change is about limiting unauthenticated access and reducing automated abuse—not removing Old Reddit for people and moderators who rely on it. We want to preserve Old Reddit for the real people that use it, not let it be a vector for automated abuse.
Reddit’s announcement noted that the current rules permit “any logged-in account to access Old Reddit, including accounts with no prior Old Reddit use.” I asked Kim why that’s a bad thing but didn’t receive a response.

articles.title: Schnellere Dateiensuche mit KI: Mit diesem Prompt gelingt es
articles.text:
Verlorene Dokumente finden: Dieser Prompt hilft
Eingespeiste Dateien und Meeting-Notizen, aber auch Ergebnisse aus der Arbeit mit KI lassen sich mitunter nur mit langem Suchen finden. Zeit und Nerven sparst du, wenn du diese Recherche mit dem passenden Prompt abkürzt. Die Vorlage gibt es im Podcast t3n MeisterPrompter.
Prompt funktioniert nur mit freigegebenen Inhalten
Mit dem Prompt findest du neben Inhalten, die du in einem KI-Chat verwendet hast, auch Dateien, auf die ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot oder Gemini über Schnittstellen zugreifen. Das gilt etwa, bei einer Verbindung zu Google-Drive, E‑Mail-Programmen oder Organisationstools wie Asana.
Der Prompt, den du vollständig in den Shownotes der verlinkten Folge findest, fragt gezielt Personen, Zeitraum und inhaltliche Hinweise ab. Außerdem trägst du mögliche Quellen ein. Natürlich lassen sich nur freigegebene Quellen durchsuchen. Was auf deinem Laptop lokal gespeichert und nicht für die KI freigegeben ist, kannst du mit dem Prompt nicht finden.
Halluzinationen möglich, Ergebnisse immer nachprüfen
Zudem ist der Prompt als Suchhilfe gedacht. Er soll Originalquellen mit Datum verlinken und Vermutungen nur mit Kennzeichnung anzeigen.
Allerdings kann es passieren, dass Halluzinationen auftreten. Wer sich etwa grob an ein Meeting erinnert und mit dem Prompt die passenden Notizen sucht, muss trotzdem den Inhalt selbst prüfen. Das Vorhandensein einer Datei ist nur eine Hilfestellung, jeder Treffer muss geprüft werden.

articles.title: Infineon Advances USB 20 Gbps Ecosystem with PCIe Reference Design for 5-Meter Cabling and 36W Power Delivery
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
	
	
	
Infineon Advances USB 20 Gbps Ecosystem with PCIe Reference Design for 5-Meter Cabling and 36W Power Delivery
Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY), a global leader in USB semiconductor solutions, today announced a new PCI Express Gen 4 x4 add-on card reference design that addresses key barriers to USB 20 Gbps (USB 3.2 Gen 2×2) adoption. Debuting at VISION Stuttgart 2026, the industry-first standalone reference design integrates ASMedia's ASM4242 USB4 host controller with Infineon's EZ-PD CCG7 USB Power Delivery (PD) controller to support robust, high-performance connectivity for machine vision systems.
A primary focus of this release is Infineon's continued effort to expand and mature the USB 20 Gbps ecosystem. While the standard offers double the bandwidth of previous generations, widespread industrial adoption has been limited by signal integrity challenges over longer distances and complex power requirements. This new reference design directly addresses these hurdles by enabling reliable data transmission over 5-meter passive USB cables, which is important for industrial environments where cameras are often mounted far from the host PC. By demonstrating USB 20 Gbps operation over passive cabling at this length, Infineon helps reduce an integration challenge for system designers.The reference design features two USB-C ports, each supporting USB 20 Gbps data transfer and USB Power Delivery up to 36 W (supporting 5 V / 3 A and 12 V / 3 A profiles). This combination allows for the deployment of AI-based camera systems without the need for separate power supplies, simplifying cabling and improving reliability in factory and lab settings. Targeting machine vision manufacturers, industrial PC suppliers, and system integrators, this solution provides a ready-to-use platform that accelerates time-to-market for next-generation imaging applications.
Ganesh Subramaniam, Senior Vice President of Wired Connectivity Solutions at Infineon"Infineon is committed to driving the USB 20 Gbps ecosystem forward by solving the real-world challenges that have slowed its adoption in industrial markets. One of the key hurdles for machine vision applications has been maintaining signal integrity over long passive cables while delivering sufficient power to advanced sensors. This PCIe Gen 4 x4 reference design demonstrates that USB 20 Gbps is not just a high-speed data standard, but a practical, robust solution for industrial connectivity. By supporting 5-meter passive cabling and 36 W of power per port, we are empowering camera OEMs and system integrators to deploy AI-driven vision systems with confidence, knowing that the underlying connectivity infrastructure is reliable and easy to implement."

articles.title: Proton Easy Switch lets businesses move from Microsoft 365 in just days, rather than months
articles.text:
Proton Easy Switch lets businesses move from Microsoft 365 in just days, rather than months
Proton's Easy Switch now covers M365
- Proton Easy Switch now covers Microsoft 365 migrations as well as Google Workspace
- It helps admins port over emails, contacts and calendars, but not documents
- 74% of EU business leaders are worried about US tech vendors
With so many European governments and public bodies starting to opt for sovereign, open-source software options in a bid to reduce reliance on foreign tech vendors, Switzerland's Proton has expanded its Easy Switch for Business to support Microsoft 365 migrations.
Previously, Easy Switch was only available for Google Workspace customers, but now, both major US vendors are being threatened by customers potentially switching to Proton.
For M365 in particular, Proton will automatically handle migration across three main categories – emails, contacts and calendars.
Proton Easy Switch for Microsoft 365
The company explained three in four (74%) European business leaders are worried that a US tech provider could cut off their access, and with the US Cloud Act threatening digital privacy, Europe's push to go sovereign has never been greater.
Migration is designed to be pretty easy, so admins only need to choose which data to migrate, connect to the relevant M365 account and select which user accounts to transfer.
But importantly, Proton's designed the process not to be disruptive, so users can continue to use their existing Microsoft 365 accounts in the meantime. For example, they can send emails from Proton or Microsoft during the transition, meaning workers are unlikely to even know what's going on behind the scenes while admins are busy configuring the migration.
However, while the Easy Switch migration tools might help guide admins through some of the more complex elements of switching email accounts, there's no simple switch for other parts of the M365 stack, like file storage. "Every week we hear from IT leaders who thought switching email providers would take months of disruption," Chief Operating Officer Raphael Auphan explained.

articles.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, called its most powerful model yet | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google parent company Alphabet has launched Gemini 4 Argon, a new AI model built to handle a variety of tasks such as coding, research, and writing. But it’s cybersecurity that Gemini 4 Argon is supposed to have a particular knack for, according to Google.
Argon is only being rolled out to a select group of the company’s cyber partners through its Fairwind Program, Google’s security initiative. The model was trained specifically for defensive cyber work, and the company says it can “autonomously find, validate, and patch critical software vulnerabilities.”
Argon is also said to be good at coding and engineering, with the company noting that its own staff have already been using the model for their daily work, including debugging and codebase migrations. Google also touts Argon’s ability to parse visuals — whether that’s analyzing the contents of long videos or charts.
“Built to sustain deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows, Argon is fundamentally changing the way we work and build at Google,” the company said in a blog post Wednesday.
Top AI labs have rushed to release increasingly powerful models, attempting to outdo each other even as those very same firms warn that AI could spin out of control. Not long ago, OpenAI released Astra — which it hailed as its best model yet. Earlier this year, Anthropic’s Fable was also released with similar rhetoric from the company.
Firms have done their best to market their services as superior to their competitors. In its blog, Google claims that Argon scored significantly higher than OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Fable and Opus models across a variety of AI benchmarks. It cites Vals — an increasingly popular AI benchmarking startup — to show that Argon is currently the leading model on the company’s AI model index.
Once considered “behind” in the AI race, Google has recently enjoyed success with Gemini. The company announced in August that its app had over a billion users per month, a metric that makes it competitive with OpenAI, which also recently announced that ChatGPT had reached a billion monthly users.

articles.title: Manufacturing Intelligence: Turning EDA Data into Trusted Action - EE Times
articles.text:
Better hardware enables better software. Better software enables better hardware. The semiconductor industry operates inside this accelerating feedback loop, generating unprecedented volumes of simulation results, metrology data, and manufacturing evidence. Yet as information becomes abundant, the industry’s bottleneck is shifting from information generation to decision-making.
The next competitive advantage will not come from generating more information. It will come from learning what matters and acting on it faster. This requires a new discipline: Manufacturing Intelligence.
Beyond information: The new bottleneck
For most of the history of semiconductor manufacturing, progress depended on our ability to generate better information. When a problem became difficult, we built a better model or a more sensitive metrology system. That effort succeeded. Today, we can simulate devices before they exist and collect fab measurements at an unimaginable scale.
However, yield does not improve simply because data exists. Manufacturing outcomes improve only when information changes a decision. Manufacturing Intelligence is the systematic conversion of physical understanding and manufacturing observations into trusted interventions that improve outcomes.
Electronic design automation (EDA) occupies a uniquely strategic position in this system. Most software benefits from better hardware. EDA also helps create better hardware, which then supports the next generation of EDA software. It participates in both directions of the hardware-software feedback loop and helps determine how quickly the underlying computing platform can evolve.
From prediction to intervention
Historically, simulation, metrology and optimization were treated as separate silos. Complexity is eroding those boundaries. As process windows narrow, prediction and observation can no longer operate as independent activities.
The distinction between information and action explains why some technologies create disproportionate value. A simulation does not change a process; a measurement does not improve a device. Even an accurate prediction creates no value until someone changes something in response.
Computational lithography provides a mature blueprint. Optical proximity correction (OPC) and inverse lithography (ILT) sit at the intersection of physical understanding, manufacturing observation and corrective action. The output is not another report; it is an intervention in the manufacturing process, applied across full-chip designs at production scale. The purpose of intelligence is not prediction. It is informed action.
Physics and measurement: A single conversation
The economic value of a measurement depends on its ability to improve a model, while the value of a model depends on how effectively it explains measurements. Neither domain is sufficient alone. A purely physics-based approach encounters material and process uncertainties that are difficult to model completely. A purely measurement-driven approach observes what happened but cannot necessarily explain why or predict what happens next.
Manufacturing Intelligence emerges from the interaction between these perspectives (figure 1). Simulation organizes exploration by identifying sensitivities and directing attention; metrology grounds the models in reality. Computational metrology and manufacturing inspection and review systems extend that relationship by converting contours, images, defects, and process-variation trends into evidence within a larger representation combining physical models, manufacturing history, and engineering knowledge. Measurement no longer stands apart from modeling. Each improves the other.
The rules of industrial AI
In semiconductor manufacturing, machine learning operates under different rules than in consumer applications.
First, Manufacturing Intelligence remains accountable to physics. The objective is not to produce a plausible answer, but one consistent with physical reality. Statistical intelligence cannot be permitted to invent a reality that the physical system does not support.
Second, manufacturing requires stability. While a chatbot can answer the same question differently tomorrow, a production flow represents years of validated engineering decisions. New information should extend existing knowledge, not casually rewrite it. Variation that is harmless in a consumer application, whether introduced by retraining, numerical precision or another optimization path, is unacceptable in a qualified production flow.
Monotonic Machine Learning (MML) technology provides one solution. Rather than permitting a system to discover any relationship supported by a training set, monotonic approaches preserve specified engineering knowledge. New evidence refines understanding without permitting physically implausible reversals. Manufacturing Intelligence must learn like a high-performing engineering organization: accumulating knowledge, maintaining traceability and avoiding “institutional amnesia” whenever a new dataset arrives.
The speed of trust
As analytical bottlenecks become less severe, the challenge shifts toward coordinating action. Foundries, equipment vendors, EDA suppliers and design teams possess different pieces of the evidence. Faster technical analysis exposes institutional friction: a system can identify an intervention in minutes while the organization requires months to validate the model, protect intellectual property and authorize a production change.
The companies that benefit most will not necessarily be those with the largest datasets or the most compute. They will be the organizations that establish confidence and convert decisions into action with the least friction. EDA, TCAD and computational metrology are not simply separate tool categories. They are mechanisms through which engineering organizations create, validate and act upon knowledge.
The next competitive advantage
The semiconductor industry has spent decades building extraordinary capabilities for generating information. Those capabilities remain essential, but they are no longer sufficient.
Competitive advantage now rests on the ability to combine physics, measurement and accumulated engineering knowledge into decisions that can be trusted. Manufacturing Intelligence is a distinct discipline because its purpose is neither to generate information nor to automate judgment. It transforms understanding into effective action.
As the hardware-software feedback loop accelerates, the bottleneck moves again. It is no longer our ability to simulate, measure or generate evidence. It is our ability to trust that evidence enough to act. The organizations that resolve that bottleneck will influence the overall pace of technological progress.

articles.title: 7 Books that help you make smarter decisions in life
articles.text:
7 Books that help you make smarter decisions in life
Discover seven insightful books that can help you make smarter decisions & navigate life's challenges with greater confidence.
Every day, we make decisions that shape our lives.
Some are small and forgettable, while others influence our careers, relationships, finances, and personal growth. Yet making good decisions is rarely easy. Emotions, biases, uncertainty, and outside pressures often cloud our judgment, causing us to act impulsively or overlook important information.
Fortunately, some of the world's most insightful thinkers have explored how people make choices and how those choices can improve.
The books on this list offer practical lessons on critical thinking, psychology, habits, and decision-making. Whether you're facing a major life change or simply want to think more clearly, these books can help you make smarter decisions.
1. Thinking, Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman
Nobel Prize-winning psychologist Daniel Kahneman explains the two systems that drive human thinking. One is fast, intuitive, and emotional, while the other is slow, analytical, and deliberate.
The book reveals common cognitive biases that influence decisions without us realising it.
By understanding these mental shortcuts, readers can become more aware of errors in judgment and make more thoughtful choices.
2. Decisive by Chip Heath and Dan Heath
Written specifically about decision-making, Decisive offers a practical framework for making better choices.
The Heath brothers explain why people often fall into predictable decision traps and provide strategies for avoiding them. From widening options to testing assumptions, the book offers actionable tools that can be applied in everyday life.
3. The Psychology of Money by Morgan Housel
Although focused on money, this book contains lessons that extend far beyond finance.
Morgan Housel explores how emotions, experiences, and personal biases influence decision-making. His stories demonstrate that success often depends less on intelligence and more on behaviour, patience, and long-term thinking.
4. The Almanack of Naval Ravikant by Eric Jorgenson
This collection of ideas from entrepreneur and investor Naval Ravikant covers wealth, happiness, learning, and decision-making.
Naval emphasises independent thinking, leverage, and long-term perspectives. His reflections encourage readers to focus on what truly matters and avoid making decisions based solely on social expectations or short-term rewards.
5. The Art of Thinking Clearly by Rolf Dobelli
Rolf Dobelli examines dozens of cognitive biases that influence everyday decisions.
Through short, engaging chapters, the book explains why people often misjudge risks, follow the crowd, or become overconfident in their beliefs. Understanding these biases can help readers make more rational and informed choices.
6. Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman
Many decisions become difficult because people feel pressured to do everything at once. Oliver Burkeman offers a refreshing perspective by reminding readers that time is limited.
The book encourages prioritising what matters most rather than constantly chasing productivity. It provides valuable insights into making decisions that align with personal values and long-term goals.
7. How We Change by Katy Milkman
Behavioural scientist Katy Milkman explores why people struggle to make decisions that support their goals and what can be done about it.
Drawing from psychology and real-world examples, she explains how habits are formed, why motivation fluctuates, and how small adjustments can lead to lasting change. The book is particularly useful for anyone trying to make better decisions consistently.
Final thoughts
Smart decisions are rarely the result of luck. They come from understanding how we think, recognising our biases, considering long-term consequences, and learning from experience.
The books on this list approach decision-making from different angles, but they all share a common goal: helping readers think more clearly and choose more wisely.
Whether you're making decisions about your career, finances, relationships, or personal growth, these books offer valuable insights that can help you navigate life with greater confidence and clarity.

articles.title: Russian state hackers use new RedFlick technique to push malware
articles.text:
The Russian state actor Star Blizzard has been using a new malware installation tactic dubbed “RedFlick” to deploy its signature CosmicPulse backdoor.
Although the tactic is not a new cybersecurity technique, it is a new delivery approach for the threat actor, allowing it to further automate attacks and reduce victim interaction.
Microsoft researchers say that Star Blizzard expanded its phishing operations and streamlined malware delivery in 2026.
Star Blizzard, active since 2017, is known for exploring new payload delivery avenues like ClickFix or WhatsApp, and for continually developing and deploying new malware families.
New RedFlick technique
RedFlick attacks begin with a phishing email, such as an invitation, followed by a second message containing a password-protected ZIP or RAR archive.
The archive contains a VHDX virtual disk with an LNK file disguised as a PDF. When the file is opened, it launches a command in a hidden window while displaying a decoy PDF to the victim.
The commands download and run an MSI installer that creates three scheduled tasks posing as legitimate maintenance components, each with a specific purpose:
- Internet Quality Test Connection: sends the computer/network name and username to the attackers and can execute a remote DLL.
- Network Configuration Manager: prepares Windows’ WebDAV functionality so remote web resources can be accessed through file-style paths.
- System Health Monitor: uses control.exe to execute a remotely hosted next-stage payload.
Since the new method uses multiple scheduled tasks with distinct roles, it helps the attacker evade detection at different stages of the attack.
The next-stage payload is a downloader known as NOROBOT and BAITSWITCH, delivered in the form of a Control Panel applet (.cpl). Its purpose is to fetch and execute the CosmicPulse backdoor.
BAITSWITCH downloads two ZIP archives, one of them containing the Python 3.8 64-bit package and a Python file acting as a bootstrapper for CosmicPulse.
"The bootstrapper reads the encrypted key from the registry, recovers it using an embedded key in AES-ECB mode, and then uses the recovered key to decode the CosmicPulse payload," Microsoft says.
Microsoft notes that the backdoor’s capabilities in the observed attacks remain the same as described in a report from Google in October 2025, including the execution of attacker-supplied Python code to download and run files or retrieve documents from infected systems.
From a practical perspective, RedFlick only requires the victim to open the malicious shortcut file to trigger an automated infection chain, whereas in the ClickFix attacks, Star Blizzard required victims to take multiple manual actions.
Microsoft's report provides technical analysis of the infection chain and the components used in the attacks.
The company says that since the beginning of the year, it has observed at least 13 distinct large-scale phishing campaigns impacting more than 100 organizations, primarily in the United States and the United Kingdom.
“The RedFlick campaigns have targeted Ukrainian individuals and institutions, as well as international NGOs, think tanks, governments, and financial institutions that have supported Ukraine politically or financially,” the researchers say.
Despite changing its tactics, techniques, and procedures, StarBlizzard continues to target users by impersonating trusted contacts or organizations, and still relies on free email providers to deliver phishing messages.
Microsoft recommends that companies use phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, email protection, and independently verify suspicious messages through established contact details.
Additionally, using an endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions in block mode should prevent infections by blocking malicious artifacts even if they are not caught by the antivirus agent.

articles.title: Précommander l’iPhone Duo : Apple réactive son option indispensable pour esquiver la rupture de stock
articles.text:
Précommander l’iPhone Duo : Apple réactive son option indispensable pour esquiver la rupture de stock
Face aux faibles stocks attendus pour l’iPhone Duo, Apple activera une méthode éprouvée depuis des générations pour préparer votre panier avant le lancement officiel des précommandes.
Comme c’est le cas à chaque grand lancement de rentrée, Apple propose une option pour être dans les starting-blocks à l’ouverture des précommandes. L’iPhone Duo n’y échappe pas, permettant de configurer son modèle et de renseigner ses informations personnelles en amont pour n’avoir plus qu’à valider l’achat d’un simple clic le jour J. Une fonction qui pourrait s’avérer plus qu’utile face aux stocks limités de la firme à la pomme pour le lancement de son premier modèle pliant.
L’astuce d’Apple pour précommander rapidement l’iPhone Duo
La sortie du premier smartphone pliant d’Apple s’avère particulièrement complexe. Selon les révélations de Jiemian News, Foxconn peinait mi-septembre à franchir les 60 % de rendement d’assemblage, freiné par le cahier des charges de la firme de Cupertino. D’après les estimations du média, il faudrait entre six mois et un an pour stabiliser la chaîne de production.
De son côté, Samsung Display aurait essuyé des déconvenues sur la charnière et les écrans pliables, ayant ralenti les livraisons de composants et provoqué des révisions matérielles en cours de route. D’autre part, la puce A20 Pro de l’iPhone Duo et des iPhone 18 Pro aurait du mal à sortir d’usine, bloquée par la pénurie de mémoire vive.
Alors que la marque vise 6 à 8 millions d’unités d’ici fin 2026, l’offre serait particulièrement limitée au lancement. Pour maximiser vos chances lors des précommandes, Apple relance son option Préparez-vous sur l’application Apple Store et son site officiel. Du lundi 12 au jeudi 15 octobre, les acheteurs pourront y préparer leur commande : finition, capacité de stockage, informations personnelles et moyen de paiement. Valider ces choix à l’avance élimine ainsi toute perte de temps le moment venu.
Le vendredi 16 octobre à 14 heures tapantes, soit dès l’ouverture des précommandes, un simple clic sur le bouton de commande suffira pour payer et conclure l’achat. Face à une forte demande anticipée et à une disponibilité restreinte, il s’agit de la meilleure façon de mettre la main sur l’iPhone Duo dès sa sortie, le vendredi 23 octobre. Les moins rapides devraient quant à eux se retrouver avec des délais de livraison repoussés de plusieurs semaines.

articles.title: Windows 11 26H2 é oficial: veja o que muda e como instalar • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Windows 11 26H2 é oficial: veja o que muda e como instalar
Atualização 26H2 começou a ser liberada pela Microsoft para computadores com Windows 11 24H2 ou 25H2.
A Microsoft está encerrando o mês de setembro com o lançamento oficial da versão 26H2 do Windows 11. A novidade não é exatamente… nova. Isso porque o pacote traz uma série de recursos que foram distribuídos em atualizações anteriores. Mesmo assim, a sua implementação é importante. Veja por que a seguir.
Também chamada de Windows 11 2026 Update, a versão 26H2 contém um conjunto de atualizações que corrigem falhas, ajustam componentes e adicionam recursos ao sistema operacional. Entre esses recursos estão:
Você pode simplesmente esperar a atualização ser liberada para a sua máquina. O pacote 26H2 será oferecido automaticamente em PCs com Windows 11 24H2 ou 25H2. Contudo, esse processo é gradual, o que significa que pode demorar um pouco para o seu PC ser contemplado.
Para descobrir se o Windows 11 26H2 já está disponível para você, vá em Configurações / Windows Update / Verificar se há atualizações. Se não estiver, marcar a opção “Obtenha as atualizações mais recentes assim que elas estiverem disponíveis” pode acelerar o procedimento.
Um detalhe interessante é que esta não é, necessariamente, uma atualização “pesada”. Como já dito, muitos dos recursos oferecidos pela versão 26H2 foram liberados em atualizações anteriores.
Por conta disso, o pacote a ser baixado só incluirá os recursos que ainda não existem no computador de destino, bem como ativará aqueles que vieram das atualizações anteriores, mas não estavam habilitados.
Também há um detalhe curioso: se você tiver a versão 26H1 do Windows 11, o pacote 26H2 não será oferecido, pelo menos não de imediato. A razão disso é que o Windows 26H1 tem componentes internos diferentes em relação às versões 24H2, 25H2 e, agora, 26H2. Essa diferença existe porque o pacote 26H1 tem como foco máquinas que utilizam determinados chips com arquitetura Arm.
Você pode descobrir a versão do seu Windows 11 digitando o comando “winver” no campo de busca da Barra de Tarefas ou do Menu Iniciar.
