articles.title: The Disney protests were a wake-up call about the risks of streaming mergers
articles.text:
There was a call to boycott Disney last fall. The owner of the ABC network had taken Jimmy Kimmel Live! off the air over comments Kimmel made about responses to Charlie Kirk’s murder, sending free speech proponents into a frenzy.
Those free speech proponents include me, who, as a reporter, has clear stakes in protecting that right. Although I was on board with halting support for a company I felt had acted wrongfully, truly boycotting Disney proved harder than I expected.
Disney’s ubiquity
Canceling Disney+ was simple but threw a hefty wrench into my evening routine. I tend to end many weekdays laughing at comforting sitcom reruns and adult animation. I usually associate Disney with princesses, kids’ movies, and, more recently, comic heroes. But Disney also owns Hulu, which exclusively streamed many of my favorite shows for unwinding at the time, like American Dad, Futurama, Living Single, Fresh Off the Boat, and It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia.
Completely boycotting Disney also meant I couldn’t watch the broadcast channels where some of these shows originated, like ABC and FX. It also limited my guilty-pleasure options, since A&E, History, and Lifetime were all partially owned by Disney (Disney has since sold its stake in those networks to Hearst), as were some video games. I had to miss some sporting events, too, since Disney owns all ESPN channels and streaming services.
Weekends often involve streaming a science-fiction or action movie my partner picked out. Due to the protests, though, I had to veto streaming content from some of his favorite franchises, including Avatar, Alien, Predator, and Die Hard.
This was all probably a reminder that I should take a break from the TV and go outside. For argument’s sake, though, I must point out that if I had wanted to spend my time outdoors at a theme park, my options would also have been limited somewhat.
A year later, as Jimmy Kimmel Live! airs its 25th season, the difficulties I faced trying to avoid Disney still perturb me.
There was a time when protesting ABC’s decision would have simply meant not watching ABC. After years of media conglomeration, however, protesting ABC can now mean boycotting a massive entity controlling many of my most prominent forms of entertainment—streaming, broadcast TV, comedies, science fiction, and video games—and even children’s programming.
It has been reported that the boycott financially impacted Disney and put pressure on the company to get Kimmel back on.
But mergers and acquisitions (M&As) are intensifying in the streaming age and consolidating power under fewer owners. And, as we’ve seen before, when there are fewer streaming owners, it can be even harder to end your business with a streaming provider you no longer want to support and for smaller voices to speak up.
Disney settled an antitrust lawsuit through acquisition
Fubo’s previous row with Disney illustrates how a bigger company can summarily silence protests.
The sports-centric streaming service sued Disney, Fox Corporation, and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) in February 2024 over the companies’ plans to launch a sports streaming app together. Fubo accused the companies of “antitrust” behavior. Fubo alleged that Disney forced it to spend millions annually on unwanted, non-sports content to get the sports programming that Fubo wanted. Disney and Fox, the complaint said, had “monopoly power in the sports programming market.” Fubo’s CEO, David Gandler, said at the time that the companies “create higher pricing for subscribers and cheat consumers from deserved choice.” Disney declined to answer the questions I sent it at the time.
In January 2025, Disney effectively made the antitrust suit go away by buying Fubo. I asked Fubo about the surprising settlement at the time and received a statement arguing that the merger would bring customers “more choice” by enabling “Fubo to create a new Sports and Broadcast service and other genre-based content packages.” The statement noted that Fubo was now perfectly fine with Disney, Fox, and WBD launching a sports app (the app was still canceled in January 2025). A smaller company that was previously rearing up to fight consolidation in sports streaming merged with one of the companies it accused of stifling competition and driving up prices.
In July, Fubo increased monthly subscription prices by $15 after it restored some of the channels it lost during a contract dispute with NBCUniversal. During the dispute, Fubo lowered its prices. After Fubo reached a deal with NBCUniversal, it ended up charging more for subscriptions than it did before the dispute, while including fewer NBCU channels than before.
As a sports-focused streaming service, the most relevant channels that Fubo got back were NBC affiliates, regional sports channels, NBC News NOW, NBC Sports Network, Telemundo, and Universo. However, the higher prices are also representative of the non-sports channels that Fubo restored: Brazo, Cozi, and True CRMZ.
“The rising cost of bringing you the programming you enjoy means that, unfortunately, we need to pass some of these increases on to you,” Fubo said in an email to subscribers about the price hikes.
Streaming’s merger-heavy future
Experts that I’ve spoken with over the past couple of years have consistently predicted more streaming mergers. Streaming services launched at unsustainably low prices aimed at growing subscriptions. Years later, streaming companies face increasing pressure to reach profitability and, subsequently, grow streaming profits. This isn’t easy for many services, and some will opt for mergers to stay in business or become more financially successful.
Mergers also help streaming companies manage content costs and build larger libraries that can attract more customers and advertisers.
But as I learned during the Disney protests, it’s difficult to limit a company’s presence in your home when the company owns so much. The streaming industry is increasingly moving toward that sort of suffocating consolidation.
WBD and Skydance Paramount are planning a controversial union that will put HBO Max, Discovery+, CNN, and Paramount+ under one owner. A true boycott against that merged company would mean avoiding the next Batman movie, The Challenge’s latest seasons, CNN’s political analysis, and CBS local news. It would also hinder free streaming options by taking Pluto TV off the table.
Merging some of the services could address complaints about today’s content fragmentation that forces streaming customers to sign up for numerous services to watch what they want. But that could easily lead to higher subscription fees, due to higher content costs, larger libraries, and/or less competition.
I have similar concerns about Fox’s plans to buy Roku. With both companies currently owning separate free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) services (Tubi and The Roku Channel, respectively), a merger could lead to fewer FAST options.
Further, potentially unfavorable strategies, such as around ad loads, content availability, or conservative programming, could theoretically spread to The Roku Channel under Fox ownership.
Other options
M&As are one response to the various economic challenges facing streaming companies. But there are other things they can do to increase revenue that would also benefit customers.
One is to license content to other platforms more often. This could help services generate additional revenue while addressing content fragmentation. Small, niche services, however, have to walk a fine line when it comes to sharing the titles that make their services stand out to current and potential subscribers.
Offering discounts if users link their streaming subscription to another subscription, like for home Internet or mobile service, is said to help streaming companies reduce cancellations. Streaming services can extract more value from this strategy if they target younger audiences by offering more bundles with services like music, gaming, or food delivery services.
“[T]he current bundles offered by media companies may miss the mark, as younger subscribers look toward broader cross-category ecosystems. Put simply: Bundles have become mainstream, but they still should keep pace with consumer expectations that have become increasingly personal,” Deloitte said in an August blog post.
Streaming services can also get better at helping subscribers with content discovery, which could help services drive subscriptions. In Gracenote’s 2025 State of Play survey of 3,000 “consumers” in the US, Brazil, France, Germany, Mexico, and the United Kingdom, 49 percent of respondents said they “are willing to cancel a service based on difficulty finding what to watch.”
Some services are already leveraging generative AI chatbots and other technologies to help users find new content. However, the challenge of creating reliable content discovery that people enjoy using extends beyond streaming services, including to smart TV operating system owners, marketers, and AI companies.
As streaming mergers steam ahead, customers are at risk of higher prices and less diversity in the ownership of countless beloved shows, movies, games, books, and franchises.
Today, fully boycotting Disney means boycotting numerous streaming services, networks, franchises, and theme parks. With more streaming services uniting, it will become harder to protest and avoid services that make disagreeable decisions, like raising prices or pulling a show because of the host’s expressed views.
Scharon is a Senior Technology Reporter at Ars Technica writing news, reviews, and analysis on consumer gadgets and services. She's been reporting on technology for over 10 years, with bylines at Tom’s Hardware, Channelnomics, and CRN UK.

articles.title: Trump tells federal agencies to use the term 'Super Intelligence ' instead of artificial intelligence — President insists that AI is only suffering from a branding problem
articles.text:
Trump tells federal agencies to use the term 'Super Intelligence ' instead of artificial intelligence — President insists that AI is only suffering from a branding problem
Will changing what we call the technology address the underlying issues?
President Donald Trump signed a directive telling federal agencies to start calling AI “Super Intelligence” after hosting a lunch at the White House with industry leaders discussing the technology and the risks that it carried. According to the executive order, the term artificial intelligence was born in the United States 70 years ago, and the capabilities achieved by AI today are much more advanced than what the original innovators envisioned. Because of this, he saw fit to have the federal government call that technology by the new term that he coined instead of referring to it as “artificial intelligence.”
“The terminology used by the Federal Government should reflect the transformative capabilities of these technologies and the limitless opportunities they create for the American people. Accordingly, the term ‘Super Intelligence’ more appropriately captures the promise, potential, and rapidly advancing capabilities of these technologies,” the order said. “It is therefore the policy of my Administration that, to the maximum extent permitted by law, the executive branch shall use the terms ‘Super Intelligence’ and ‘SI’ in place of ‘Artificial Intelligence’ and ‘AI’ and will not acknowledge the usage of ‘Artificial Intelligence’ and ‘AI’ in any applicable setting.”
Trump believes that AI is only suffering from a branding issue, just as a recent poll showed that 79% of Americans think that AI safety is more important than having frontier models, while 73% said they will push back against the construction of an AI data center in the neighborhood. Opposition against the AI infrastructure build-out has been increasing throughout 2026, with protests primarily driven by concerns about local utility hikes and noise pollution. Aside from that, there have also been numerous security incidents involving AI going rogue, to the point that Anthropic listed “existential risk to humanity” as one of its risk factors in its IPO prospectus. But even though Trump changes what he and the rest of the federal government call AI, it still does not address all those concerns.
Using the term “Super Intelligence” could also bring some confusion, as it’s the term that scientists use for a level of AI that has achieved cognitive superiority to humans and are better at them in every conceivable task. While the latest frontier models are extremely good at doing particular actions, they still are nowhere near the level of superintelligence described by experts. While the White House wants to win the AI race with China and has been pushing hard for the development of this technology, some industry leaders and politicians are concerned that an artificial superintelligence could get out of control and end humanity. Senator Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), alongside Senator Greg Cezar (D-Texas), have even proposed a bill banning its development, with the included penalty at par with the illegal development of nuclear weapons.
Still, it seems that some of the executives of the biggest AI tech companies are following the President’s lead, with Elon Musk adopting the term while in Trump’s presence. As for the President, he told reporters that the change has officially been made “by the biggest, the smartest, the greatest people anywhere in the world at this,” likely referring to the AI executives who attended the lunch at the White House. “We’re using the word super because the other word is a fake word.”
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.

articles.title: Instagram: So holst du 2026 das Maximum aus deinen Reels heraus
articles.text:
Offizieller Guide von Instagram: So holst du 2026 das Maximum aus deinen Reels heraus
Mal eben ein Reel posten? Das geht zwar schnell, doch zwischen Templates, Musik, Text, Untertiteln, Effekten, Collabs und zahlreichen Bearbeitungsoptionen ist inzwischen einiges möglich. Damit Creator dabei den Überblick behalten, hat Instagram jetzt einen umfangreichen neuen Guide veröffentlicht, der Schritt für Schritt durch die Erstellung von Reels führt.
In diesem Guide erklärt die Plattform nicht nur die Basics, sondern liefert auch Tipps zur Länge, Bearbeitung und Veröffentlichung von Reels. Dabei geht es von den Grundlagen über Editing und Audio bis hin zu Remix und Collab. Das sind die wichtigsten Punkte im Überblick.
Was sind Instagram-Reels?
Wer Instagram öffnet, kommt an Reels kaum noch vorbei. Das Kurzvideoformat, das einst als Antwort auf Tiktok gestartet ist, gehört inzwischen zu den wichtigsten Formaten der Plattform. Reels lassen sich mit Musik, Audio, Effekten, Text und weiteren kreativen Elementen gestalten. Anders als Stories verschwinden sie nicht nach 24 Stunden, sondern bleiben dauerhaft im Profil sichtbar.
Reels sollen vor allem eines: entdeckt werden. Instagram spielt sie nicht nur im Feed und Reels-Tab aus, sondern kann sie über Explore und Empfehlungen auch Usern zeigen, die einem Account noch nicht folgen. Damit können Creator ihre Reichweite über die bestehende Community hinaus ausbauen. Dabei zählen allerdings nicht nur Views: Instagram priorisiert bei Reels inzwischen andere Signale und gewichtet Interaktionen wie Shares und Saves stärker.
Wie lang dürfen Instagram-Reels sein?
Drei Sekunden oder drei Minuten? Beides geht. Instagram zufolge sollten Reels zwischen drei Sekunden und drei Minuten lang sein. Für besonders kurze Trends und Transitions empfiehlt sich demnach eine Länge von drei bis 15 Sekunden. Tutorials, „Ein Tag in meinem Leben“-Clips und andere kreative Formate passen laut Instagram häufig in den Bereich zwischen 15 und 60 Sekunden. Bis zu drei Minuten bieten wiederum mehr Raum für längeres Storytelling, Walkthroughs oder detaillierte Anleitungen.
Wenn du die Reels-Kamera öffnest, werden dir unten im Bildschirm verschiedene Optionen für die Dauer angezeigt. Per Tap kannst du die maximale Länge auswählen, bevor du mit der Aufnahme startest.
Mindestens genauso wichtig wie die Länge ist allerdings, wie lange User tatsächlich dranbleiben. Die Instagram-Reels-Retention zeigt, an welchen Stellen Zuschauer:innen abspringen und wie viele bis zum Ende weiterschauen. Instagram gibt Einsteiger:innen außerdem einen einfachen Tipp:
Wenn du Reels zum ersten Mal ausprobierst, fang am besten mit einem 15-sekündigen Reel an. Kürzere Videos sind einfacher zu bearbeiten und halten die Aufmerksamkeit der Betrachter*innen länger. Sobald du mit den Tools vertraut bist, kannst du auch längere Videos machen.
So erstellst du dein erstes Reel
Ein neues Reel ist in wenigen Schritten erstellt. Über das Pluszeichen kannst du entweder direkt aufnehmen oder Fotos und Videos aus deiner Galerie hochladen. Mehrere Clips lassen sich miteinander kombinieren und anschließend im Editor mit Musik, Text, Effekten und Stickern versehen. Vor der Veröffentlichung kannst du unter anderem Caption, Cover und Zielgruppe festlegen.
Wer schneller loslegen möchte oder einen kreativen Impuls sucht, kann Reels-Vorlagen nutzen. Dabei setzt du deine eigenen Clips in eine bestehende Vorlage ein, während Timing und Übergänge schon vorgegeben sind. Mit First Draft erstellt Instagram dir aus einem Video in Sekunden eine erste geschnittene Version, die du nur noch anpassen musst. Creative Director des Videos bleibst du.
Deine Reels wie ein Profi bearbeiten
Nach der Aufnahme geht es ans Feintuning. Direkt im Reels-Editor kannst du Musik und Voiceovers hinzufügen, Texte und Effekte einbauen und festlegen, wann einzelne Elemente im Video erscheinen. Für aufwendigere Bearbeitungen bietet Instagram zusätzlich die eigene Videobearbeitungs-App Edits. Dort kannst du deine Clips auf einer detaillierteren Timeline schneiden, mit mehreren Audiospuren arbeiten und einzelne Frames präziser bearbeiten.
Meta baut Edits laufend aus. Seit diesem Jahr können Creator die CapCut-Alternative von Meta unter anderem nutzen, um bis zu drei Reels miteinander zu vergleichen, ihre Performance anhand von Views, Watchtime und neuen Followern auszuwerten und mit detaillierteren Audience Insights zu arbeiten. Beim Editing kamen außerdem Funktionen wie Keyframes, zusätzliche Effekte, Voice Enhance und neue Textoptionen hinzu.
Musik und Audio hinzufügen
Der richtige Sound kann einem Reel erst den richtigen Vibe geben. Instagram ermöglicht es, im Editor Songs zu suchen, aktuelle Titel und Playlists zu durchstöbern und genau den Ausschnitt auszuwählen, der im Reel zu hören sein soll. Musik und Originalaudio lassen sich anschließend separat in der Lautstärke anpassen.
So wählst du Musik aus:
- Tippe oben im Bearbeitungsbildschirm auf das Musiknotensymbol.
- Suche nach einem Song oder stöbere durch aktuelle Titel und Playlists.
- Wähle den gewünschten Titel und anschließend über die Audiowellenform den passenden Ausschnitt aus.
- Passe an, wie laut Musik und Originalaudio jeweils sein sollen.
Nach der Aufnahme kannst du außerdem über das Mikrofonsymbol ein Voiceover aufnehmen, etwa für Tutorials, Erklärungen oder Storytelling.
Über Edits lassen sich darüber hinaus eigene Sounds für Reels importieren und speichern. Dazu kommen automatisches Lautstärke-Matching und 200 neue Sound-Effekte. Creator können außerdem lizenzfreie Musik nutzen und Voice-Effekte einsetzen.
Text-Overlays hinzufügen
Ein starker Hook muss nicht immer gesprochen werden. Text-Overlays lassen sich frei auf dem Bildschirm platzieren und zeitlich so steuern, dass sie nur an bestimmten Stellen im Reel erscheinen. So kannst du Kontext ergänzen, Aussagen hervorheben oder direkt im ersten Frame Aufmerksamkeit erzeugen.
Für ein Text-Overlay tippst du im Bearbeitungsbildschirm auf „Aa“, gibst deinen Text ein und passt Schriftart, Farbe, Größe und Position an. Über die Timeline bestimmst du anschließend, wann er erscheint und wieder verschwindet. Mehrere Textebenen lassen sich dabei unabhängig voneinander timen, etwa für eine Frage im ersten Frame und die Antwort einige Sekunden später.
Instagrams Tipp: Ein prägnanter Text im ersten Frame kann ähnlich wichtig sein wie das Cover des Reels. Auch Edits bietet dafür zunehmend mehr Optionen, darunter zahlreiche Texteffekte und zusätzliche Fonts.
Bildunterschriften und Untertitel hinzufügen
Text-Overlays und Untertitel erfüllen unterschiedliche Aufgaben. Während du Overlays selbst platzierst und gestaltest, lässt sich das gesprochene Audio eines Reels mit automatischen Untertiteln transkribieren und synchron einblenden. Dadurch werden Inhalte auch für Menschen leichter zugänglich, die Videos ohne Ton ansehen oder gehörlos beziehungsweise schwerhörig sind.
Für automatische Untertitel öffnest du nach der Aufnahme die Sticker-Auswahl und wählst den Untertitel-Sticker. Instagram transkribiert anschließend das Audio. Den erzeugten Text kannst du korrigieren sowie Schriftart, Farbe, Hintergrund und Position anpassen.
Instagram empfiehlt, Untertitel und Text-Overlays nicht als Alternativen zu betrachten: Während Overlays einzelne Aussagen hervorheben können, machen Untertitel das komplette gesprochene Audio sichtbar. Mit Auto-Highlight-Captions kann Edits außerdem einzelne Wörter innerhalb der Untertitel automatisch hervorheben.
AR-Effekte und Filter
Effekte können entweder den gesamten Look eines Reels oder nur einzelne Clips verändern. Über das Funkelnsymbol kannst du vor der Aufnahme oder im Editor durch verschiedene Kategorien stöbern, Effekte testen und Favoriten über das Lesezeichensymbol speichern. Soll nur ein einzelner Clip verändert werden, wählst du diesen in der Timeline aus und wendest den Effekt dort an.
In Edits gehen die Möglichkeiten noch weiter: Mit Opacity Blending lassen sich Text, Sticker und Overlays stärker mit dem Videomaterial verschmelzen. Außerdem kann Restyle Videos per Prompt in unterschiedliche Looks und Stilrichtungen verwandeln.
Tempo, Timer und Transitions richtig nutzen
Für saubere Transitions oder Zeitraffer braucht es nicht zwangsläufig zusätzliche Tools. Instagram bietet dafür mehrere Aufnahmehilfen:
- Tempo: Die Aufnahme lässt sich beispielsweise auf 0,5-fache Geschwindigkeit verlangsamen oder auf zweifache beziehungsweise dreifache Geschwindigkeit beschleunigen.
- Timer: Ein Countdown von drei oder zehn Sekunden gibt dir Zeit, dich vor der Aufnahme zu positionieren. Zusätzlich kannst du festlegen, wie lange die Aufnahme laufen soll.
- Ausrichten: Ein transparentes Overlay des letzten Frames hilft dabei, zwei Clips möglichst nahtlos miteinander zu verbinden.
Gerade das Ausrichten-Tool eignet sich für Outfit-Wechsel, Standortwechsel oder andere Transitions, bei denen die Position zwischen zwei Aufnahmen möglichst gleich bleiben soll.
Wer beim Tempo noch mehr Spielraum braucht, kann Edits nutzen. Dort lassen sich Clips bis zu hundertfach beschleunigen, etwa für Timelapse-Reels oder schnellere Trend-Cuts.
Reels im Feed und auf Explore teilen
Fertig geschnitten heißt noch nicht fertig gepostet. Vor der Veröffentlichung kannst du festlegen, wie und wo dein Reel erscheint. Dazu gehören die Caption, das Titelbild, markierte Personen und Orte sowie die Entscheidung, ob das Reel zusätzlich im regulären Feed beziehungsweise Profilraster auftauchen soll.
Instagram empfiehlt für die Caption Kontext, Fragen oder passende Hashtags. Als Titelbild kannst du einen Frame aus dem Reel auswählen oder ein eigenes Cover hochladen. Personen- und Ortsmarkierungen können außerdem helfen, das Reel zusätzlichen Usern zugänglich zu machen und bei standortbezogenen Suchen sichtbar zu werden.
Beim Cover bietet Instagram ebenfalls verschiedene Gestaltungsmöglichkeiten. So kannst du beispielsweise Text auf dem Reels-Cover platzieren, damit schon im Profil deutlich wird, worum es in deinem Video geht.
Wer die Veröffentlichung vorbereiten möchte, kann Reels außerdem im Voraus planen, jetzt auch am Desktop, und zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt automatisch posten lassen.
Remix und Collab: Reels gemeinsam erstellen
Reels müssen nicht allein entstehen. Instagram bietet dafür mit Remix und Collab zwei unterschiedliche Funktionen.
Mit Remix kannst du ein bestehendes Reel aufgreifen und daraus deinen eigenen Spin machen. Dein Video erscheint dabei zum Beispiel neben dem Original, im Splitscreen oder als Greenscreen-Version. So eignen sich Remixes besonders für Reaktionen, Duetts, Challenges oder eigene Varianten eines Trends. Dafür öffnest du das gewünschte Reel, tippst auf die drei Punkte, wählst „Dieses Reel remixen“ und anschließend dein Layout.
Mit Collab kannst du dagegen ein Reel gemeinsam mit anderen Accounts veröffentlichen und so mehrere Communities mit demselben Beitrag erreichen. Der Beitrag erscheint auf den beteiligten Profilen, während Views, Likes und Kommentare zusammenlaufen. Regulär können bis zu fünf Accounts an einem Collab-Post mitwirken; 2026 hat Instagram allerdings bereits Collab-Posts mit bis zu 16 Accounts getestet.
Praktisch für bereits veröffentlichte Inhalte: Instagram ermöglicht es inzwischen außerdem, Mitwirkende nachträglich zu einem Reel hinzuzufügen.
Reels können mehr denn je und du kannst trotzdem sofort loslegen
Reels sind gemacht für den nächsten Swipe: schnell konsumiert, schnell geteilt und mit ordentlich Potenzial für organische Reichweite. Auf der Plattform werden sie mehr als 4,5 Milliarden Mal pro Tag weitergeteilt. Umso mehr lohnt es sich, die wichtigsten Tools zu kennen, ohne sich von der Funktionsfülle erschlagen zu lassen. Mit Edits wird die Erstellung und Bearbeitung noch vielseitiger und einfacher. Und mit Instagrams neuem Guide gibt es jetzt ein aktuelles Tutorial, das Schritt für Schritt zeigt, wie es geht.
Also: Reel-Kamera öffnen, Sound oder Vorlage auswählen und einfach loslegen. Und wer dabei möglichst viel Reichweite mitnehmen möchte, sollte auch wissen, was Creator bei Reels unbedingt vermeiden sollten.
Der Artikel stammt von Larissa Ceccio aus der OnlineMarketing.de-Redaktion und wird im Rahmen einer Content-Kooperation auf t3n veröffentlicht.

articles.title: Microsoft Launches Windows 11 26H2 Update
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Microsoft Launches Windows 11 26H2 Update
Microsoft today released its latest Windows 11 26H2 update, bringing a new milestone for Windows 11 users. In this release, Microsoft is highlighting a few features that Windows 11 25H2 users have not yet experienced. These include a smarter File Explorer with new capabilities such as summarization, additional archive formats, and AI productivity enhancements. Additionally, Windows Search has been improved to prioritize searching through your files before resorting to web searches, while also handling typos and partial application names more effectively. Frequently used folders will receive automatic indexing, making them easier to find. Other optimizations include updates to Magnifier with new zoom and screen tint options, Narrator adding a Braille Viewer, and Voice gaining a wider range of voice-driven commands on Copilot+ PC. Finally, the Start menu and Taskbar now offer new customization options, positioning changes, and a smaller view option.
Interestingly, this update focuses more on resetting the support cycles that Microsoft is implementing, rather than introducing major features or overhauls. For those upgrading, the main change will be an extension of the support cycle as users transition to the 26H2 release. Starting September 29, 2026, there will be 36 months of servicing support for Enterprise and Education editions of Windows 11, version 26H2. Home and Pro editions will receive 24 months of support.Since late 2024, support and updates have been rolled out across every OS branch, with each new release cycle activating these features rather than leaving them dormant in the kernel. Enablement packages (eKB) are central to this process, as downloading an update essentially involves eKBs that activate certain functionalities. For instance, on a device running Windows 11 24H2 or 25H2, a simple eKB is needed to upgrade to the latest Windows 11 26H2 version. For older versions like 22H2 and 23H2, which are on an older servicing branch, Windows 11 26H2 is a full feature update.

articles.title: South African startup Exten AI helps non-technical founders build full-stack apps in plain language - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African startup Exten AI has developed an AI-native platform that lets entrepreneurs with no coding skills build working software applications just by describing them in everyday language.
Launched earlier this year by Luncedo Simelane, Exten AI turns natural-language prompts into production-ready apps. Unlike many “text-to-code” tools, it goes beyond the frontend, providing a robust underlying infrastructure layer for every generated application, and instantly provisioning a full backend that includes an isolated database, file storage, secure user authentication infrastructure, and the runtimes required to host and run autonomous AI agents.
“It is basically a digital tech co-founder to a non-technical entrepreneur with a great software idea, delivering a production-ready stack in under 30 minutes,” Simelane told Disrupt Africa.
Simelane taught himself coding before leaving his LLB studies to focus on software architecture full-time.
“I realised that tech infrastructure gaps were the single biggest bottleneck holding back African innovation,” he said, adding that the key gap in the market is what he calls the “plumbing problem”.
“Global text-to-code platforms primarily serve existing developers to make them code faster, or stop at creating superficial visual frontends,” he said. “Solo builders and small business merchants hit a brick wall because they don’t know how to deploy backend systems, structure relational databases, or handle security authentication. Exten AI solves this exact problem by acting as an automated technical partner.”
On competition, Simelane said: “We sit between global frontend prompt tools, which skip the database entirely, and complex enterprise low-code systems like Microsoft Power Apps, which are far too expensive and rigid for emerging market creators.”
The startup is fully bootstrapped. An early proof of concept was endorsed on Sunday Sessions by Professor Mamokgethi Phakeng, former vice-chancellor of the University of Cape Town, and Exten AI is launching a pilot at the end of September with the University of Fort Hare’s Centre of Entrepreneurship and Rapid Incubator. Student founders there will use the platform to build MVPs for their businesses.
“Demand immediately outpaced our initial server capabilities,” Simelane said. The first public release drew over 100 signups, and Exten AI moved into a closed-cohort testing phase to keep its infrastructure stable. Early users have already launched live apps, including LedgerAI for accounting automation, EduAgent for teachers’ lesson planning, and LuminaAI, a custom communication dashboard.
Exten AI uses a tiered SaaS subscription model.
“While generating and testing apps is frictionless, users pay a predictable monthly subscription once their apps go live to the public,” Simelane said. Pricing scales with server load, database storage, and AI agent usage. “Because we’ve prioritised architecture optimisation during our closed-cohort phase to perfect our user unit economics, early revenues have been minimal.”
Scaling has been the biggest challenge.
“Having dozens of users simultaneously asking an AI engine to map out, provision, and launch complex database schemas live on the cloud caused massive infrastructure queues early on,” Simelane said. “It required weeks of deep-dive architecture rewrites to isolate and stream these automated builds.”
Exten AI is now raising a ZAR1.5 million (US$90,000) investment round to scale its server layers and support thousands of concurrent builds. The startup is currently focused on South African SMEs and solo founders, but plans to expand to tech hubs and university incubators across Sub-Saharan Africa.
“Emerging markets are experiencing a severe software developer shortage alongside an explosion of young entrepreneurs who need localised digital tooling to survive and scale,” Simelane said.

articles.title: 7 Must-read books for Gandhi Jayanti that inspire change
articles.text:
7 Must-read books for Gandhi Jayanti that inspire change
Discover seven powerful books for Gandhi Jayanti that explore truth, nonviolence, self-reliance, social change, and the enduring spirit of khadi.
Every year on October 2, Gandhi Jayanti invites us to revisit the ideas that shaped one of the most influential figures in history. Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy extended far beyond India's freedom struggle. His teachings on truth, nonviolence, simplicity, self-reliance, and service continue to inspire people around the world.
One symbol closely associated with Gandhi is khadi. More than a hand-spun fabric, khadi represented self-reliance, dignity of labour, equality, and resistance to colonial rule. Gandhi believed that spinning and wearing khadi could help villages become economically independent and strengthen the spirit of swadeshi. He saw it as a pathway to self-sufficiency and social transformation.
This Gandhi Jayanti, consider picking up books that reflect these values. From Gandhi's own writings to modern works inspired by his ideas, these books offer timeless lessons on creating meaningful change.
1. The Story of My Experiments with Truth by Mahatma Gandhi
No Gandhi Jayanti reading list is complete without Gandhi's autobiography. Written with remarkable honesty, the book chronicles his journey from childhood to becoming a leader of India's freedom movement. Rather than presenting himself as a hero, Gandhi shares his mistakes, struggles, and attempts to live according to truth. The book offers a deeply personal look at how small daily choices can shape a larger purpose.
2. Hind Swaraj by Mahatma Gandhi
First published in 1909, Hind Swaraj remains one of Gandhi's most influential works. In it, he outlines his vision of self-rule, not only politically but also morally and socially. The book explores ideas such as self-reliance, ethical living, and community-centred development. Gandhi's emphasis on swadeshi and local production later became closely linked with the khadi movement and his vision of an empowered India.
3. Gandhi: An Autobiography (Illustrated Edition) by Mahatma Gandhi
For readers new to Gandhi's life and ideas, illustrated editions of his autobiography provide an accessible entry point. The visuals help bring historical events to life while preserving the power of Gandhi's words.
It is an excellent choice for young readers and anyone looking to understand the principles that guided his actions.
4. The Essential Gandhi, edited by Louis Fischer
This collection brings together Gandhi's speeches, letters, and writings, offering a comprehensive introduction to his philosophy. Readers can explore his views on education, religion, social justice, economic equality, and nonviolence. The book demonstrates how Gandhi's ideas remain relevant in discussions about leadership and ethical living today.
5. India After Gandhi by Ramachandra Guha
While not exclusively about Gandhi, this acclaimed history examines the India that emerged after independence. The book helps readers understand how Gandhi's vision influenced the nation and how subsequent generations have grappled with the challenges of democracy, diversity, and development.
6. The Good Boatman: A Portrait of Gandhi by Rajmohan Gandhi
Written by Gandhi's grandson and noted historian Rajmohan Gandhi, this acclaimed biography offers a nuanced portrait of the Mahatma beyond the familiar historical narrative. The book explores Gandhi's views on truth, nonviolence, caste, religion, leadership, and India's struggle for freedom while also examining the complexities and contradictions of his life. Rather than presenting a one-dimensional hero, it portrays Gandhi as a deeply human figure whose ideas continue to shape discussions on ethics, politics, and social change.
7. My Experiments with Truth for Young Readers by Mahatma Gandhi
Adapted for younger audiences, this version introduces Gandhi's ideas in a simple and engaging manner.
It focuses on values such as honesty, compassion, discipline, and courage, making it an ideal read for students and families looking to celebrate Gandhi Jayanti through meaningful learning.
Why khadi matters this Gandhi Jayanti
When Gandhi promoted khadi, he was advocating more than a fabric. He viewed it as a symbol of self-reliance, equality, and empowerment. The spinning wheel, or charkha, became a powerful representation of ordinary people contributing to a larger movement for freedom and dignity.
Khadi embodied the principles of swadeshi and encouraged communities to support local production rather than depend on imported goods. Today, khadi continues to remind us of the importance of sustainable choices, local craftsmanship, and responsible consumption, values that remain relevant in a rapidly changing world.
Final thoughts
It is an opportunity to reflect on ideas that continue to shape conversations around leadership, social change, and personal responsibility.
Whether you choose Gandhi's own writings or books inspired by his legacy, these seven reads offer valuable insights into truth, resilience, self-reliance, and the power of individual action. As Gandhi's association with khadi demonstrates, even the simplest actions can contribute to meaningful change when guided by purpose and conviction.

articles.title: FTC is Investigating OpenAI and Anthropic Over Possible Risks to Consumers
articles.text:
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has opened an investigation into OpenAI, Anthropic and other artificial intelligence companies over dangers their technology may pose to consumers, the agency said Wednesday.
The AI giants and other tech companies in recent months have disclosed examples of their AI agents going beyond human instructions, finding their way onto the internet and hacking external websites.
An FTC spokesperson confirmed the investigation but declined further comment. The investigation was first reported by the New York Post, which said it has been underway for months.
Representatives for Anthropic and OpenAI did not immediately respond to messages for comment on Wednesday.
Concerns around the dangers powerful AI models may pose to humanity have led some of the top AI developers to call for a slowdown. The CEO of Anthropic, Dario Amodei, said this month that the industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without such a slowdown, Amodei warned that within six to 12 months AI could be capable of leading a swarm of agents that could take over the entire internet.
OpenAI, meanwhile, recently delayed the launch of its newest model this week over safety concerns.

articles.title: Over 543,000 valid credentials exposed in public GitHub repositories
articles.text:
More than 543,000 credentials exposed in public GitHub repositories were still valid in July despite the platform’s security measures to prevent accidental leaks of sensitive data.
Data pulled from scanning 224 million repositories and more than 58 billion files show that the median time a unique credential remained publicly accessible was 784 days.
The research was conducted by Truffle Security, which found that about 10% of the working credentials were older than 6.3 years and the oldest one dated from 2009.
In total, the researchers identified 543,699 unique credentials that appeared repeatedly across more than 1.1 million files and repositories, including copies in forks.
The assessment was conducted on a dataset assembled to train large language models, based on a crawl that closed on August 7, 2025.
Truffle Security says that the number of exposed credentials on GitHub exposure is more than double to what it found in August after scanning Hugging Face, where it detected 221,303 working credentials.
The researchers note that secret density has increased over time, with the number of working credentials rising from 3.72 per million files in 2015 to a peak of 11.62 in 2025.
Push Protection effect
GitHub's safeguard against accidentally leaking credentials, Push Protection, was introduced in April 2022 for Advanced Security users and became available for public repositories in May 2023. A year later, GitHub enabled it by default.
The mechanism scans incoming code for secret patterns like API keys and access tokens, and blocks the upload if it detects one. However, it does not revoke previously exposed credentials.
Truffle Security reports that 199,843 of the credentials identified in July were exposed after GitHub activated Push Protection for all users in February 2024, accounting for roughly 36.8% of the total.
A little over half (51.8%) of the live credentials fell into categories that GitHub's default Push Protection does not block, including database connection strings and Google API keys.
However, Push Protection appears effective within its coverage: the rate of exposed credentials in protected categories fell by 53% after the feature was enabled by default.
Revocating exposed secrets
Looking at the dataset more broadly, Truffle says some credential types are a lot more likely to be revoked than others, depending on the service.
For example, of 101,886 committed npm tokens, the researchers found only 1 that still worked. In contrast, out of 126,963 exposed Google Cloud service account credentials, 69,041 were still valid and working at the time of the analysis.
The practical recommendation for those affected is to immediately rotate exposed credentials, clean up repositories, scan history, and set automatic expiration for all active secrets.
Truffle’s Security findings indicate the level and scale of working secret exposure on GitHub, but they don't reveal what percentage of those secrets are actually stolen and abused by attackers.

articles.title: Así se puede ‘reparar’ un cerebro adicto a las pantallas para que vuelva a concentrarse
articles.text:
Reparar un cerebro adicto a las pantallas para que vuelva a sostener la concentración es posible, según coinciden varios especialistas en neurociencia y psicología cognitiva.
El punto de partida es una cifra que preocupa a los investigadores: el tiempo promedio que una persona dedica a una tarea frente a una pantalla antes de cambiar de actividad cayó de dos minutos y medio en 2004 a apenas 47 segundos en la actualidad.
PUBLICIDAD
El dato surge de los estudios de Gloria Mark, profesora de Informática en la Universidad de California en Irvine, quien mide este fenómeno desde hace dos décadas.
Por qué las pantallas fragmentan la atención
El cerebro humano no procesa la información de forma continua, sino mediante filtros que priorizan ciertos estímulos y suprimen otros. Ese mecanismo recibe el nombre de atención.
“Aspectos de la atención a veces se comparan con un foco que escanea continuamente el entorno y se detiene para iluminar la información importante”, señaló Ian Fiebelkorn, profesor asociado de Neurociencia en el Instituto Del Monte para la Neurociencia de la Universidad de Rochester.
Según sus investigaciones, ese foco atencional no solo se atenúa en los períodos largos que solemos llamar “capacidad de atención”, sino también en una escala de tiempo mucho más veloz. Entre cuatro y seis veces por segundo existe una ventana en la que una distracción puede desviar el foco de lo que se intenta hacer.
PUBLICIDAD
Las pantallas explotan esas ventanas de vulnerabilidad. Las aplicaciones combinan sonidos y vibraciones para mantener un flujo constante de sensaciones, de manera que el cerebro asocia el cambio de tarea con una recompensa inmediata. Ese circuito de estímulo y premio refuerza el hábito de saltar de una actividad a otra.
El costo de saltar entre tareas y pantallas
Cambiar de actividad todo el tiempo no es gratuito para el organismo. Mark encontró una correlación directa entre la frecuencia con la que una persona cambia de foco y sus niveles de estrés, medidos con monitores de frecuencia cardíaca.
“Cuanto más rápido ocurre el cambio de atención, el estrés aumenta”, indicó la investigadora, quien agregó que décadas de estudios de laboratorio muestran que la multitarea eleva la presión arterial y otros marcadores fisiológicos de tensión.
PUBLICIDAD
A ese desgaste se suma lo que Mark denomina “costo de cambio”: cada vez que se interrumpe una tarea para pasar a otra, el cerebro necesita tiempo para reorientarse y recordar en qué punto se había quedado. Ese proceso consume recursos mentales adicionales, incrementa los errores y ralentiza el desempeño, algo documentado en estudios con médicos, enfermeros y pilotos.
No todos los cambios de actividad son perjudiciales. Tomar una pausa después de terminar una sección de trabajo, en lo que Mark llama un “punto de quiebre” natural, permite recuperar energía sin generar el mismo desgaste que una interrupción abrupta en medio de una tarea.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo entrenar de nuevo la concentración
La primera recomendación de los especialistas apunta a reducir las distracciones antes de que aparezcan. “La mejor manera de evitar cambios frecuentes del foco atencional es eliminar las distracciones potenciales”, afirmó Fiebelkorn, quien sugiere apagar el celular o dejarlo en otra habitación durante el estudio o el trabajo, y desconectar internet si la tarea puede hacerse sin conexión.
Otra estrategia consiste en disminuir el atractivo visual del teléfono. Apagar la vibración, el sonido y el color de la pantalla desde los ajustes reduce los estímulos que recibe el cerebro y, con el tiempo, baja las ganas de revisar el dispositivo.
PUBLICIDAD
Programar descansos estructurados también ayuda a reducir la incertidumbre que agota al cerebro. Comenzar con bloques breves de concentración, de uno a tres minutos, e ir aumentando la duración de forma progresiva permite entrenar la capacidad de sostener el foco sin que una distracción arruine el intento.
Fiebelkorn coincide en la importancia de este punto: “El cerebro se cansa después de concentrarse durante mucho tiempo. Para ayudar a evitar esta fatiga, se pueden programar pausas breves dentro de una sesión de estudio o trabajo”.
Finalmente, ambos especialistas remarcan que concentrarse en una sola tarea a la vez es más eficaz que intentar abarcar varias. “Si tienes una tarea importante, dale toda tu atención y completala antes de pasar a la siguiente”, propuso Fiebelkorn.
PUBLICIDAD
Mark agrega que mantener el “tanque” de recursos mentales lleno, con buen descanso nocturno, es determinante para poder enfocarse: la falta de sueño acumulada, o “deuda de sueño”, se asocia directamente con lapsos de atención más cortos y con la tendencia a refugiarse en actividades livianas, como las redes sociales, en lugar de tareas que exigen esfuerzo.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Loewe Neo : une enceinte nomade haut de gamme rétro-éclairée et design
articles.text:
Une enceinte Bluetooth, oui, mais une enceinte haut de gamme, s'il vous plait. Loewe, habitué des enceintes de salon sobres et design, se lance dans une enceinte personnalisable et portable, toujours sur un segment tarifaire que l'on connaît au constructeur.
On connaît Loewe pour ses enceintes Bluetooth haut de gamme et design. Le constructeur allemand se lance maintenant dans les enceintes rétroéclairées, chose que l'on ne lui connaissait pas, avec la Neo, une enceinte en aluminium résistante à l'eau.
Un positionnement premium, comme toujours
Loewe n'a pas pour habitude de faire de l'entrée de gamme, et cette Neo n'est pas accessible à toutes les bourses. Cependant, la Neo est une des rares enceintes portables du fabricant.
Conçue en aluminium, elle est également certifiée IP67, afin de résister à l'eau et à la poussière. Pour rappel, la norme IP67 certifie que l'appareil peut être immergé dans l'eau jusqu'à 1 mètre durant 30 minutes. Si ce n'est pas une raison pour la plonger sous l'eau, elle peut être utilisée au bord de la piscine sans problème.
Si l'on connaît Loewe pour le design très sobre de ses produits, la Neo quant à elle, n'opte pas pour la sobriété absolue. C'est la première enceinte de la marque à proposer un rétroéclairage via une bande lumineuse sur l'enceinte. Un côté très gadget, mais original que proposent déjà d'autres enceintes, comme celles de chez JBL.
Avec, Loewe fournit également une sangle en cuir amovible et un étui rigide en feutre pour la transporter.
Comme une touche de personnalisation en plus est toujours appréciable, le fabricant propose également des extérieurs modulaires et des grilles de haut-parleurs interchangeables.
Une qualité audio travaillée
Niveau audio, elle propose jusqu'à 50 watts de puissance sonore avec deux membranes passives, pour optimiser les basses fréquences.
Une application dédiée complète l'offre en permettant à l'utilisateur de choisir parmi trois préréglages sonores, de régler séparément les basses et les aigus via un égaliseur, mais également de configurer l'éclairage selon ses préférences.
Prix et disponibilité
La Loewe Neo sera commercialisée en trois finitions : "aluminium argent", "aluminium noir" et "champagne". Le prix de vente conseillé est de 400 euros et l'enceinte sera disponible à partir du 20 novembre 2026. La version "champagne" sera produite en édition limitée.

articles.title: A new PS5 jailbreak works on almost every firmware version, and it already runs the latest games
articles.text:
Modding FTW: A recently unveiled exploit can allegedly unlock the PlayStation 5's compatibility with unlicensed content on a larger number of consoles. The underlying security issue works with almost any PS5 firmware version, and newer games can apparently be played on unlocked consoles already.
Code hackers focused on the PlayStation 5 have just released another massive contribution to the homebrew scene for Sony's console. The "Relapse" exploit can be used to jailbreak most PS5 machines, turning the DRM-ridden device into a custom computing powerhouse. Needless to say, a jailbroken PS5 also plays pirated games.
The Relapse exploit is a further addition to the growing list of "useful" security issues developers and white hat hackers have discovered in the PS5 platform over the years. Unlike other exploits, Relapse can apparently work on most PS5 firmware versions except the most recent one (14.00.00). The 14.00.00 firmware was only released a couple of weeks ago, which means Sony is now going to have a much bigger security problem to deal with.
Most PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles currently available at retail use the vulnerable firmware versions, so they should be compatible with the Relapse exploit. Newer game releases usually come with a mandatory firmware update, but modding enthusiasts are currently having a field day trying to run open-source operating systems, custom applications, and pirated game releases on jailbroken consoles.
 – Lance McDonald (@manfightdragon) September 29, 2026
Thanks to Relapse, users can apparently run the latest PS5 games without paying Sony and publishers a single cent. Marvel's Wolverine, a game released on September 15, seems to work fine. The same applies to The Witcher III Remastered, a free update to the Witcher III experience released just yesterday. Relapse can also turn a stock PS5 into a homebrew-compatible console in less than a minute.
Relapse couldn't have come at a worse time for Sony. The Japanese gaming giant is facing growing user distrust after announcing that physical disc releases will soon be dead. Furthermore, an over-excited community of programmers and vibe-coding fans is rapidly turning PlayStation 5 emulation on PC into a tangible goal.
PlayStation is one of the leading platforms in the console gaming industry, and people will likely target these machines for much longer than Sony could ever anticipate. Enthusiasts are still uncovering technical secrets related to the ancient, legendary PlayStation 2 console decades after the machine's retail debut.

articles.title: Trump plan to combat AI risks hinges on Big Tech pals policing themselves
articles.text:
Amid escalating AI security incidents causing OpenAI to halt training and pause releases, Donald Trump continues to advocate for the AI industry to regulate itself as the best path to combat emerging risks when developing frontier AI.
In an agreement Tuesday, two dozen tech firms voluntarily committed to implementing controls recommended by the White House, including undergoing independent safety audits that will test whether firms’ internal controls, monitoring, and detecting are actually working. Key focuses for external reviews included “risks related to cybersecurity, biosecurity, chemical threats, and unintended actions by AI models.”
Firms also agreed to regularly meet to discuss best practices and set common AI safety standards and benchmarks. Among signers were leaders like Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI’s Sam Altman, SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, and Alphabet/Google’s Sundar Pichai.
Nothing new is legally required of firms, and some—like Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI—had already committed to external audits, The Information reported. Additionally, many firms have voluntarily committed to highly secretive government safety testing. Adding to these tests, Trump insisted the Tuesday deal will somehow better address real emerging risks and is “morally binding,” despite carrying no legal weight, Bloomberg reported.
“It’s almost like a constitution, in a way,” Trump told reporters at the White House following a lunch with tech leaders. “The biggest people in the world signed that, and I signed it as president, and it really is a form of protection.”
Eventually, it “may make sense to codify” the recommendations, the agreement said near the end. But for now, Trump stressed that the best possible future for the US requires trusting AI firms to regulate themselves.
Trump’s Big Tech friends embrace “SI”
So far, very few details have been released about how the new round of safety audits would work. Trump has only posted a summary of the accord on Truth Social.
It’s also unclear who Trump is tapping to audit frontier models. Bloomberg noted that Trump seems to be politicizing the selection process, while some AI firms appear uncertain what might qualify as a third party to test their frontier AI. Some progress has been made already in finding candidates, though, as Bloomberg reported that “some of the firms poised to conduct those reviews have already met” with the US agency conducting voluntary government pre-deployment safety tests, the Center for AI Standards and Innovation.

articles.title: OpenAI dispara contra los creadores de Kimi por supuestamente copiar su IA
articles.text:
Moonshot, la empresa detrás de Kimi, una de las IA chinas más capaces y populares, ha quedado envuelta en una polémica por el desarrollo de su tecnología. OpenAI ha publicado un reporte sobre una campaña de destilación de sus modelos de lenguaje cuya autoría correspondería en parte a individuos vinculados con la firma del gigante asiático.
Según explica OpenAI, la destilación de modelos se inició el 1 de julio y alcanzó su pico entre los días 24 y 25 de ese mes. Pocos días más tarde, la compañía que lidera Sam Altman logró interrumpir el accionar de forma definitiva.
El reporte explica que los intentos de destilar los modelos que impulsan ChatGPT y otros productos de la compañía buscaban extraer razonamiento protegido. OpenAI menciona que para ello se utilizaron métodos bastante novedosos y que la propia firma considera que se volverán todavía más sofisticados con el correr del tiempo.
Tanto el cifrado como las bases de datos y otras infraestructuras de OpenAI no se vieron afectadas por el incidente, se menciona. Y si bien la empresa californiana no ha señalado al autor absoluto de esta campaña, sí ha apuntado contra individuos presuntamente relacionados con Moonshot, la startup china que desarrolla Kimi.
"No está claro si todos los operadores que observamos durante el periodo pertinente provenían de un mismo actor. Sin embargo, atribuimos un núcleo principal de la actividad a personas vinculadas a Moonshot AI, la empresa desarrolladora de Kimi", remarcan los estadounidenses.
Kimi, bajo la lupa por acusaciones de destilación de modelos de OpenAI
No es la primera vez que Moonshot recibe acusaciones de destilación de modelos occidentales. En julio pasado, la Oficina de Política de Ciencia y Tecnología de Estados Unidos acusó a la firma china de copiar sin autorización los datos de entrenamiento de Claude Fable, para usarlos en Kimi K3.
"La destilación legítima de IA, utilizada para crear modelos más pequeños y eficientes, desempeña un papel fundamental en este ecosistema de innovación abierta. Sin embargo, la destilación industrial encubierta a gran escala, cuyo objetivo es robar tecnología patentada estadounidense y socavar la investigación en Estados Unidos, es inaceptable", publicó por entonces el jefe del citado organismo.
Por lo pronto, Kimi no se ha pronunciado respecto de las acusaciones vertidas por OpenAI sobre la destilación de sus modelos. Esta práctica lleva tiempo generando polémica, pues permite el desarrollo de modelos de inteligencia artificial capaces, pero con una fracción del coste y del tiempo que se requiere al hacerlo desde cero.
Tanto empresas de inteligencia artificial estadounidenses como el gobierno de Donald Trump han catalogado la práctica como "robo". No obstante, NVIDIA parece ahora tener una mirada diferente. Días atrás, Jensen Huang, CEO de la compañía, lo definió como un tipo "competencia".

articles.title: Das 9-to-5-Diktat: Warum starre Arbeitszeiten für Abendtypen zum Gesundheitsrisiko werden
articles.text:
Neue Studie zeigt: Nachteulen verlassen den Beruf deutlich früher
Menschen mit einer späten inneren Uhr haben ein um rund 70 Prozent höheres Risiko, vorzeitig aus dem Erwerbsleben auszuscheiden. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt ein Team von Forscher:innen der finnischen Universität Oulu, wie in einer im Fachjournal Occupational and Environmental Medicine veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist.
Die Mediziner:innen analysierten die Daten von 5.679 Teilnehmer:innen einer finnischen Geburtskohorte aus dem Jahr 1966. Die Beobachtung erstreckte sich über einen Zeitraum von zwölf Jahren, in dem das Lebensalter der Personen von 46 auf 57 Jahre anstieg.
Dabei zeigte sich, dass sogenannte Nachteulen deutlich häufiger eine Erwerbsminderungsrente in Anspruch nehmen mussten als Morgentypen (Lerchen) oder keine den beiden Extremen zuzuordnende Personen. Dieser Unterschied blieb bei beiden Geschlechtern als konstante statistische Größe bestehen, selbst als externe Faktoren wie Bildungsebene, Einkommen und der spezifische Beruf herausgerechnet wurden.
Methodik zur Bestimmung der Chronotypen
Die Zuordnung zu den jeweiligen Biorhythmen erfolgte nicht allein auf Basis subjektiver Einschätzungen der Proband:innen. Das Team der Universität Oulu nutzte validierte Fragebögen, die detailliert erfassten, wie schwer das Aufwachen fiel und wie stark die Müdigkeit in der ersten halben Stunde des Tages ausgeprägt war.
Zusätzlich glichen die Wissenschaftler:innen diese Selbsteinschätzungen mit genetischen Daten aus einer früheren Erhebung ab. Dieser polygene Score für frühes Aufstehen bestätigte die biologische Basis der Angaben, wodurch eine Verfälschung der Ergebnisse durch rein persönliche Vorlieben unwahrscheinlich wurde.
Etwa 10 Prozent der befragten Männer und 12 Prozent der Frauen fielen am Ende der Auswertung in die Kategorie der Nachteulen. Die Gruppen der Morgen- und Zwischentypen machten jeweils mehr als 40 Prozent der Gesamtmenge aus.
Gesundheitliche Ursachen bei Abendtypen
Die Auswertung ergab, dass fast die Hälfte der männlichen und gut 43 Prozent der weiblichen Nachteulen ihre allgemeine Gesundheit als schlecht einstuften. Sie berichteten häufiger über Schlaflosigkeit, geringere körperliche Aktivität und einen ausgeprägten sozialen Jetlag.
Dieser Jetlag entsteht, wenn die biologisch präferierte Schlafzeit klar von den tatsächlichen Zeiten an Arbeitstagen abweicht. Laut der ergänzenden Zusammenfassung auf StudyFinds führt diese Diskrepanz langfristig zu chronischem Schlafmangel, der kognitive Fähigkeiten beeinträchtigt und den körperlichen Abbau beschleunigt.
Erst als die Forscher:innen eben jene gesundheitlichen Einschränkungen und die absolvierten Arbeitszeiten in ihre Modelle einbezogen, schrumpfte die statistische Lücke zwischen Eulen und Lerchen messbar. Vor allem die geleisteten Wochenstunden und das Arbeiten in Schichten hatten einen starken Einfluss auf die Wahrscheinlichkeit eines frühen Berufsausstiegs.
Konsequenzen aus starren Schichtmodellen
Während über 70 Prozent der Nachteulen angaben, in regulären Tagesjobs zu arbeiten, war der Anteil an Nachtschichten bei ihnen dennoch signifikant höher als bei den Lerchen. Die Forscher:innen betonen, dass ein typischer Arbeitstag in Finnland um acht Uhr morgens beginnt, was einer Zeit entspricht, in der späte Chronotypen noch unterhalb ihres maximalen Leistungsniveaus operieren.
Die Daten offenbarten zudem weitere soziodemografische Auffälligkeiten innerhalb der untersuchten Gruppen. Nachteulen waren zwar im Durchschnitt höher gebildet, lebten aber seltener in einer Ehe oder festen Partnerschaft und waren häufiger von Erwerbslosigkeit betroffen.
Eine Erwerbsminderungsrente wird in dem untersuchten finnischen System nur bewilligt, wenn ein medizinisches Gutachten eine dauerhafte und schwerwiegende Einschränkung der Arbeitsfähigkeit bestätigt. Das bedeutet, dass der beobachtete Ausstieg nicht auf eine fehlende Motivation zurückzuführen ist, sondern auf nachweisbare medizinische Diagnosen fußt.
Die Studienautor:innen weisen explizit darauf hin, dass dieser Verlust von erfahrenen Arbeitskräften ein ernst zu nehmendes Problem für die Volkswirtschaften darstellt. Der unfreiwillige Abschied aus dem Berufsleben geschieht während der produktivsten Kernjahre einer normalen Karriere.
Trotz der umfassenden Datenlage weisen die Forscher:innen auf gewisse Limitierungen ihrer Methodik hin. So basierte die Erfassung des Chronotyps lediglich auf einer einmaligen Befragung im Alter von 46 Jahren, weshalb sich die Resultate vornehmlich auf diese spezifische Altersgruppe beziehen.
Das unbedingte Festhalten an konventionellen Arbeitszeiten, die sich vorwiegend am Rhythmus von Lerchen orientieren, benachteiligt die Gruppe der Eulen demzufolge systematisch. Ob asynchrone Arbeitsmodelle diese Entwicklung stoppen können, müssen weitere Analysen klären, da die Studie lediglich Beobachtungen festhält, aber keine Kausalität zwischen flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und einer sinkenden Rentenquote isolieren konnte.

articles.title: Factory CEO just accused his VC board adviser of spying for Cognition | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Matan Grinberg, co-founder and CEO of the AI coding startup Factory, said in a post on X on Wednesday that he fired VC Chris Degnan from his role as a board adviser. Grinberg alleges that Degnan shared confidential information with Factory’s biggest competitor, Cognition.
Two hours after Grinberg’s post, Degnan announced on both X and LinkedIn that he had joined Cognition as its chief revenue officer. He also subsequently refuted Grinberg’s allegations, saying in a separate X post that he wasn’t fired but resigned when he told Grinberg he was taking the job.
Degnan was Snowflake’s first sales hire and later spent 11 years as the data company’s chief revenue officer. For the past five months, he has been a partner with RPT Partners, a Newport Beach, California, investor in Factory. Degnan is also a go-to-market adviser to startups at the much bigger venture firm Iconiq, a role that dates back to October of last year.
Three-year-old, San Francisco-based Factory is an agentic coding startup whose AI agents can carry out programming tasks largely on their own. The company raised $200 million at a $5 billion valuation this month from Khosla Ventures, Blackstone, Sequoia Capital, Insight Partners, and others. Its customers include Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada, Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile.
Grinberg said he sees Cognition, the maker of the Devin coding agent, as his biggest competitor. Cognition raised another $2 billion at a $48 billion valuation earlier this month, and counts Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Citi as customers.
Grinberg said on X that Degnan had earlier acknowledged having a “casual” conversation with a Cognition executive but had assured Grinberg that he had no interest in working for the competitor. According to Grinberg, Degnan said he had “made too much money” and was “too lazy to go work for Cognition,” which Grinberg said he “trusted and believed.”
On Monday, however, Degnan apparently disclosed that he had actually been in ongoing talks with Cognition.
This caused Grinberg to grow concerned about how much confidential information Degnan had about Factory, and how much he had shared and might share in the future with his new employer. He says he fired Degnan as a board adviser on Tuesday, writing:
For weeks, while he sat in our board meetings and advised our leadership team, he was also confiding with executives of our largest competitor. Chris was subject to confidentiality obligations in connection with his work with Factory. We do not know the extent of the information he shared, but it puts his timely questions about our product roadmap and what the parity gap involves into a new light.
But Degnan disputes that account as well. He says the last Factory board meeting he attended was weeks before he had “ever spoken” to Cognition and that he hasn’t shared confidential information. Degnan also says that when he told Grinberg that he was resigning to take the role at Cognition, Grinberg offered him a full-time job at Factory, which he declined.
Degnan’s post announcing his new job at Cognition doesn’t mention Factory. Very notably, it does say that RPT Partners and the firm’s managing partner, Chad Peets, will now be working with Cognition. “I am thrilled that Chad and the RPT team will be working closely with me in our pursuit of building a generational company,” Degnan wrote.
In the old, pre-AI world, a VC firm was especially cautious not to engage in conflict-of-interest business. In today’s world, many a VC has invested in direct AI competitors, such OpenAI and Anthropic.
In fact, Khosla Ventures is an investor in both Cognition (since at least early 2025) and Factory.
That didn’t stop the venture firm’s founder, Vinod Khosla, from jumping into the drama, seemingly in defense of his bigger portfolio company Cognition. Nor did it stop Khosla Ventures partner Keith Rabois from weighing in as well — in defense of Factory.
In a post on X, Khosla accused Grinberg of lying about firing Degnan. He called Factory a “struggling second tier competitor” and said Grinberg showed “no decency or sense of proper behavior,” which “shows your desperation.”
Grinberg replied that he has email receipts to verify his version of events but did not share them.
Meanwhile, Rabois opined on X, “It is unethical per se to even interview at a competitor while attending Board meetings and Board dinners.” He added that “to even sit for an interview while having access to board level information and without resigning is absolutely insane.”
Tracking the back-and-forth, Cognition co-founder and CEO Scott Wu also weighed in on the controversy on X. He politely expressed respect for the smaller competitor while insisting that his company has “no interest in Factory’s info.” Wu also contends that Degnan resigned on Monday but didn’t refute that Degnan was in talks with Cognition before that happened.
Either way, there could be consequences for perceived board-level conflicts of interest. VC giant Andreessen Horowitz is reportedly the subject of a Justice Department probe into its partners serving on competitors’ boards.
Grinberg argued that startup founders must be able to rely on their board members. “Chris’s conduct is unacceptable to me. Trust in Board Membership is one of the sacred bonds in the Silicon Valley, one that helps the startup ecosystem thrive. With it comes an enormous responsibility. That trust was violated.”
Degnan, Peets, Factory, and Khosla Ventures did not immediately respond to requests for further comment.
Note: This story was updated to include responses from Degnan, Khosla, Rabois, and Wu.

articles.title: Home interiors startup Gravity raises $15M led by 3one4 Capital and Info Edge Ventures
articles.text:
Home interiors startup Gravity raises $15M led by 3one4 Capital and Info Edge Ventures
Gravity will use this funding round to strengthen its technology, distribution and key-account infrastructure, and support category expansion.
Home interiors startup Gravity has raised $15 million in funding led by 3one4 Capital and Info Edge Ventures, with participation from Alteria Capital, Genesia Ventures and angel investors. This funding round was a combination of equity and debt.
Gravity will use this funding round to strengthen its technology, distribution and key-account infrastructure, support category expansion, build brand capabilities and provide the working capital needed to scale the platform over time.
Founded by former Livspace executives, Saurabh Jain and Lalit Mittal, Gravity is building common infrastructure for India's interior materials ecosystem by bringing together specialist businesses across the kitchen and wardrobe segment with a shared technology, distribution, key-account management and operating backbone.
Gravity Co-founder Saurabh Jain said, “Over the last decade, organised design and execution have transformed the home interiors market. However, the materials layer behind every project remains fragmented and complex. Designers, studios and suppliers continue to navigate multiple stakeholders, systems and processes to get projects delivered. We are building Gravity to make sourcing simpler, more dependable and more efficient through a platform designed around the needs of the industry. Our focus is to combine product depth with strong service, availability and execution at scale.”
According to Gravity, there is a structural shift underway in India's home interiors market. While designers, architects, modular showrooms and design-and-build studios increasingly influence material decisions, the supply landscape remains fragmented across dealers, distributors and single-category suppliers.
Gravity aims to simplify sourcing for these customers while improving availability, service levels, fulfilment and pricing visibility across categories.
Gravity co-founder Lalit Mittal said, “Designers and studios today influence a significant share of material decisions, yet managing sourcing across categories remains time-consuming and operationally challenging. Gravity brings together common capabilities across technology, distribution, procurement and customer service, enabling a better experience for both category businesses and specifiers.”
As part of its future plans, Gravity plans to expand beyond kitchens and wardrobes into adjacent interior systems, leveraging its shared operating infrastructure to serve a wider set of material categories.

articles.title: Google Pixel 11a : vous ne devinerez jamais à quoi il ressemble
articles.text:
C’est sous le nom de code « Formosan » que le Google Pixel 11a fait parler de lui à travers des premières images partagées par Android Headlines. Le Pixel 10a ressemblait déjà beaucoup au Pixel 9a, et cela devrait également être le cas du Pixel 11a si l’on en croit ces images. Mais les changements seraient à aller chercher à l’intérieur.
Le Pixel 11a, un Pixel 10a avec une moustache ?
Impossible d’être surpris en découvrant les lignes de ce Pixel 11a, puisque Google conserverait le même design que sur les deux générations précédentes. Le smartphone garde un bloc photo arrière totalement plat et un format minimaliste, même si la forme du module photo évolue légèrement vers un ovale un peu plus court. Côté mensurations, les leaks annoncent un boîtier d’environ 153,46 x 72,35 x 9 mm pour un écran de 6,3 pouces, ce qui le rend un tout petit peu plus court que les Pixel 9a et 10a.
Source : Android Headlines / OnLeaks
Quatre coloris seraient disponibles au lancement : noir (Obsidian), argent (Fog), vert (Olive) et une option violette. À l’avant, les bordures restent en revanche assez épaisses, un choix qui donne un petit coup de vieux à l’appareil avant même sa sortie. Côté affichage, la dalle de 6,3 pouces profiterait toujours d’un taux de rafraîchissement allant de 60 à 120 Hz et d’une luminosité maximale en plein soleil jusqu’à 3 350 nits.
La bascule vers la puce Tensor G6 et un nouveau modem
Contrairement au Pixel 10a qui avait la même puce que le Pixel 9a (un Tensor G4), le Pixel 11a passerait directement au processeur Tensor G6, c’est-à-dire celui qui équipe les Pixel 11 et Pixel 11 Pro. Le SoC serait accompagné d’un modem MediaTek censé régler les petits soucis de réseau des générations précédentes, tout en grappillant de précieuses heures d’autonomie grâce à une meilleure gestion du signal.
Pour épauler ce nouveau processeur, Google intégrerait le co-processeur de sécurité Titan M3 afin d’assurer la protection des mots de passe et des paiements. L’appareil embarquera également une batterie avoisinant les 5 000 mAh et tournera sous Android 17. Côté photo, le duo de capteurs arrière de 48 et 13 mégapixels reste en place, mais la caméra selfie profiterait d’un tout nouveau capteur. Quant au tarif, si la marque est restée bloquée à 499 dollars pendant quatre ans, la hausse générale des composants liée à l’intelligence artificielle pourrait bien faire grimper la facture à 599 dollars. Reste maintenant à voir comment cela se traduira en euros chez nous. Pour rappel, les Pixel 9a et Pixel 10a ont été lancés à 549 €.
