articles.title: Alarmierende Google-Zahlen: KI verdoppelt entdeckte Sicherheitslücken
articles.text:
Google-Analyse zeigt Verdopplung von Softwareschwachstellen durch KI
Die Google Threat Intelligence Group hat einen aktuellen Bericht zur Cybersicherheit veröffentlicht. Darin dokumentiert die Analyseeinheit eine Verdopplung der gemeldeten Softwareschwachstellen innerhalb weniger Monate.
Im Januar 2026 registrierte Google noch 5.045 sogenannte Vulnerability Disclosures, während die Zahl im August bereits auf 10.740 anstieg. Wie der Bericht weiter ausführt, spielt der Einsatz von Künstlicher Intelligenz bei dieser Entwicklung eine zentrale Rolle.
KI-Agenten finden veränderte Fehlerprofile
Sicherheitsforscher:innen nutzen zunehmend autonome KI-Agenten, um komplexe Systeme auf Schwachstellen zu prüfen. Diese Werkzeuge decken strukturell andere Arten von Fehlern auf als herkömmliche Scanner.
Laut der Analyse führen 50 Prozent der durch KI gefundenen Fehler zu einer Remotecodeausführung, bei der Angreifer:innen Code aus der Ferne ausführen können. Bei klassisch aufgespürten Lücken liegt dieser Anteil bei lediglich 26 Prozent.
Die Google-Einheit erklärt diesen Unterschied damit, dass Forschungsteams ihre KI-Werkzeuge gezielt auf kritische Infrastrukturen und Speicherfehler ansetzen. Die Systeme können tiefergehende logische Fehler in Programmiersprachen wie C identifizieren, die statische Analysetools übersehen.
Einfluss von Anbieterzyklen auf die Daten
Die reine Anzahl der gemeldeten Schwachstellen wird laut dem Google-Bericht allerdings auch durch automatisierte Meldeprozesse beeinflusst. So verursachte allein der Begriff „Linux Kernel“ im laufenden Jahr rund 5.000 Einträge, ohne dass in diesem Zusammenhang eine einzige ausgenutzte Zero-Day-Schwachstelle registriert wurde.
Gleichzeitig sorgten konzentrierte Patch-Veröffentlichungen einzelner Anbieter für Spitzenwerte in der Statistik. Im August 2026 stammten 128 der als hochriskant eingestuften Schwachstellen aus den vierteljährlichen Updates des Technologieunternehmens Oracle aus dem US-Bundesstaat Texas sowie aus Netzwerktreiber-Advisories für Linux.
Beschleunigte Ausnutzung von N-Days
Neben der reinen Entdeckung verändert sich auch die Ausnutzung der Schwachstellen durch böswillige Akteur:innen. Die Zahl der ausgenutzten Zero-Day-Lücken, für die es noch keine Fehlerbehebung gibt, stieg laut dem Bericht nur leicht von durchschnittlich acht auf elf pro Monat an.
Deutlich stärker wuchs hingegen die Ausnutzung von Fehlern mit hohem Risiko, sogenannten N-Days, die bereits bekannt und oft auch gepatcht sind. Hier stieg die Zahl der ausgenutzten Lücken von 28 im gesamten Jahr 2025 auf 75 zwischen Januar und August 2026.
Die Studienautor:innen vermuten, dass Angreifer:innen große Sprachmodelle einsetzen, um Produktversionen und Patch-Informationen automatisiert abzugleichen. Auf dieser Basis lassen sich bekannte Schwachstellen schneller in funktionsfähige Exploits umwandeln.
Die Angriffe konzentrieren sich dabei weiterhin auf Perimeter-Appliances und exponierte Unternehmensdienste. Edge-Gateways stellen laut der Analyse einen primären Vektor für den initialen Zugriff dar.
Mehr als 65 Prozent der ausgenutzten Schwachstellen an diesen Netzwerkrändern fielen in die Kategorien mit hohem oder kritischem Risiko. Angreifer:innen zielen dabei primär auf unauthentifizierte, öffentliche Verwaltungsschnittstellen ab, um die blinden Flecken von Unternehmenssoftware auszunutzen.
KI-Infrastruktur als eigenes Ziel
Der Google-Bericht beleuchtet zudem Schwachstellen in der KI-Infrastruktur selbst. Von Januar 2025 bis August 2026 zählte die Analyseeinheit in diesem Bereich 2.076 gemeldete Fehler.
Über 1.500 dieser Meldungen entfallen allein auf das laufende Jahr, wobei Orchestrierungs-Frameworks wie Langflow etwa die Hälfte der Fälle ausmachen. Diese visuellen Workflow-Builder beinhalten oft Knotenpunkte zur Codeausführung, die durch gezielte Eingaben manipuliert werden können.
Inferenz-Server im Fokus der Angreifer:innen
Wie Siliconangle berichtet, nutzen Angreifer:innen hier Techniken wie Prompt-Injections, um über die Systeme Schadcode einzuschleusen. Darüber hinaus verzeichnete Google 212 Meldungen zu Inferenz- und Serving-Software wie vLLM und Ollama.
Fast ein Viertel dieser Fehler ließ sich auf unauthentifizierte Programmierschnittstellen oder fehlerhafte Anfragenfälschungen auf der Serverseite zurückführen. Bislang hat die Google Threat Intelligence Group jedoch noch keine Zero-Day-Ausnutzung dieser KI-Infrastruktur beobachtet.
Wenn Schwachstellen in KI-Middleware ausgenutzt werden, geschieht dies zumeist bei Systemen, die ungeschützt aus dem Internet erreichbar sind. In einem Fall dokumentierte das kalifornische Cybersicherheitsunternehmen Sysdig einen autonomen Ransomware-Angriff, der über eine ältere Schwachstelle in Langflow eindrang.
Solche zentralisierten KI-Gateways stellen eine doppelte Bedrohung dar. Einerseits legen kompromittierte Systeme Schnittstellenschlüssel und private Datenströme offen, andererseits dienen sie als initialer Ankerpunkt, um seitwärts in interne Cloud-Umgebungen einzudringen.
Neues Vorgehen beim Patch-Management
Aus den gesammelten Daten leitet die Analyseeinheit konkrete Empfehlungen für IT-Abteilungen ab. Das klassische, unpriorisierte Massen-Patching ist den veränderten Zeitabläufen demnach nicht mehr gewachsen.
Stattdessen rät das Unternehmen dazu, Fehlerbehebungen auf Basis aktueller Bedrohungslagen zu priorisieren. Ein gezielter Schutz an den Netzwerkrändern bilde dabei die betriebliche Grundlage.
Softwareanbieter sollten zudem eigene KI-gestützte Code-Reviews durchführen, bevor sie Produkte ausliefern. Dadurch ließe sich das Wachstum der öffentlich gemeldeten Schwachstellen langfristig eindämmen.

articles.title: Apple's new CEO wants to move faster, cut jobs, and squeeze more out of services
articles.text:
The takeaway: John Ternus took over as Apple CEO at the start of September, and a recent report offers clues on how his reign might differ from Tim Cook's. The new chief executive officer reportedly wants to reduce headcount, extract more revenue from services, and change the company's traditional hardware release cycle.
Sources have informed Bloomberg that Apple might shift to a more aggressive hardware release schedule under its new head. John Ternus aims to reshape the Cupertino giant into a leaner company to navigate ongoing memory shortages and compete in the AI space with companies like Microsoft, Meta, and Google.
The former hardware chief, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1, aims to move away from Apple's traditional spring and fall release schedule and instead release products throughout the year. While some inside the company estimate the shift could take years, Ternus also wants future products to be more experimental.
Part of the new approach will mean slimming down by eliminating some middle management positions to speed up communication between on-the-ground engineers and top executives. One source described the situation as "hectic" and more hands-on under Ternus.
Some engineering program managers, including half a dozen directors, have already been given a few weeks to find new jobs within Apple or be laid off at the end of this year. The affected programs include the development of the Vision Pro headset, Siri, and other AI-related software. The company almost replaced 5,000 AppleCare customer service employees with AI, but eventually changed its mind.
Apple's near-future product roadmap is already quite busy. Over the next year, the company is expected to release game controllers under its Beats brand, the iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2, iPhone 18e, a refreshed iPad lineup, new Apple Pencils, a new HomePod mini, an upgraded Apple TV, and several new Mac devices, some of which feature the product line's first-ever touchscreens. This follows a year that has already included the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple's first-ever foldable phone, the AirPods 5, and a Mac mini that introduced the M6 processor.
Meanwhile, the new CEO also aims to extract more revenue from services such as iCloud, Apple TV Plus, and other subscriptions. The sector has been a major growth driver for Apple, but its importance might grow amid the RAM crisis. Like virtually every other hardware manufacturer, the company has already raised prices to offset higher component costs, but it is seeking new revenue sources to avoid making its core products too expensive.

articles.title: Ethereum: cuál es la cotización de esta criptomoneda
articles.text:
Ethereum es una plataforma digital que adopta la tecnología de cadena de bloques (blockchain) y expande su uso a una gran variedad de aplicaciones, mientras que ether es su criptomoneda nativa. En el mundo de las finanzas digitales es común que la criptomoneda sea llamada como la red, aunque en realidad no son lo mismo.
La plataforma ethereum, creada en el 2015 por el programador Vitalik Buterin, buscaba ser un instrumento para aplicaciones descentralizadas y colaborativas sobre las que se pueden hacer contratos inteligentes (dAPPs)
PUBLICIDAD
Al igual que el bitcoin, el valor de ether se disparó en un corto periodo de tiempo. En enero de 2016, ether cotizaba alrededor de un dólar y actualmente tiene un máximo histórico de 4.953,73 dólares.
El precio de la criptomoneda de ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2724.65 dólares por unidad.
Esto quiere decir que el activo digital tuvo un cambio del -0.33 las últimas 24 horas, así como una variación del 0.0 % en la última hora.
Actualmente, ethereum se encuentra en el lugar #2 de popularidad en el mercado digital. Cabe mencionar que el máximo histórico que ha alcanzado esta divisa digital es de 4891.7 dólares por unidad.
PUBLICIDAD
Costo de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
PUBLICIDAD
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: Deadlock City Never Sleeps Update Adds 6 New Heroes and Makes Numerous Map and UI Changes
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Deadlock City Never Sleeps Update Adds 6 New Heroes and Makes Numerous Map and UI Changes
Deadlock, Valve's MOBA that has been in beta testing for nearly two years, has just received another major update, building on its previous UI refinements and adding six more heroes into the mix, to boot. The update is called City Never Sleeps, and Deadlock's development team says that many of the new features and updates in this latest update have been in the works in parallel for several months. 
The new heroes are Nurse Harrow, Rat King, Solomon, Deadman Danny, Baba, and Violet, although not much else has been revealed about them other than their tags. As with previous hero drops, the new heroes can be voted on from within the game, but there is a now a double hero vote for your first win of the day, and voting takes place in the pre-game lobby, where you can argue about who to vote for with your teammates.
The Cursed Apple is ever-changing, and these streets are nothing like you remember. A massive visual update to the map and neutrals, six new heroes, HUD updates, numerous quality-of-life additions, accessibility options, and more.
In the full update notes, Valve details the changes to the map, which now consists of the Yellow (York), Blue (Broadway), and Green (Greenwich) lanes, each of which has its own distinct zones where players can encounter new neutral creatures with new behaviors, like the Specimens in the Blue lane, Gutter Ghouls and Barrel Mimics in York, and the Past Dues in Greenwich. Each lane now has a very distinct visual language and history, with three sectors, each offering plenty of obstacles and cover for Deadlock's customary high-mobility antics.The update also introduces the four districts—the Theater District, Chinatown, Haunted Lot District, and Plaza District—each of which has its own haunt: the Stage Hands in the Theater, Crabbage Pots and Festival Spirits in Chinatown, Shrooms in the Haunted Lot, and Underhands in Plaza. There are also new challenges to give players extra opportunities to earn souls, and there are new Buff Containers, Tough Crates, and Healing Snacks scattered around the map for players to augment their gameplay, gather more souls, and heal up in sticky situations.The in-game UI updates also usher in new health bars that offer a lot more information about the enemy's current status, and there are now clear ally indicators, all of which should help players be more aware of their current status and how viable a confrontation is. Player buff status and stack indicators have also received an update that better communicates to players what they are capable of and what they may want to focus on building more throughout the match.

articles.title: DoorDash's drone strategy started on the ground | TechCrunch
articles.text:
When DoorDash set out to build a drone delivery business, it started with the tricky logistics that happen on the ground before it looked up.
The autonomous drone came last, according to the company, which unveiled its new six-propeller aircraft at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event on Wednesday.
Before DoorDash worked on the aircraft, the company focused on ground infrastructure, including loading systems, how food would be handed off from a restaurant’s kitchen, and packaging.
DoorDash Labs, the R&D team that built its autonomous sidewalk delivery bot Dot, created the drone delivery service now called DoorDash Air. The same team also developed the underlying software, called the Autonomous Delivery Platform (ADP), to handle the coordination challenges in deliveries handled by humans, sidewalk delivery bots, and now drones.
The ADP software uses smart routing, incorporating factors like weather, flight range, and ground traffic to narrow down which orders actually make sense to send by air.
The company’s systems-first strategy for its DoorDash Air business aligns with its strengths. DoorDash isn’t a hardware company, but it is sitting on 13 years of user data from the merchant and customer sides of the business. (DoorDash has previously disclosed that more than 500,000 restaurants are on its delivery marketplace.)
The company says it sized the whole DoorDash Air system around its historical order data, including how much orders weigh and how far they typically travel.
“We didn’t start with a drone and ask what would fit,” Harrison Shih, who heads up DoorDash Air, said in a statement. “We started with what people order and how local businesses actually operate, then built the entire system from there.”
DoorDash announced plans in July to launch the drone delivery business after receiving a Part 135 air carrier certification from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration. The certification allows the company to legally operate a commercial drone delivery service in the United States.
The drone, which has six slow-spinning propellers mounted at the ends of its arms, is equipped with a winch to pick up, carry, and drop off packages.
DoorDash said it plans to kick off early pilot deliveries in Northern California with partners including Chipotle, Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen, and Momo N Curry.

articles.title: Firefox 157 arrive avec Nova, son plus grand redesign depuis 2021
articles.text:
On connaissait le grand ménage de printemps, mais il faut aussi compter sur la grande refonte de l’automne. En préparation depuis des mois, le nouveau design de Firefox fait ses grands débuts ce mardi 29 septembre 2026, avec la sortie de la version 157 du navigateur web. Et c’est pour Mozilla le plus gros changement esthétique du logiciel depuis des années.
L’interface de Firefox n’avait en effet pas été autant remaniée depuis bien 5 ans.
Sur son blog, l’équipe présente Nova comme le plus gros bond visuel depuis Proton, arrivé avec Firefox 89 en 2021. Ce design n’avait pas plu à tout le monde cependant ; des utilisateurs lui reprochaient des onglets énormes et trop d’espace perdu. Mozilla avait en plus caché le mode compact, qu’il fallait réactiver à la main dans les réglages avancés.
Que change le nouveau design de Firefox ?
Le nouveau design de Firefox, que Mozilla présente plus en longueur dans un billet de blog dédié, est activé par défaut, sur ordinateur comme sur mobile. Jusqu’ici, on ne le voyait que dans Nightly, la version expérimentale du navigateur. Mozilla assure que les favoris, les extensions et les raccourcis restent à leur place.
Visuellement parlant, Mozilla a profité de ce redesign pour redessiner les couleurs, les icônes, les thèmes, les onglets, les barres d’outils, la page Nouvel onglet et la navigation privée. L’ordinateur et le mobile partagent la même identité visuelle désormais. Mozilla promet que ce nouveau look ne ralentit pas Firefox, sans donner de chiffres à l’appui dans son billet.
La mise à jour Nova relance le mode compact, qui fait son retour de façon officielle. Il réduit la taille des onglets et de la barre d’outils pour laisser plus de place aux pages web. Une option l’active toute seule sur les petits écrans. D’après les notes de version, il sert aussi en écran partagé.
Par ailleurs, un nouveau sélecteur permet de parcourir et d’appliquer thèmes et fonds d’écran, avec des variantes intégrées en version claire ou sombre. La page Nouvel onglet, qui affichait déjà des encarts publicitaires en 2014, laisse désormais choisir les éléments affichés et épingler des raccourcis vers les sites qu’on visite le plus.
Nova arrive après une année chargée en nouvelles fonctionnalités : l’affichage de deux pages côte à côte, un VPN intégré et le blocage des traqueurs. Sur Reddit, les utilisateurs de r/firefox discutent déjà du nouveau design dans un fil consacré à l’arrivée de Nova et dans un autre sur le « retour » de Firefox.
Ces changements sont nécessaires pour que Firefox reste à la page, mais en évoluant parfois sur une ligne de crête : il lui faut à la fois satisfaire sa base historique, tout en séduisant une nouvelle communauté. Pas simple face aux autres navigateurs web, et quand sa part de marché est très réduite : 2,98 % des pages vues dans le monde en août, selon StatCounter.
La mise à jour, qui corrige aussi des failles de sécurité, s’installe automatiquement. Pour la forcer, ouvrez le menu Aide, puis À propos de Firefox. Si la nouvelle barre latérale, activée pour tous, ne vous plaît pas, passez le réglage sidebar.revamp à false dans about:config pour retrouver l’ancienne, ce qui désactive aussi les onglets verticaux. Mozilla laissera cette option jusqu’à la fin de 2027.

articles.title: StuckInProfit, AFAZ partner on Africa–Azerbaijan enterprise development pilot - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
African SME-focused business education company StuckInProfit has partnered with the Africa–Azerbaijan Cooperation (AFAZ) to launch a three-week virtual professional and enterprise development programme, to kick off in November.
The StuckInProfit × AFAZ Professional & Enterprise Development Programme 2026 will see participants coached by a network of AFAZ instructors across 11 areas, including project presentation, emotional intelligence, leadership, virtual collaboration, time management, finance for non-finance professionals, entrepreneurship, critical thinking, creativity and intercultural communication.
The programme’s instructors are drawn largely from Azerbaijan’s academic, corporate and development sectors. They include ADA University senior instructor Aygün Mammadova, international development specialist Nadir Guluzade, former Ministry of Economy official Natig Madatov, and Hokuma Karimova, director of public relations and corporate communications at Nar (Azerfon).
Beyond the pilot, the partners say the longer-term goal is to build practical bridges between African entrepreneurs, SMEs and professional talent and international ecosystems through education, capacity development and market knowledge.

articles.title: Venu Srinivasan flags governance lapses, seeks probe into Tata Trusts: Report
articles.text:
Venu Srinivasan flags governance lapses, seeks probe into Tata Trusts: Report
A media report said Venu Srinivasan has asked the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner to inquire into the governance of two Tata Trusts and their role in Tata Sons, amid an ongoing tussle between the two entities.
Venu Srinivasan, a member of two Tata Trusts and also of Tata Sons, has asked the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner to inquire into the governance structure of the Trust, according to a media report.
A report in The Economic Times said, Srinivasan had alleged serious governance lapses in the Trusts and also its involvement in Tata Sons, which is a commercial enterprise. He has also written a letter in this regard to the Charity Commissioner of Maharashtra.
This is the latest missive by a member of the Tata Sons Board in its ongoing tussle with Tata Trusts led by Noel Tata.
The Trusts in question are the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT).
Srinivasan also questioned the appointment and continued status of Noel Tata as a perpetual trustee, the basis of his chairmanship of Tata Trusts. On the other hand, Tata Trusts holds 66% stake in Tata Sons.
Meanwhile, Tata Trusts had on Monday outlined a reorganisation of Tata Sons, the holding company of Tata Group companies which when given effect would ensure it would neither be a non-banking financial company or a core investment company.
A statement from Tata Trusts said it has already written to the Tata Sons Board to consider and approve the proposal. It further asked Tata Sons board to take necessary steps including applying to the Reserve Bank of India for the necessary “no-objection certificate” for the reorganisation.
Tata Trust said the proposed reorganisation essentially entails the merger of “Tata Electronics Systems Solutions Private Limited’ (TESS) and ‘Tata Consulting Engineers ‘(TCE) with Tata Sons.
The Trust also noted that along with Tata Sons, it will engage with the RBI on all aspects of the proposed reorganisation.
The ongoing tussle between Noel Tata and Tata Sons has taken a ugly turn. Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran reversed his decision of not seeking reappointment and Board overwhelmingly voted for his continuation with sole opposition from Noel Tata.

articles.title: Samsung unveils new Galaxy Tab S12 tablet series and smaller Galaxy SmartTag 3 trackers - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Samsung has unveiled its new Galaxy Tab S12 series – Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Tab S12+ – the most capable tablets it has ever created with outstanding performance, longer battery life, and the latest Galaxy AI onboard.
Samsung has also revealed its Galaxy Smart Tag 3 – it’s new tracker which is smaller and lighter with longer range finding.
SAMSUNG GALAXY TAB S12 SERIES – From $1,999
The Samsung Galaxy Tabs include their signature ultra-thin design and the power and performance to run complex workflows to satisfy all your productivity and creativity needs.
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and the Tab S12+ feature bright immersive displays and come with the ergonomically designed S Pen for easy notetaking and precision editing.
The Tab S12 Ultra has a 14.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display while the Tab S12+ features a 12.6-inch screen.
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is just 5.1 mm thick and supports your productivity for the entire day whether you’re working in an office, at a café or on your commute.
It has been engineered for durability with an IP68 rating for water and dust resistance.
Both models have ultra-long battery life with the Tab S12 Ultra lasting up to 23 hours and the Galaxy Tab S12+ up to 21 hours.
Under the hood is a new 3D vapour chamber to dissipate heat and promote more reliable performance during demanding tasks.
And on the audio side the new Samsung tablets have four-channel spatial audio, twice as many as the previous model, to deliver a more immersive experience while streaming content or playing games.
The Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 series is running Android 17 with One UI 9, as well as the latest Galaxy AI.
Users can turn the tablet into a professional workstation with the Pro keyboard, which has a premium aluminium finish and a dedicated Galaxy AI key for instant access to AI assistance.
The Book Cover Keyboard Slim is another accessory to offer flexibility with comfortable viewing and easy typing.
Customers will receive a 6-month trial of Google AI Pro when they purchase the Samsung tablet for expanded access to Google’s capable AI models.
The Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 series will go on sale on October 22.
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra will be priced from $2,299 while the Galaxy Tab S12 Plus will start at $1,999.
SAMSUNG GALAXY SMARTTAG 3
The Samsung Galaxy Smart Tag 3 is 35 per cent smaller by volume and 33 per cent lighter than the previous model, which makes it even easier to attach to keys, bags and luggage and even a pet’s collar.
It now has a more rounded form factor and finish with an aluminium button for a more durable look and feel.
And for the first time the Galaxy Smart Tag 3 offers cross-OS compatibility for Galaxy and iOS devices to make it even easier for families and groups to access finding and sharing features across platforms.
And when Galaxy SmartTag 3 moves outside of direct connection range, the Galaxy Find network helps keep the search going thanks to more than 900 million participating Galaxy devices around the world, which act as finding nodes to help detect the Galaxy Smart Tag 3 and update its location.
The Samsung Galaxy Smart Tab 3 will be available in Australia in early 2027 in black and white.

articles.title: L'application Téléphone de Google fait machine arrière sur l'un des changements les plus controversés
articles.text:
L’an dernier, la firme de Mountain View avait surpris pas mal d’utilisateurs en éjectant cet onglet de la barre principale de son application Téléphone pour le reléguer dans le menu latéral. Une décision qui n’avait pas vraiment fait l’unanimité. Heureusement, la dernière version bêta de l’application vient corriger le tir, même si tout le monde n’y a pas encore droit.
Le grand retour du bouton Contacts dans l’application Téléphone
Repéré dans le code de la dernière version bêta (version 240.0.98) de l’application Google Téléphone sur un Pixel 9, l’onglet réapparaît sagement entre l’historique des appels et le pavé numérique. Un soulagement pour ceux qui en avaient assez de fouiller dans les menus pour retrouver un numéro et qui finissaient sûrement par ouvrir l’application Contacts.
Source : Android Authority
Malgré cette mise à jour, la transition prend son temps et ressemble à un déploiement progressif en plusieurs vagues. Impossible de deviner quand Google généralisera le retour du bouton à l’ensemble des utilisateurs de la version stable de l’application. Sur la version stable que nous avons sur un Pixel 10, il n’y a toujours que deux onglets en bas et un accès aux contacts via le menu hamburger en haut à gauche.
Comment retrouver l’onglet Contacts plus rapidement
Pour forcer un peu le destin, les plus impatients peuvent tenter de télécharger et d’installer manuellement la dernière bêta publique de l’application depuis des plateformes comme APKMirror. Mais attention, même avec cette version, le résultat varie et certains mobiles refusent toujours de réafficher le fameux bouton.
© 01net
En attendant le déploiement de la version stable, le meilleur moyen de trouver un contact sur l’application Téléphone est d’utiliser le filtre « Contacts » qui se trouve sous l’onglet de recherche pour n’afficher que les personnes enregistrées dans votre carnet d’adresses. Google montre tout de même qu’à force de retours négatifs, l’entreprise peut faire machine arrière.

articles.title: Rockstar ha confirmado lo enorme que es GTA VI. Ahora sabemos que quiere evitar el gran problema de los mundos abiertos
articles.text:
El mundo abierto de GTA VI prometía ser grande. Enorme. Mucho mayor que el de sus predecesores: el mapa con la mayor superficie desarrollado por Rockstar. Ya habíamos podido anticipar esa extensión en los primeros 27 minutos de gameplay, aunque nos faltaban datos oficiales. Los ha dado Aaron Garbut, codirector de Rockstar North y jefe de desarrollo.
El doble de superficie que GTA V. Si robar pedir prestado un coche, e ir de una punta a otra del GTA V, ya era una tarea para la que hacía falta una buena cantidad de minutos, Garbut ha confirmado a Game Informer que el terreno disponible en GTA VI hará más largos los trayectos de extremo a extremo. El nuevo mapa tendrá el doble de superficie que el de GTA V y una densidad de interiores sin precedentes. No solo eso: superará el mundo abierto de GTA 5 en numerosos apartados técnicos y jugables, palabrita de Aaron Garbut.
Las primeras filtraciones e imágenes oficiales del juego anticipaban un mapa gigantesco. Es lo lógico tratándose de una secuela. El problema es que tamaño no es sinónimo de diversión, que se lo pregunten a Ubisoft: los Assassin’s Creed poseen mapas enormes donde no siempre hay alicientes para perderse en ellos.
Las estimaciones apuntaban alto. El codirector de Rockstar North ha confirmado en Game Informer que el estado ficticio de Leonida, que compartirá protagonismo con Vice City, es, "con diferencia", el mapa más extenso de toda la trayectoria del estudio.
Aunque Garbut no desveló cifras concretas, los 83,218 km² estimados inicialmente por la comunidad para la masa de tierra podrían verse rebasados. Ignoramos, eso sí, contra qué ha comparado Garbut: si con el área terrestre efectiva o con el total del escenario, incluyendo el mar navegable que rodea las costas.
El mapa no lo es todo. Ya comentaba que en el mundo abierto lo más importante no es el tamaño de la superficie por donde puedes perderte, sino todo lo que haya por hacer en ese terreno. Según explica el codirector de Rockstar North, los escenarios han crecido en posibilidades:
"Nos obsesionamos con cada parte: los tejados, los callejones, los interiores y todo lo que hay entre medias, hasta alcanzar una masa crítica en el número de interiores. Es entonces cuando empiezas a sentir que los edificios son más reales por dentro y por fuera”.
“El mundo funciona como un conjunto orgánico y cohesionado gracias a la densidad del contenido y a la calidad artesanal de cada rincón".
¿Un huracán en GTA? Un huracán en GTA. Game Informer también ha obtenido datos jugosos de otros aspectos del juego, como la meteorología: Jason y Lucía sufrirán el envite de huracanes y de tormentas tropicales. Y no estarán precisamente solos: Leonida contará con más de 170 especies animales, entre ellas manatíes, flamencos, pelícanos y caimanes. Florida en versión Rockstar promete tener vida hasta debajo de las piedras.
Rockstar se ha puesto como meta ofrecer un ecosistema mucho más interactivo y minucioso que el de sus anteriores títulos. A falta de poder probarlo de primera mano, algo para lo que queda aún algo más de mes y medio, tendremos que conformarnos con el trailer extendido.

articles.title: AI's Third Wave: Coworkers Break the Security Model That Worked for Agents
articles.text:
An AI agent borrows your credentials. An AI coworker never gives them back.
By Itamar Apelblat, Co-Founder and CEO, Token Security
We no longer have the luxury of adapting to change over several years. The fundamental shift in AI-driven work keeps morphing month after month, so much so that in just three years we've already experienced distinct waves of work-related AI, and another one is no longer on the horizon but right around the corner.
First came the session-scoped chats, where the risk was what the model says. Then came task-scoped agents, where the risk is in what the model does. Broadly speaking, that's where we are now, but the goalposts are already elsewhere. Truly persistent AI coworkers are nearly here, and with them, the dissolution of current access models.
As with so much in this space, you can see that's where the AI companies want to go by their vocabulary. Microsoft talks about agents as "digital colleagues," and OpenAI's Sam Altman outlined the plan for virtual co-workers what seems like a lifetime ago, in February 2025.
That vision is now becoming a reality, and we need to adapt our security models to address fundamental differences in how AI colleagues work.
Persistence changes everything
You should plan for this sooner rather than later. For a few years, we were able to pigeonhole AI into existing access models, but a "true" coworker that works independently requires a different way of thinking.
Agentic co-workers will require access front-loading or a more machine-friendly (yet secure) way of provisioning it, as approving actions on a case-by-case basis only works if there's a human available to review. True digital co-workers can't rely on regular approvals for everything but should be able to request additional access when it's needed for their tasks.
Currently, provisioning identities purpose-built for AI agents is still far from being the norm. The standard is to use OAuth grants, in-session hand-offs, and service accounts. The first two options usually place humans as the primary entity; the third one is rarely created specifically for agents.
Persistence leads to a different risk profile for the digital co-worker's credentials in yet another respect. They're essentially becoming a standing privilege, same as with people. We'll need to address their lifecycle, including the all-important deprovisioning step, to ensure security.
And consider access creep. If a digital co-worker is persistent, it's bound to accumulate access from different projects. For humans, access creep is the oldest unsolved problem in identity governance. For machines, it's bound to be much worse, both because of the speed with which access will accumulate and the agentic propensity to use all access they're given. Agents can combine several reasonable grants into an overall reach that no one intended to give them.
Beyond The Checkbox
Your SOC 2 report says the controls worked, but it never says what they missed. Agents run on borrowed credentials, with no owner and no off switch.
Token Security finds every agent, assigns it an identity, and remediates its access to the job it was intended to do.
Find your agents
Everyone will need to adapt
Businesses aren't the only ones that will need to adapt to the third wave of agentic workflows. For now, the two most widely deployed agent platforms do not issue agents their own credentials. Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI run the OAuth client credentials grant in their hosted chat products, while ChatGPT connectors reject service accounts and JWT assertions outright.
Both do allow a developer to hand an agent a static bearer token via their APIs, but that’s far from a proper identity.
As a result, not only do AI systems hold full standing privileges that were right-sized for humans, but the logs are also tainted. When AI acts under its user-granted privileges, the human is usually recorded as the actor in any audit trail.
The desire to keep a human in the loop doesn't just impact AI; it also creates a burden on people. OAuth assumes a human will read a consent screen and approve a fixed list of scopes. Agents are rarely satisfied with their initial access; they discover tools at runtime and attempt to use them.
Confirming sensitive actions every few minutes is both annoying and a security risk, since there's only so much attention to go around.
The people building coworkers are explicit about what they need
Tara Seshan, who leads product for ChatGPT Work and Codex at OpenAI, described what actually makes an agent useful on Lenny's Podcast in August 2026.
Model intelligence is only part of it. The rest comes down to what she described as "meat and potatoes tactical" work: access to data, cloud infrastructure, and reliability.
Her analogy was this: you hire a colleague and then lock them in a room with no access to Google Docs, Slack, or the company database. That colleague is not going to be effective. An isolated cloud agent, she argued, is useless for the same reason.
She is right about the requirement. The route to a useful coworker runs through the same systems a human employee touches.
Seshan also described her agent spawning sub-agents to parallelize work, and a near future where her agents and her colleagues' agents collaborate on shared tasks. Both are reasonable directions that assume an identity model that does not exist.
When one person's agent hands work to another person's agent, the credential that executes belongs to whichever human happened to start the chain.
Google built the right model in 2024. It never shipped.
At I/O in May 2024, Google demoed a Workspace agent named Chip. Chip had its own Workspace account, a designated role, configured permissions, and a stated set of objectives. It joined chat rooms and answered from the history it could see.
Workspace VP Aparna Pappu said at the time that Google had a lot of work to do before "agentive" experiences, such as virtual teammates, could reach the product. Chip stayed a demo.
What Google (and all its competitors) shipped instead are agents where the coworker inherits a human's authority.
What to do about it
The platform vendors have started adapting. Microsoft shipped Entra Agent ID with first-class agent identities and a named human sponsor. Okta added agent identities to Universal Directory, with short-lived, scoped tokens and a revocation path. SailPoint and CyberArk have comparable offerings. The downside is that each secures agents inside its own estate.
If you want to be platform-agnostic, identity controls are the only de facto checkpoint at which you can enforce policies, since identity governs access to every action. Here are five things you should do:
- Find the shadow coworkers. Registration only captures agents that someone remembered to register. Detect them by their authentication traffic.
- Give every persistent agent an identity of its own. If it authenticates as human, no downstream control can distinguish the two, and no investigation can correctly attribute an action.
- Record a human owner. Orphaned agents with live credentials are the most common source of agent-related standing privileges.
- Scope access to the agent rather than to the person who started it. An agent that reads Jira should not hold a token that also writes to your cloud provider just because the engineer who launched it happened to have both.
- Decide in advance when it dies. Digital coworkers aren't project-based, so they aren't tied to them, but that doesn't mean you should scope them as immortal. Let's say a team they're "a part of" gets disbanded, or the employee who's responsible for an agent is let go. Write those conditions down when you create the agent, along with an idle period after which it expires on its own.
What the third wave asks of you
For wave one, where the risk was driven by the model's output, we had prompt filtering, guardrails, and output classification. For wave two, with action-based risk and a human-in-the-loop process, the focus was on access controls and approvals. Wave three takes the human away and leaves the access in place.
The pressure is about to rise. Seshan's account has agents that spawn sub-agents and collaborate across teams. One person's coworker might soon hand work to another person's coworker. Those handoffs are governable only if the coworker holds an identity of its own. In other words, give it a badge before you give it a job.
For us at Token, we’re already identifying the AI agents and MCP servers running in your environment, including those nobody registered, based on their OAuth grants, API keys, and login traffic. We’re giving each agent its own identity and a human owner, scopes and rotates its credentials, and retires it when the owner leaves or it sits idle.
Token Security covers your cloud and SaaS systems as a whole, not just one vendor's.
Book a Token demo to see how many of your agents are running on borrowed human credentials.

articles.title: Government, Finance Orgs Targeted in Weeks-Long NetScaler Zero-Day Attacks
articles.text:
Google’s Mandiant and Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) have published details on attacks exploiting the NetScaler zero-days that Citrix patched over the weekend.
The vulnerabilities are tracked as CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, and they affect NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway instances. Attackers can exploit these critical flaws for unauthenticated remote code execution.
Before Citrix released patches, government cybersecurity agencies and security firms took the rare step of urging administrators to disconnect affected NetScaler appliances from the internet immediately while zero-day exploitation investigations were ongoing.
Mandiant and GTIG, whose report focuses on the exploitation of CVE-2026-88772, spotted attacks in late September. However, their investigation found that the zero-day campaign has been “ongoing since at least early September.”
The attacks likely impacted organizations in North America and Europe. These organizations are in the government, financial services, education, legal, and professional services sectors.
The attackers exploited the vulnerability to gain root access to NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances. They then changed the appliance’s web server configuration so they could plant web shells and run them with root privileges.
Mandiant found previously unseen malware in the attacks, including a PHP web shell named WHIPSHOT and a Python-based tunneling tool named SLAPSHOT. The two work together to give the attackers a path from the compromised appliance into the victim’s internal network.
According to Mandiant, the tools enable internal reconnaissance, lateral movement and credential theft. In at least one intrusion, the hackers used the tunnel to manually explore the internal network and steal credentials.
Mandiant also saw signs that the threat actor may be managing similar web shells in multiple compromised environments.
Mandiant CTO Charles Carmakal noted that dozens of organizations have been hit, including by suspected state-sponsored threat actors.
“We expect broad and opportunistic exploitation of CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88771 by a variety of threat actors in the near term,” Carmakal warned.
Cybersecurity expert Kevin Beaumont reported being aware of more than 100 victim organizations as of Tuesday, noting that the attacks appear to be part of an espionage campaign.
Security firm WatchTowr, one of the first to confirm in-the-wild exploitation, has released technical details on both CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88771.
Threat intelligence company GreyNoise observed zero-day exploitation attempts on September 24, several days before the flaws were disclosed and patched.
“The [malicious cyber actor] attempted to set both the Set User ID (setuid) and Set Group ID (setgid) bits on /bin/sh to obtain a root shell and install a password-protected webshell that accepts communication by the cookie value sent by the adversary. This may be to avoid persisting their commands in web logs,” GreyNoise explained.
Palo Alto Networks reported that there had been roughly 50,000 potentially exposed NetScaler instances as of September 27.

articles.title: Brosse à dents Dyson à 479€ : on sait enfin ce qui a provoqué le couac industriel
articles.text:
Retirée de la vente en France dix jours seulement après son lancement, une partie des CameraJet souffre d’un défaut de fabrication pouvant laisser passer de l’eau dans l’appareil. Dyson dit avoir identifié le problème, mais doit désormais rassurer les premiers acheteurs.
Dix jours auront suffi pour transformer un lancement surmédiatisé en sérieux couac industriel. Présentée le 1er septembre à 479 euros, la brosse à dents connectée Dyson CameraJet a vu sa commercialisation suspendue en France dès le 11 septembre. Après avoir évoqué des tensions sur les stocks, la marque avait fini par reconnaître l’existence d’un composant défectueux. Elle précise désormais l’origine du problème.
Une fuite provoquée par un défaut de fabrication
Dans une déclaration transmise à Allure, Dyson met en cause un lot de production de tubes utilisés par le jet interdentaire. Un problème survenu lors de leur fabrication aurait créé un risque d’infiltration d’eau susceptible d’altérer le fonctionnement de certains appareils.
La marque affirme avoir isolé les produits concernés, repris la production à plein régime et commencé à expédier des appareils à ses distributeurs. Elle ne donne toutefois aucune date précise pour leur retour en rayon en France.
Sauf qu'on ne comprend pas comment un problème aussi gênant a pu passer entre les mailles du contrôle qualité. Kyle Wiens, patron d’iFixit, avançait auparavant auprès de Wired plusieurs scénarios possibles, notamment des pièces mal ajustées ou une colle ayant mal polymérisé.
Dans ce dernier cas, un produit peut parfaitement fonctionner au moment des tests, puis se dégrader sous l’effet de la chaleur ou de l’humidité pendant le transport. Dyson n’a toutefois pas confirmé l’une ou l’autre de ces hypothèses.
Des premiers acheteurs à rassurer
Plusieurs propriétaires ont signalé de l’eau à proximité de la batterie, des messages de surchauffe ou des appareils devenus inutilisables peu après leur achat. Ces témoignages ne permettent pas de mesurer l’ampleur exacte du problème et Dyson indique qu’aucun rappel général n’est organisé à ce stade, même si certains confrères ont été surpris de voir le géant anglais récupérer leurs exemplaires de test.
Dans ce genre de situation, en cas de fuite ou d’alerte de température, le plus prudent reste évidemment de cesser d’utiliser la CameraJet et de ne pas la remettre en charge avant d’avoir contacté le vendeur ou le SAV Dyson. Mieux vaut également conserver sa preuve d’achat et le numéro de série de l’appareil.
Des consignes de reprise et de remboursement ont circulé chez certains distributeurs, mais leurs modalités peuvent varier. Pour un appareil acheté directement auprès de Dyson, la marque demande de contacter son service consommateurs.
Pour Dyson, l’affaire tombe particulièrement mal. La CameraJet devait marquer son arrivée spectaculaire dans l’hygiène dentaire après six années de développement et 38 brevets déposés. Si aucun blessé ne semble avoir été signalé à ce stade, voir un produit à 479 euros disparaître des rayons dix jours après son lancement ressemble tout de même à un sérieux crash industriel.

articles.title: Rising Tide Africa commits $1m to Ororo Waste’s UCO expansion
articles.text:
Rising Tide Africa, a women-led pan-African angel investment network, has committed up to ₦1.4 billion ($1 million) to Ororo Waste Management Limited, a Lagos-based used cooking oil (UCO) waste management company, to expand its collection infrastructure and working capital.
Ororo Waste, Lagos State’s partner for institutional-scale UCO collection and export, received the first allocation on September 16, with additional funding potentially available through December 16. The new capital will finance the purchase of used cooking oil from its collector network and cover hub operating costs.
The investment comes as Ororo Waste attempts to scale a business around Nigeria’s used cooking oil waste stream. Nigeria consumes an estimated 1 million tons of vegetable oil and produces about 1.4 million metric tonnes of palm oil annually. However, there is little formal infrastructure to collect and recover used cooking oil after it is discarded, leaving much of the waste stream uncaptured.
Ororo is betting that the oil Nigerians treat as waste can become valuable for global biofuel markets and generate income for the people who collect it.
“Refiners in Europe don’t buy good intentions—they buy documented, ISCC-certified tonnes,” Ayo Banjo, co-chief executive officer (CEO) of Ororo Waste, said in a statement. “Rising Tide’s capital helps fund the unglamorous but necessary part—drums, trucks, hub storage, and the working-capital float that lets us pay a market woman in Alausa the same day she sells to us.”
Founded in 2021, Ororo Waste builds the infrastructure to collect and export used cooking oil. The company is certified under the International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) system as a collector and exporter of used cooking oil from households, markets, restaurants and other institutional generators. The company says its collection platform uses Global Positioning System (GPS) and quick response (QR) codes to track oil from the collector to the export container.
Ororo Waste said the new capital will finance its expansion beyond its three existing collection hubs in Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt to more than 40 hubs across Nigeria over the next five years.
The investment also establishes a development-impact partnership between Ororo and Rising Tide Africa, with both parties agreeing to track how the expansion affects the people participating in the collection network, the statement said.
Under the preliminary five-year targets, Ororo Waste wants to grow its formally paid collector network from roughly 5,000 people today to more than 200,000 by 2031. It also plans to increase certified UCO collection from the few thousand metric tonnes it has exported to date to more than 150,000 tonnes annually by 2031.
“Market women and waste pickers already do most of the collecting. Few have ever been paid fairly for that work, and even fewer at scale,” said Yemi Keri, co-founder of Rising Tide Africa. “Our capital helps fund the infrastructure that pays those women the same day, for a commodity that some of the world’s largest offtakers are already contracted to buy.”
The investment builds on work Ororo began in Lagos in July with the Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency, Shell Foundation and the Waste Pickers Association of Nigeria (WAPAN). The organisations trained roughly 250 market women, waste pickers and youths at the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry on the safe collection, handling and storage of used cooking oil. The programme was part of a partnership between Ororo and the Lagos State government to expand household used cooking oil collection through LASEPA’s zonal offices.
Ororo Waste’s fundraise comes as African climate-tech companies turn locally produced waste into an economic resource. In September, Nigerian climate-tech startup Biochar Industrial Group raised $1.5 million to convert agricultural waste from food-processing factories into biochar and carbon-removal credits.
Ororo Waste expects to complete a baseline income survey of the first formally onboarded collector cohort from the July training by the end of 2026. It plans to use the results to track income and employment outcomes for participating women, waste pickers and young people, alongside the gender composition of its workforce and leadership, as part of its environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting.
“We are very honoured to be in a position to deploy infrastructure that will offer dignified incomes to several hundred thousand women, at a minimum,” Banjo said.

articles.title: Container Apps Express Reaches GA on a Newly Generally Available Sandbox Layer
articles.text:
Microsoft recently made Azure Container Apps Express generally available, a deployment model that removes the environment provisioning step and replaces most configuration with opinionated defaults. It ships alongside the general availability of Azure Container Apps Sandboxes, the isolated compute layer Express runs on. The pairing follows the same shape Google shipped in Kubernetes Engine this year.
Express takes a container image, a region, and whatever configuration the app needs, then provisions the compute, ingress, and scaling itself. Apps run on consumption CPU with per-second billing, scale to zero when idle, and carry no environment provisioning fee. Microsoft describes Express as developer-first and agent-first, and makes the second part explicit:
AI-assisted workflows can create and update apps far faster than anyone can configure infrastructure by hand.
The speed comes from underneath. Microsoft's documentation states that Express is built entirely on Container Apps Sandboxes, a platform primitive that provisions from prewarmed pools for subsecond startup, isolates each workload in its own hardware-isolated microVM boundary, and bursts to thousands of concurrent sandboxes. Sandboxes also support suspend and resume, snapshotting full state including memory and disk, with sub-second restore.
Developers can use Sandboxes directly rather than through Express, which Microsoft positions for agent platforms and secure code-execution services. The top-level ARM resource is Microsoft.App/SandboxGroups, described as a management boundary for sandboxes sharing configuration, comparable to a Container Apps environment.
Reaction on Reddit suggests the primitive was in use well before the announcement. Commenter MuhBlockchain offered a detail Microsoft's own material does not state:
ACA Sandboxes actually underpin a lot of core Azure services including Foundry Hosted Agents.
Others described their own deployments. Commenter tankerkiller125real wrote that his team uses them for Python sandboxes for a customer facing agent harness. Commenter Minute_Passion_8077 described deploying them for clients through Bicep:
Just point it to an image and off you go. Dont need it? Scale to 0.
Asked how Sandboxes differ from Container Apps jobs, commenter brianveldman drew the line at lifecycle:
ACA Jobs are designed for run to completion tasks and batch processing (start to run to complete), while Sandboxes provide programmable, isolated compute environments with lifecycle control.
Not everyone was convinced by the isolation claim. Commenter RustOnTheEdge responded to the hardware-isolated microVM description with open skepticism, though without elaborating. One question went unanswered: commenter HgnX asked whether the same capability is available in Azure Kubernetes Service, noting that his team runs AKS because of requirements Container Apps does not meet.
That combination is recognizable. Google Kubernetes Engine pairs Pod snapshots, which checkpoint CPU and GPU memory through gVisor, with GKE Agent Sandbox for running untrusted agent code. Microsoft now pairs microVM isolation with snapshot-based suspend and resume, aimed at the same workloads. Both vendors are answering the same question: how to give an agent an isolated environment that costs nothing while idle and returns in under a second.
Express itself is the opinionated application layer on top, offering a focused subset of Container Apps capabilities: scale to zero, multiple replicas, HTTP ingress on a Microsoft-managed domain, environment variables, manual secrets, IP restrictions, log streaming, and autoscaling on HTTP, CPU, or memory rules.
The exclusions define where it stops. Express does not support custom domains, zone redundancy, Key Vault secret references, Easy Auth, OpenTelemetry, Dapr, jobs, workload profiles, GPU workloads, multiple revisions and traffic splitting, or system-assigned managed identities. Service discovery is absent, so apps communicate through their public URLs, and ingress is HTTP only. Microsoft's documentation carries the full list, along with constraints on outbound subnets, which cannot be changed once set, and on per-replica storage.
Microsoft is direct about the boundary, advising a standard environment where teams need greater control over networking, GPU compute, advanced configuration, or environment-level capabilities such as Dapr. The documentation nonetheless also lists rapid prototyping as a case where teams build quickly and then keep running in production without replatforming. For a workload needing a custom domain, zone redundancy, or Key Vault-backed secrets, those two statements pull in different directions.
Access is also narrower than standard Container Apps. Express requires a Microsoft Entra ID-backed account, and personal Microsoft accounts are not supported. Management happens through specialist interfaces rather than the Azure portal: containerapps.azure.com for Container Apps and sandboxes.azure.com for Sandboxes. Asked whether those replace the portal, MuhBlockchain said they do not:
It's just a separate view, though with a lot more detail. You'll still be able to manage them through the regular portal experience to.
Teams already running standard environments have a migration path, and a nudge. Self-migration works through archive and restore: archive the existing environment, then restore it as an Express environment. Microsoft says the process preserves app and environment configuration, takes about 15 minutes, and does not change the consumption-free grant. The FAQ also mentions an opt-out form in the migration notice for organizations needing additional approval or coordination, and notes that inactive environments, meaning those with no running apps or jobs and no recent activity, may be archived and put to sleep.
At general availability, Express reaches more than 40 Azure regions, covering almost every public region where Container Apps is offered. Microsoft says thousands of Express apps were created during public preview, and that customer feedback set the priorities for this release.

articles.title: AMD's new Zen 6 Epyc Venice lineup starts at $700 and scales all the way to 256 cores for $14,900
articles.text:
First look: AMD is pricing its upcoming Epyc 9006 Venice server processors from $700 to $14,904, covering systems from small single-socket servers to dual-socket machines with 512 Zen 6 CPU cores. The lineup is built around two platforms with different priorities: SP7 for maximum memory bandwidth and capacity, and SP8 for systems that need more PCIe connectivity. The pricing list includes 31 processors ranging from the eight-core Epyc 9106 to the 256-core Epyc 9996.
AMD has not finalized the prices, but the list offers a clearer view of how it intends to position Venice in the data center.
The Epyc 9996 is the top model in the lineup. It has 256 cores and a list price of $14,904. Two installed in a dual-socket SP7 server would provide 512 Zen 6 cores, though the processors alone would cost $29,808 before memory, storage, networking and accelerators are added.
At that level, the price is not far from the previous-generation 192-core Epyc 9965, which launched at about $14,800. Venice changes the value calculation, however. The 256-core chip works out to about $58.21 per core. The 64-core Epyc 9556, priced at $8,008, costs about $125.12 per core. That makes the largest parts more attractive for customers trying to consolidate workloads or increase compute density in a limited number of servers.
SP7 is AMD's high-end Venice platform. It supports up to 16 memory channels and can use DDR5 RDIMMs or MRDIMMs at speeds up to DDR5-12800. It also provides up to 96 PCIe 6.0 lanes. The processors designed for the socket have thermal design power ratings from 400W to 600W.
The platform is meant for workloads that need a large pool of memory and high memory throughput, including virtualization, databases and analytics. It supports both one- and two-socket systems.
AMD is also offering high-frequency models for workloads that benefit more from clock speed than from very high core counts. The 64-core Epyc 9586F and the 96-core Epyc 9686F can boost to 5 GHz. The trade-off is price and power use. The 64-core 9586F is priced close to the 96-core Epyc 9656 even though it has fewer cores, and its TDP is 100W higher.
The lower-cost SP8 platform takes a different route. It has eight memory channels and does not support MRDIMMs, so it cannot match SP7's peak memory capacity or bandwidth. It does, however, offer 128 PCIe 6.0 lanes, compared with 96 on SP7.
That extra I/O could matter in servers built around GPUs, AI accelerators, high-speed networking cards or dense NVMe storage. SP8 parts are also rated from 130W to 400W, giving system builders more options for lower-power configurations.
The SP8 lineup begins with the $700 eight-core Epyc 9106 and tops out with the 128-core Epyc 9746 at $11,679. It also includes "P" models limited to single-socket systems. Those parts offer the same CPU performance as comparable standard versions at a lower price because they do not support two-socket configurations. AMD lists the 128-core Epyc 9736P at a price 6% lower than the regular Epyc 9736, while the 32-core Epyc 9356P is 26% cheaper than its non-P counterpart.
One of the more specialized chips is the 16-core Epyc 9176F. It has a 5 GHz boost clock and 192MB of L3 cache, or 12MB per core. That's four times the cache of the 16-core Epyc 9116. It also costs more than three times as much. The design appears aimed at customers that need strong per-core performance and large cache capacity while keeping core counts low, which can be important for software licensed by the core.
AMD expects SP7 Venice systems to arrive in the fourth quarter, with SP8 systems due in the first half of 2027. A Venice-X family using AMD's 3D V-Cache technology is expected later in 2027, with up to 96 cores and 1,152MB of cache.

articles.title: Aprender inglés tiene un truco sencillo: cambiar el idioma del celular, la aplicaciones y más
articles.text:
Querer aprender un idioma implica mucho más que asistir a las clases y seguir las guías de un profesor. Este proceso requiere un cambio de hábitos que ayuden a tener un entorno que permita entender mejor el idioma y los recursos digitales son una gran opción
Andrés Prieto, experto en enseñanza de idiomas, recomienda cambiar “el idioma de tu móvil durante más de 24 horas, ese es el verdadero compromiso”, aseguró en uno de los últimos episodios de Focus On Podcast.
PUBLICIDAD
La idea no se limita al teléfono: incluye aplicaciones, relojes inteligentes, plataformas de streaming y asistentes de voz.
Por qué funciona cambiar el idioma del celular
Según Prieto, el error habitual es tratar el inglés como una materia escolar que se memoriza para un examen. “Los métodos tradicionales de la academia nos enseñaban a memorizar cosas para el examen, pero eso no sirve para nada. Por eso, muchos entienden inglés, pero no lo hablan”, explicó.
Cambiar el idioma del celular obliga a identificar patrones de forma constante: cómo se construyen las frases, cuáles se repiten en el uso diario. “Esos patrones se te van a grabar en la cabeza. Eso es lo más importante en el inglés, más que aprender reglas infinitas o memorizar”, sostuvo el divulgador.
PUBLICIDAD
Exponerse al inglés todos los días mediante el teléfono ayuda a memorizar frases de uso frecuente sin estudiar gramática de forma aislada, porque el cerebro absorbe patrones repetidos en contextos reales como notificaciones, menús o mensajes cotidianos.
El experto también destacó el papel de la música como refuerzo de esa exposición diaria. “Yo me levanto todos los días y pongo música en inglés y la canto. Cantar ayuda muchísimo a desarrollar el ritmo del inglés”, afirmó.
Sobre las aplicaciones específicas de aprendizaje, Prieto fue claro respecto a sus límites. “No soy enemigo de las aplicaciones, creo que ayudan, pero la única forma de conseguirlo es hablando con otras personas o chateando”, indicó.
PUBLICIDAD
En la misma línea, el British Council compara aprender un idioma con aprender a nadar o a tocar un instrumento: una habilidad que solo se desarrolla con práctica activa, no con el estudio aislado de vocabulario y gramática.
Cómo cambiar el idioma en Android
Los nombres exactos pueden variar según la marca del dispositivo, pero la ruta general es la siguiente:
- Abrir Configuración desde el ícono de la rueda dentada en el menú de aplicaciones.
- Ingresar a Sistema o Administración general y desplazarse hacia abajo hasta encontrar esa opción.
- Seleccionar Idiomas y entrada y tocar el menú de Idiomas.
- Presionar Agregar un idioma, buscar English y elegir la región preferida, generalmente United States o United Kingdom.
- Mantener presionado el idioma inglés y arrastrarlo hasta la posición número uno de la lista. El sistema aplicará el cambio de forma automática.
Cómo cambiar el idioma en iPhone
En dispositivos con iOS, el proceso parte desde los ajustes generales del sistema:
- Abrir Configuración desde el ícono gris de engranaje en la pantalla de inicio.
- Desplazarse hacia abajo y seleccionar General.
- Tocar Idioma y región para ver los ajustes vigentes.
- Tocar Agregar idioma, buscar English y seleccionarlo.
- Confirmar el cambio al tocar Usar inglés cuando el sistema pregunte qué idioma se prefiere usar como principal. La pantalla se reiniciará brevemente mientras se aplica el ajuste.
Cómo ajustar el idioma en aplicaciones específicas
Por defecto, la mayoría de las aplicaciones cambia automáticamente al inglés en cuanto se modifica el idioma principal del celular. Sin embargo, existe la opción de mantener el teléfono en español y ajustar solo algunas apps, o corregir aquellas que no cambiaron de forma automática.
PUBLICIDAD
En iPhone, iOS permite configurar el idioma de cada aplicación por separado sin afectar el resto del sistema:
- Ir a Configuración.
- Desplazarse hasta el final, donde aparece la lista completa de aplicaciones.
- Tocar la aplicación que se quiera modificar, como WhatsApp o Instagram.
- Seleccionar English dentro de la sección Preferred Language.
En Android, el ajuste se realiza desde el menú interno de cada aplicación:
WhatsApp:
- Abrir WhatsApp y tocar los tres puntos ubicados arriba a la derecha.
- Entrar en Settings.
- Seleccionar App language.
- Elegir English.
Instagram:
- Abrir el perfil y tocar el menú de tres líneas ubicado arriba a la derecha.
- Ingresar a Settings and privacy.
- Buscar la opción Language.
- Seleccionar English.
Facebook:
- Abrir el menú de tres líneas.
- Entrar en Settings & Privacy.
- Ingresar a Settings.
- Tocar Language and region y cambiar el idioma de botones y títulos a English.
Google Maps:
- Abrir la aplicación y tocar la foto de perfil.
- Ingresar a Settings.
- Seleccionar App language.
- Elegir English.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Google annonce Gemini 4 Argon et affirme battre GPT-6 et Opus 5.5
articles.text:
Face à GPT-6 Astra, lancé le 3 septembre, et à Claude Opus 5.5, sorti le 22 septembre, Google faisait pâle figure avec son Gemini 3.1 Pro. Ce mercredi 30 septembre à 22h, la firme a levé le voile sur son nouveau modèle haut de gamme. Google saute le Gemini 3.5 Pro et passe directement à Gemini 4 Argon. Le modèle n’a pas de date de sortie, mais Google le donne premier sur 12 des 18 tests qu’il a publiés.
Pendant ces dix derniers mois, Google a surtout sorti des modèles Flash, plus petits et moins chers. Gemini 3.8 Flash, lancé le 2 septembre, était déjà le troisième en six semaines, et deux modèles de synthèse vocale ont suivi le 23 septembre. Par contre, Google a abandonné le Gemini 3.5 Pro qu’il avait promis.
Argon fait-il vraiment mieux que GPT-6 et Claude ?
Selon les chiffres de Google, oui, dans la plupart des cas. Sur 18 tests, Argon arrive premier sur 12 et à égalité sur un. GPT-6 Astra, d’OpenAI, en remporte trois, et Claude Opus 5.5, d’Anthropic, deux.
DeepSWE v1.1 mesure la capacité à mener de longues tâches de développement logiciel. Sur ce test, Argon obtient 77,9 %, contre 74,2 % pour Claude Opus 5.5 et 74,1 % pour GPT-6 Astra. En revanche, GPT-6 Astra garde 10,5 points d’avance sur FrontierSWE v2, un autre test de programmation. Claude Opus 5.5 devance aussi Argon de 9 points sur Terminal-bench 4.0, qui évalue le travail en ligne de commande.
Il faut creuser dans le billet de blog pour avoir un peu plus de détails sur Gemini 4 Argon. C’est un modèle beaucoup plus volumineux que les précédents conçu pour le raisonnement approfondi et l’exécution de tâches complexes à long terme.
Google affirme l’utiliser déjà en interne. Des agents Argon (des IA qui enchaînent seules plusieurs actions) ont par exemple retravaillé libgav1, le décodeur vidéo open source de Google. D’après l’entreprise, la nouvelle version tourne 2,7 fois plus vite que la version précédente, écrite dans le même langage de programmation.
Il démontre des performances de pointe dans des flux de travail complexes, la défense cybernétique et l’ingénierie logicielle. Les équipes l’utilisent de manière intensive chez Google, de la programmation à l’informatique quantique, avec d’excellents retours.
Traduction du message de Sundar Pichai sur X
Google destine Argon à trois usages : la programmation sur de longues tâches, le travail de bureau spécialisé comme le juridique ou la finance, et la défense informatique. Surtout, le modèle peut produire jusqu’à 1 million de tokens dans une seule réponse, contre 64 000 auparavant, soit environ 15 fois plus. Avec cette marge, Argon peut théoriquement réécrire un gros programme ou rédiger un long dossier juridique en une seule fois, sans s’arrêter en cours de route.
Qui peut l’utiliser, et à quel prix ?
Pour l’instant, Argon est réservé à des experts en cybersécurité sélectionnés par Google dans le cadre de son programme Fairwind. Ils reçoivent une version sans les garde-fous qui bloquent normalement les demandes liées au piratage, pour trouver et corriger des failles. D’après Google, l’entreprise de sécurité Wiz a ainsi découvert une faille critique dans un logiciel médical utilisé par des hôpitaux du monde entier, qui exposait des données personnelles.
Google fait aussi tester Argon dans le cadre d’une démarche volontaire du gouvernement américain, qui peut ainsi examiner les modèles avant leur sortie. Les prochains servis seront les clients payants de l’API (l’accès réservé aux développeurs) et les abonnés Google AI Ultra.
Pour les développeurs, le prix de lancement est de 2 dollars par million de tokens envoyés au modèle et 10 dollars par million de tokens générés (environ 1,75 € et 8,80 € HT). Le tarif de GPT-6 Astra est cinq fois plus élevé, à 10 et 50 dollars. Après cette période, dont Google n’a pas donné la durée, le prix doublera à 4 et 20 dollars (environ 3,50 € et 17,60 € HT), soit le même tarif que Claude Opus 5.5.
Côté grand public, Google promet une sortie « dès que possible », en commençant par les abonnés Google AI Ultra. Aucune date n’a été annoncée pour l’application Gemini.

articles.title: Apple CEO John Ternus Reportedly Plans Faster Product Launches and a Leaner Company
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Apple CEO John Ternus Reportedly Plans Faster Product Launches and a Leaner Company
New Apple CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1, is reportedly planning an overhaul aimed at faster launches and a leaner company, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Ternus, previously Apple's hardware engineering chief, has apparently discussed moving away from the usual spring and fall launch windows and wants the company to be more experimental. Product teams are said to be pushing out more devices on shorter timelines, and one person familiar with the situation described the mood inside as hectic. Moreover, the cuts have already started. 
Apple has reportedly dismissed a number of engineering program managers in hardware engineering over the past two weeks, including roughly half a dozen directors. Some affected staff were given a limited window to find other roles inside Apple, and those who don't will apparently be let go later this year. Apple also reportedly considered cutting about 5,000 AppleCare jobs this summer while looking at AI support agents, but dropped that plan. It's unclear how this affects the October launches rumored for the OLED iPad mini, HomePod mini 2, and Apple TV 4K. Employees reportedly expect more job cuts in the coming months, and they caution that changing how Apple builds products could take years.
