articles.title: Menü-Umbau bei Whatsapp: Meta weicht die Trennung von privaten Chats und Kanälen auf
articles.text:
Menü-Umbau bei Whatsapp: Der Aktuelles-Tab steht offenbar vor dem Aus
Wie das auf Vorabversionen spezialisierte Blog WABetaInfo berichtet, arbeitet Whatsapp intern daran, die sogenannten Kanäle künftig im primären Chats-Tab anzuzeigen, auch wenn die Funktion in den aktuellen Beta-Versionen für externe Tester:innen noch nicht freigeschaltet ist. Bislang waren diese rein sendebasierten Nachrichtenströme von Organisationen strikt von den privaten Unterhaltungen getrennt und in einem separaten Reiter ausgelagert.
Dem Bericht zufolge erprobt Meta aktuell drei unterschiedliche Konfigurationen für diese strukturelle Integration. Ziel der Entwickler:innen ist es offenbar, anhand der laufenden Tests die präferierte Nutzerführung zu ermitteln.
Whatsapp-Beta: Drei verschiedene Ansichten im internen Testlauf
In der ersten Variante tauchen die abonnierten Kanäle direkt in der allgemeinen Chat-Liste auf, wo sie sich zwischen die regulären Unterhaltungen einreihen. Um die Übersicht zu behalten, können die Einträge in diesem Szenario über einen speziellen Filter am oberen Bildschirmrand sortiert werden.
Die zweite Option wählt einen zurückhaltenderen Ansatz, bei dem die Kanäle erst nach der aktiven Anwahl des erwähnten Filters auf dem Display erscheinen. In der Standardansicht des Posteingangs bleiben die Unternehmensnachrichten bei dieser Konfiguration folglich verborgen.
In der dritten Konfiguration integriert das Entwicklerteam einen separaten Ordner für Kanäle direkt innerhalb der Haupt-Chat-Übersicht. Diese Variante würde eine Premiere darstellen, da Whatsapp bislang keine Ordnerstrukturen innerhalb der primären Chat-Liste anbietet.
Updates-Tab: Ein neuer Platz für Kontakte
Unabhängig von der letztlich gewählten Ansicht würde der bisherige Aktuelles-Tab durch den Umzug der Kanäle seinen primären Zweck verlieren. Bisher finden Nutzer:innen dort neben den Kanälen lediglich die Status-Updates ihrer gespeicherten Kontakte.
Beobachter:innen gehen daher davon aus, dass der Reiter im Zuge der Umstellung durch einen neuen Kontakte-Tab ersetzt wird. In diesem neuen Bereich sollen nach aktuellem Kenntnisstand dann Statusanzeigen und Geburtstagserinnerungen gebündelt werden.
Der mögliche Umzug der Kanäle markiert dabei eine konzeptionelle Kehrtwende in der bisherigen Produktstrategie des Messengers. Bei der Einführung der Broadcast-Funktion hatte Meta noch explizit eine andere Herangehensweise kommuniziert.
Meta-Strategie: Abkehr von der strikten Trennung
Der US-Konzern hatte stets versprochen, dass die persönliche Kommunikation mit dem direkten Umfeld strikt von den gewerblichen Inhalten getrennt bleibe. Eine Zusammenlegung in einer einzigen Übersicht bricht diese Grenze nun auf und ordnet die private Kommunikation im selben Reiter wie die Unternehmensnachrichten ein.
Für Betreiber:innen der Kanäle dürfte dieser Schritt die Sichtbarkeit ihrer Inhalte spürbar erhöhen, da Nutzer:innen den primären Chat-Tab weitaus häufiger öffnen. Allerdings besteht die Möglichkeit, dass die private Chat-Übersicht für Anwender:innen dadurch an Übersichtlichkeit einbüßt.
Diese Entwicklung steht im Kontrast zu den bisherigen Aussagen von Meta, den Messenger für den privaten Austausch möglichst werbefrei zu halten. Wie das Unternehmen in seinem hauseigenen Blog erklärte, seien Neuerungen wie beworbene Kanäle und kostenpflichtige Abonnements ganz bewusst in den separaten Aktuelles-Tab ausgelagert worden.
Business-Fokus: Monetarisierung rückt an private Chats heran
Mit dem nun getesteten Umzug rücken die Monetarisierungsfunktionen des Dienstes unweigerlich näher an die private Kommunikation heran. Das Unternehmen hatte zuvor drei neue Einnahmequellen vorgestellt, die auf dem Wachstum der Kanäle basieren.
Dazu gehören Kanalabonnements gegen eine monatliche Gebühr sowie beworbene Kanäle, mit denen Administrator:innen ihre Reichweite gegen Bezahlung erhöhen können. Ergänzt wird dieses Modell durch Anzeigen im Status, die den direkten Kontakt zwischen Nutzer:innen und Unternehmen fördern sollen.
Trotz dieser kommerziellen Ausweitung bleiben die grundlegenden Datenschutzmechanismen der Kanäle, wie sie in den offiziellen Support-Dokumenten beschrieben sind, unangetastet. Die Telefonnummern und Profilbilder der Abonnent:innen sind für die Kanal-Administrator:innen und andere Follower:innen weiterhin nicht sichtbar.
Ebenso bleibt die Kommunikation auf den Kanälen vorerst eine Einbahnstraße, bei der lediglich der Absender Inhalte publiziert. Die Empfänger:innen können weiterhin nur über Emojis oder die Teilnahme an Umfragen auf die gesendeten Textnachrichten, Fotos und Videos reagieren.

articles.title: OpenAI's Jev clone could help the frontier lab stop its swarming agents | TechCrunch
articles.text:
One of the more intriguing announcements at OpenAI’s Dev Day event on Tuesday came in an aside from CEO Sam Altman, who revealed the company’s new “Decisions API.”
The API apparently provides similar functionality to Jev, a model released by TypeSafe AI earlier this month that’s explicitly designed for software automation. A kind of super-powered classifier built on an LLM, developers can give Jev a set of choices that it outputs as probabilities cheaply and at high speeds.
OpenAI’s Decisions API seems to be the same sort of product. At the event, Altman described the API as a way to give the lab’s Luna model a predefined set of options to choose between, such as categories in which to classify an image or different agent behaviors.
“By focusing the model on that choice, we can make it extremely fast while keeping capabilities like image understanding, broad language support, and safety protections,” Altman said.
TypeSafe didn’t respond to TechCrunch’s questions about the new product, but CEO Diogo Almeida, a former OpenAI engineer who co-invented reinforcement learning, joked on X about the beginning of the clone wars.
He added that OpenAI’s interest could be “a sign…that building in a System One compatible way is the future.” (“System One” is TypeSafe’s term of art for fast, intuitive thinking, versus “System 2,” which it applies to deliberate reasoning.)
The subtext here is that LLMs as we know them aren’t the right solution for a lot of software because they are comparatively slow and expensive. Developers have been using Jev to augment LLMs and, in doing so, have found that they’re faster and cheaper.
It’s not clear how similar Decisions API will be to Jev, since OpenAI released it as a limited preview and, thus far, TechCrunch hasn’t spotted developers running it through its paces. However, there is clearly interest, according to the conversations on X.
Decisions API isn’t the only Jev-like API on the internet — other startups are rolling out similar models; OpenAI won’t be the last tech giant to produce one. A key question is how well calibrated each of these decision models’ outputs will be to real life.
Almeida says his company’s moat is the synthetic data it creates to generate statistically useful outputs.
“Fast and cheap is very easy, you know,” Almeida told TechCrunch last week. “If you want it really fast and cheap, use dice, right? Intelligence is the hard part, and my North Star is always pushing the intelligence-per-dollar Pareto curve.”
After just weeks, it seems clear that these models have a future ahead of them, and one likely application is monitoring and securing AI agents. One of OpenAI’s new security measures following a series of incidents where its agents misbehaved on the open internet is using a separate model to watch for bad actions at “significant compute cost.”
Shapor Naghibzadeh, a long-time cybersecurity professional who leads the startup QueryStory, thinks that a model like Jev could make that possible far more cheaply.
He built a demo for a hackathon held last weekend that uses Jev to check each agentic action against the task it was given, blocking actions it had high confidence were bad, flagging others for review, and permitting the rest.
In theory, such monitoring could have stopped the Hugging Face incident — and monitoring of that kind costs $2.94 with Jev, versus $372 with a frontier LLM.
A key observation is that Jev is arguably cheap enough to run on every agentic action, which offers a layer of review that could improve the reliability of agents writ large. It’s the kind of thing TypeSafe was hoping to achieve — and now OpenAI has seen the value as well.

articles.title: Los hermanos Russo revelan la duración de 'Avengers: Doomsday' y prometen un final "muy sorprendente"
articles.text:
Con Avengers: Doomsday camino a ser el gran estreno cinematográfico de 2026, los hermanos Russo han revelado algunos detalles interesantes de la película. La dupla de directores no solo reveló la duración aproximada de la cinta, sino que también prometió un final "muy sorprendente".
Los cineastas no comentaron la cantidad exacta de minutos de extensión de Avengers: Doomsday, pero sí indicaron que será similar a la de Infinity War. Para ser más precisos, comentaron que el largometraje durará alrededor de dos horas y media. Esto la ubicará en el mismo nivel del filme de 2018 (minutos más, minutos menos), pero la dejará bastante por detrás de los títulos más extensos del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel. No olvidemos que Avengers: Endgame superó levemente la marca de 3 horas.
"Es una película de unas dos horas y media. Te sientas a verla y te encuentras con una narrativa centrada y dinámica que tiene un principio organizador en su núcleo, y todo debe orbitar en torno a eso. Allí reside parte del desafío creativo para Joe y para mí: averiguar cuál es esa órbita y cómo encaja todo ello", explicó Anthony Russo sobre Avengers: Doomsday.
Por supuesto que los directores mantienen sus naipes contra su pecho y no quieren revelar más de lo necesario sobre Avengers: Doomsday. Pocos días atrás se concretó el estreno de Avengers: Endgame Encore, con nuevas escenas y un final modificado para adaptarlo al ingreso del Doctor Doom de Robert Downey Jr, y el material adicional no tardó en filtrarse generando todo tipo de reacciones entre el público.
Recientemente, los hermanos Russo revelaron en una entrevista con Empire Magazine que el colapso del multiverso es "lo más profundo que le ha pasado al UCM". Además, lo catalogaron como "crucial para la narrativa" de Avengers: Doomsday.
Avengers: Doomsday tendrá un final muy sorprendente, según sus directores
Por supuesto que los hermanos Russo no han querido ofrecer detalles sobre cómo terminará Avengers: Doomsday o de cómo establecerá la continuidad en Avengers: Secret Wars. No obstante, sí han comentado que el final de su próxima película será "muy sorprendente".
Esto ha disparado las especulaciones de un final abierto que repita la fórmula de Infinity War, lo cual tiene sentido si consideramos que no será la única película con el Doctor Doom. De modo que es lógico pensar en una conclusión sin resolución definitiva que replique lo que en su momento sucedió con Thanos en el arco que concluyó con Endgame.
"Creo que la gente se va a sorprender. Es un final muy sorprendente. Es una película muy sorprendente, y eso es todo lo que diremos al respecto", mencionó Joe Russo. Sea como sea, la expectación de los fanáticos se encuentra en niveles altísimos. Avengers: Doomsday se estrena en cines el próximo 18 de diciembre.

articles.title: AI Drives Larger, Denser Packaging- EE Times
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence is pushing advanced packaging in seemingly opposite directions: Package sizes are getting larger, while interconnect pitches and defect tolerances continue to shrink.
At A*STAR’s Innovate Together 2026 in Singapore, experts from KLA, ASM, ASMPT, and the National University of Singapore (NUS) discussed how advanced packaging is evolving beyond individual equipment or process technologies. The challenge is to integrate materials, bonding, metrology and inspection, optical interconnects, and system design while maintaining yield, reliability, and cost efficiency across larger package areas and finer interconnect pitches.
Surya Bhattacharya, head of system-in-package at A*STAR’s Institute of Microelectronics (IME) and moderator of the panel, said that as continued transistor scaling becomes insufficient to meet AI computing demands, systems must integrate more dies and functions, making packaging an increasingly integral part of system design.
Hybrid bonding puts materials and processes to the test
Avi Shantaram, corporate director of advanced packaging at ASM International, said hybrid bonding is an important technology for next-generation, high-density 3D interconnects, but the challenge extends well beyond the bonding equipment itself. Interface engineering is equally critical.
As chiplets and 3D stacking drive higher interconnect densities, wafer surface roughness, chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) dishing, cleanliness, and particle control can all affect bonding results. Hybrid bonding requires highly flat and clean surfaces, making precursor characteristics, CMP, atomic layer deposition, surface treatment, materials interface engineering, and low-temperature processing important elements of process control.
As interconnect dimensions shrink, even tiny particles can create much larger voids at the bonding interface, potentially affecting reliability and yield.
Gary Widdowson, senior VP and CTO of ASMPT’s semiconductor solutions, said hybrid bonding will not immediately replace conventional thermal compression bonding (TCB). TCB still offers advantages in process maturity and cost, and the two technologies are likely to coexist at different stages, particularly in high-density stacking applications such as high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
However, as interconnect pitch continues to shrink, the advantages of direct copper-to-copper bonding for high-density interconnects could make hybrid bonding necessary for some advanced packages.
The pace of adoption will ultimately depend on both cost and yield, Widdowson said. “We are dealing with a complete process, not a single equipment problem.” Equipment makers therefore need to work with wafer manufacturers, packaging companies, and materials suppliers to establish process windows that can take hybrid bonding from technology demonstrations into high-volume manufacturing (HVM).
HBM raises the bar for advanced packaging process control
When HBM and multiple logic dies are integrated into a single package, small process variations can become system-level yield problems. Chia Wee Teck, VP and general manager of KLA’s Global Customer Organization, said advanced packaging cannot rely solely on final inspection; defects and process variation must be monitored throughout the manufacturing flow.
“If you can’t see it, you can’t measure it, you can’t control it,” Chia said. Equipment makers need to connect inspection, metrology, and process data to identify the sources of defects and feed the information back into the process, creating a continuous control loop.
For HBM and hybrid bonding, this means monitoring high-density interconnects, fine pitches, copper surface profiles, bond voids, surface contamination, and die and wafer geometry. As packages move from engineering validation into HVM, turning these data into controllable process windows will be critical to yield and reliability.
KLA’s collaboration with A*STAR focuses on advanced packaging process control, using inspection and metrology to identify defects earlier and monitor process variation.
Optical interconnects emerge as another AI packaging bottleneck
Data movement is emerging as another bottleneck for AI systems. Aaron Thean, deputy president (Academic Affairs) and provost of NUS and director of SHINE, said the importance of optical interconnects is increasing as AI computing scales, with data rates moving from 200 Gb/s per lane toward 400 Gb/s per lane and beyond.
This means photonics can no longer be treated simply as a collection of discrete components. It must be designed together with electronics, packaging, and the overall system architecture. Future heterogeneous integration will need to incorporate photonic components at the system level, including light-source integration and connections between optoelectronic components.
Thean also pointed to materials such as lithium niobate as potential options for high-speed photonic devices.
From an equipment and packaging perspective, Widdowson noted that optical interconnects bring together a range of components, including electronic integrated circuits (EICs), photonic integrated circuits (PICs), laser diodes, fiber arrays, and microlenses. While each component may be relatively mature on its own, integrating them into a single package introduces challenges in alignment, bonding, thermal management, and reliability.
Chia said the greater challenge is integrating multiple optical and electronic components while maintaining yield, reliability, and cost efficiency. As co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-package optics (NPO) move toward tighter integration with compute and switch chips, packaging process control will become increasingly important.
Panel-level packaging amplifies manufacturing challenges
As AI systems integrate more dies into a single package, package size is also becoming a manufacturing-efficiency issue. Bhattacharya said that as high-performance computing systems scale, packages may need to accommodate larger compute and memory components. Even when package sizes reach 9× the reticle or beyond, manufacturing packages or interposers on a 300-mm wafer becomes increasingly inefficient, prompting the industry to consider larger panel-based platforms.
Widdowson said the industry is exploring a range of panel sizes, starting at roughly the 300-mm class and extending to 600 mm, 700 mm, 800 mm, and even close to 1 m. There is no industry consensus yet on a final panel size, although 510 × 515 mm is among the dimensions currently being discussed. Standards will be needed for panel dimensions, equipment interfaces, and infrastructure to avoid unnecessary complexity across the manufacturing ecosystem.
Larger panels, however, introduce new process control challenges. Chia noted that large, heavy panels can suffer from warpage and distortion and create handling difficulties. Maintaining inspection capability for fine-pitch routing across a much larger area is also challenging.
At the same time, package areas are expanding while defect sizes are not—and may continue to shrink. Equipment makers therefore need to maintain nanometer-level inspection and metrology across increasingly large manufacturing areas, while feeding the results back into materials, bonding, CMP, and other processes. The goal is to enable advanced packaging to continue scaling toward both higher density and larger package sizes.

articles.title: Egyptian fintech startup Paymob raises $35m pre-Series C funding round - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian startup Paymob, the leading payments infrastructure service provider in the MENA region, has secured US$35 million in a pre-Series C funding round to support its ongoing expansion across the region.
Founded in 2015 by Islam Shawky, Alain El Hajj and Mostafa Menessy, Paymob is an infrastructure technology enabler providing payment solutions to empower digital financial service providers through mobile wallet technology.
Its omnichannel gateway offers more than 60 payment solutions and empowers close to 350,000 merchants with access to innovative financial services. It has expanded to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Saudi Arabia and Oman.
Disrupt Africa reported in September 2024 Paymob had extended its Series B round to US$72 million, and it has now secured US$35 million in pre-Series C funding in a round co-led by Mubadala Investment Company, an Abu Dhabi-based sovereign investor, and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). British International Investment, Global Ventures and DPI Ventures also took part in the raise.
The fresh capital will support Paymob’s ongoing growth across MENA, by scaling its core digital payments acceptance operations and by rolling out new products aimed at SME merchants and at agentic commerce use cases. Paymob has onboarded around 20,000 merchants across its three GCC markets since it received its Retail Payment Services Licence from the Central Bank of the UAE in January 2025.
“Paymob morphed into a regional platform over the past 18 months, propelled by the exponential growth of our GCC business. This pre-Series C funding round will help us accelerate our growth plan across the MENA region and fast-track our product roadmap to become the go-to payments platform for agentic commerce. We are very excited about Mubadala joining our cap table and grateful for the continued support of our existing shareholders,” Shawky, Paymob’s CEO, said.

articles.title: Temporary Disaster Roaming has been activated to keep users connected during natural disasters - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Australia’s three major mobile operators – Telstra, Optus and Vodafone – have today activated Temporary Disaster Roaming (TDR) to keep remote and regional Australians connected in the event of a natural disaster causing mobile network outages.
TDR can be activated in designated areas where another mobile network is available and can support additional call traffic.
This way communities can stay connected and communicate as well as find information through an available network service during an emergency.
In the event of a natural disaster or other circumstances, people whose usual mobile network is down will still be able to make calls and send and receive text messages and access data via another available network.
TDR will be provided at no extra cost to customers.
“If your usual mobile network is impacted by a natural disaster, TDR will enable you to make calls, send texts, and use basic data via another mobile network where there’s one available,” says Australian Telecommunications Alliance CEO Luke Coleman. “There is no additional cost to use it, and for most customers, connection will occur automatically once TDR has been activated and is available.
“Australians have always been able to use any available mobile network to call Triple Zero – even when their usual network is impacted by an outage or out of coverage.
“TDR takes this even further. When it is activated and available, it is designed to allow customers to stay in touch with family and friends via voice calls and texts, and access basic data to use emergency service apps, WhatsApp, and iMessage.”
The activation of TDR will be managed between the mobile network operators themselves through their Network Operations Centre (NOC) which is operational 24/7.
If an operator recognises their network has been disrupted by a natural disaster, it can then contact one of the surviving networks to assess whether they still have coverage and capacity to support the affected area.
Each of the operators has conducted field testing to ensure the capability is prepared for the high-risk weather season.
TDR will also work hand in hand with the existing Camp-On setup for Triple Zero calling.
Camp-On allows users to still connect to emergency services using another mobile network when their usual network is unavailable.
But an important consideration of TDR is ensuring the still-active networks have enough coverage and capacity to handle the additional customers without putting their existing services, including Triple Zero, at risk.

articles.title: Inox Clean Energy files papers for Rs 10,000-cr IPO
articles.text:
Inox Clean Energy files papers for Rs 10,000-cr IPO
This offering would mark the largest private-sector renewable energy public issue in India to date.
Renewable energy company Inox Clean Energy has filed draft papers with the market regulator SEBI to raise up to Rs 10,000 crore through an initial public offering (IPO).
This offering would mark the largest private-sector renewable energy public issue in India to date. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 8,000 crore and an Offer-for-Sale (OFS) of shares worth Rs 2,000 crore by promoter Devansh Jain, according to the Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) filed on Tuesday.
The company, part of the INOXGFL Group, plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue to repay or prepay, in full or part, certain outstanding borrowings of the company and its subsidiaries, as well as for general corporate purposes.
Inox Clean Energy is an integrated renewable energy platform with two principal businesses—renewable power generation and solar manufacturing.
As of August 31, 2026, its renewable independent power producer (IPP) portfolio stood at 9.29 GW across India and Africa, comprising 2.37 GW of operational capacity, around 0.80 GW under construction, 2.99 GW of pipeline capacity and 3.13 GW of future capacity, the draft papers noted.
Its solar manufacturing business has an operational solar module manufacturing capacity of 6 GW across India and the US, while solar cell manufacturing capacity is under construction in India and the US.
Inox Clean Energy faces competition from a growing pool of listed renewable energy companies, including Adani Green Energy, NTPC Green Energy, ACME Solar Holdings, Waaree Energies, Premier Energies, Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions and JSW Energy.
Inox Clean Energy is part of the broader INOXGFL Group, which has interests in chemicals and renewable energy and has three listed entities: Gujarat Fluorochemicals Ltd, Inox Wind Ltd, and Inox Green Energy Services Ltd.
The group provides integrated capabilities spanning solar module manufacturing, wind turbine generation, engineering, procurement and construction, and renewable energy operations and maintenance.
Nuvama Wealth Management, CLSA India, Emirates NBD Capital India, HSBC Securities and Capital Markets (India), ICICI Securities, IIFL Capital Services, JM Financial, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors and UBS Securities India are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

articles.title: Piratage des impôts : l'ANSSI révèle ce qu'il s'est vraiment passé lors de la cyberattaque
articles.text:
On en sait désormais plus sur le piratage des impôts, qui a défrayé la chronique cet été. L’Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d’information (ANSSI) vient de rendre public son rapport sur la cyberattaque qui a frappé la direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP). Le constat est sans appel : le fisc a été victime de ses propres vulnérabilités.
« La compromission des SI de la DGFIP n’est pas la conséquence d’une attaque sophistiquée, mais de l’exploitation de faiblesses dans trois domaines », tranche l’agence.
Les trois domaines épinglés par l’ANSSI sont l’identité, l’architecture et la détection. Pour rappel, ce rapport de 20 pages a été commandé par le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu, dans la foulée de la fuite de données.
 📄 L’ANSSI publie le rapport d’incident sur les cyberattaques ayant touché la DGFIP.
➡️Plus d’informations sur :https://t.co/PoNuVGKW3u pic.twitter.com/LdXxNYM3aM
— ANSSI (@ANSSI_FR) September 29, 2026
Des dizaines d’identifiants piratés
La cyberattaque commence par des mots de passe compromis. Pendant trois mois, l’attaquant a mis la main sur plusieurs dizaines d’identifiants d’agents de la DGFiP. Selon l’ANSSI, ils ont « probablement » été compromis par le biais « de logiciels espions (de type infostealers) sur des ordinateurs non administrés par la DGFIP ». Les identifiants ont notamment été piratés sur les appareils personnels des agents.
« Aucune tentative d’attaque par force brute ou credential stuffing n’a été identifiée, ce qui signifie que l’attaquant disposait de mots de passe pour ces comptes », souligne le rapport.
Les premières connexions suspectes remontent au mois de mai, par le biais d’adresses IP géolocalisées en France et en Inde. Le fisc disposait pourtant d’un filet de sécurité pour empêcher les fuites. Un prestataire, Recorded Future, était en effet chargé de surveiller la revente d’identifiants d’agents sur Internet. Une fois que des identifiants sont identifiés, le centre de sécurité de la DGFiP (SOC) réinitialise les mots de passe concernés.
Malheureusement, toutes les plateformes de revente ne sont pas dans le colimateur de Recorded Future. L’ANSSI souligne qu’il s’écoule toujours un délai trop long entre le vol et la réinitialisation des mots de passe. Ce délai est « suffisant pour qu’un attaquant […] débute une exfiltration ». L’ANSSI pointe aussi du doigt l’absence d’authentification à deux facteurs sur les deux portails de la DGFiP qui ont été compromis. Les identifiants piratés suffisaient donc pour se connecter aux portails sans rencontrer le moindre obstacle.
À lire aussi : Nouvelle fuite de données à l’État – les IBAN de 143 000 Français compromis
Deux vagues d’extraction passées inaperçues
Une fois à l’intérieur, le pirate s’est intéressé à E-Contact, l’application de messagerie qui permet d’échanger avec les utilisateurs. Fin juin, il s’est mis à exfiltrer une montagne de données sur les réseaux du fisc. Il a subtilisé 11 gigaoctets de données dans un premier temps. Un mois plus tard, le pirate a volé 3 gigaoctets supplémentaires.
L’opération n’est pas totalement passée sous le radar. Des recherches suspectes ont poussé le centre de sécurité de la DGFiP à émettre une alerte, mais personne ne s’en est occupé avant le lendemain. Les équipes ont réinitialisé le mot de passe du compte piraté, mais il était déjà trop tard. Des données avaient déjà été siphonées. L’ANSSI reconnaît elle-même ne pas avoir décelé l’attaque, car l’attaquant utilisait des comptes légitimes. Elle admet toutefois que « le volume cumulé de requêtes que l’attaquant a dû générer pour orchestrer l’exfiltration de données aurait dû déclencher des alertes ».
À lire aussi : Fuite de données – les hackers des impôts ont fait une nouvelle victime
Les mesures exigées par l’ANSSI
Pour éviter qu’une cyberattaque de ce type se reproduise, l’ANSSI dresse une longue liste de mesures. Elle demande d’abord de généraliser l’authentification multifacteur sur toutes les applications, avec un second facteur robuste. L’agence recommande plutôt des clés physiques ou des applications d’authentification, et non des codes envoyés par mail.
Dans le rapport, l’agence estime aussi que « l’usage d’appareils personnels pour accéder à des ressources professionnelles doit être proscrit ». Elle recommande de placer toutes les applications sous surveillance, de mieux sensibiliser les agents et d’instaurer des quotas sur les volumes de données qui peuvent être consultés.
L’agence précise que seul un audit complet permettra de recenser toutes les vulnérabilités dans les systèmes du fisc. Cet audit a d’ailleurs été ordonné en août par Sébastien Lecornu, qui demande à ses ministres de réagir dans les plus brefs délais. En attendant, des mesures d’urgence ont été prises dès le mois d’août 2026. Les agents de la DGFiP n’ont plus accès aux portails compromis. D’ici la fin de l’année, l’authentification multifactorielle sera généralisée sur tous les systèmes.
Arrestation et contrôle de la CNIL
En parallèle, un jeune homme de 18 ans, connu sous le pseudonyme de « ChatNoir », a été interpellé par les forces de l’ordre françaises. Décrit comme un « pirate chevronné » déjà connu des services de police, le jeune homme est suspecté d’appartenir au groupe de cybercriminels « Zerobytes ». C’est ce gang qui a revendiqué le piratage du fisc dès l’été. De son côté, la CNIL va mener une enquête approfondie pour déterminer qui sont les responsables de la violation.

articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro : des utilisateurs signalent des crépitements dans le haut-parleur
articles.text:
À peine commercialisé, l’iPhone 18 Pro voit déjà les signalements se multiplier. Après Face ID et l’écran, c’est désormais le haut-parleur qui fait parler de lui, avec des propriétaires confrontés à des crépitements et autres bruits parasites.
Depuis quelques jours, les témoignages se multiplient sur les forums de MacRumors et Reddit. Des propriétaires d’iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max disent entendre un bruit inhabituel dans le haut-parleur de leur appareil : crépitement, claquement sourd ou petit « tick » intermittent, les descriptions diffèrent, mais le problème reste le même. Apple n’a pour l’heure pas réagi publiquement à ces remontées.
iPhone 18 Pro : le haut-parleur crépite dans plusieurs situations
Le bruit ne se manifeste pas de la même manière chez tous les utilisateurs. Certains l'entendent régulièrement, tandis que d'autres ne le constatent que dans des situations précises, par exemple en faisant défiler une page web, à la réception d'une notification, lorsque le clavier apparaît à l'écran ou pendant un appel passé sur le réseau cellulaire. Sur certains appareils, deux manipulations permettraient également de reproduire le phénomène : activer puis désactiver le mode Avion, ou modifier rapidement la luminosité de l'écran.
Le son semble principalement provenir du haut-parleur d'écoute, celui utilisé pour les appels. Plusieurs propriétaires expliquent par ailleurs avoir retourné leur iPhone avant de recevoir un appareil de remplacement présentant le même problème. Ces témoignages suggèrent que le phénomène ne serait donc pas limité à quelques unités isolées, même si sa portée réelle du problème reste pour l'instant inconnue.
La mise à jour iOS 27.0.1 ne règle pas le problème
Apple a récemment déployé iOS 27.0.1, une mise à jour destinée à corriger un autre bug touchant les iPhone 18 Pro. Celui-ci pouvait provoquer le redémarrage de l’appareil après un échec d’authentification avec Face ID. Les notes de version ne font en revanche état d’aucun correctif concernant le son, et les premiers retours après l’installation indiquent que les crépitements sont toujours présents.
Ce nouveau problème s’ajoute aux autres signalements apparus depuis la sortie des iPhone 18 Pro. Dans les premiers jours de commercialisation, des utilisateurs avaient notamment rapporté des anomalies liées à l’écran. Pour le haut-parleur, la cause reste encore inconnue. S’il s’agit d’un bug logiciel, Apple pourrait le corriger avec une prochaine mise à jour. En revanche, si le problème est matériel, sa résolution pourrait devenir beaucoup plus contraignante pour les utilisateurs.

articles.title: Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra, Smart Tag 3… Samsung fait le plein de nouveautés pour la rentrée - Numerama
articles.text:
Un an après les Galaxy Tab S11, Samsung renouvelle ce 30 septembre 2026 sa gamme de tablettes Android haut de gamme. Les Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra et Galaxy Tab S12+ arriveront en magasin le 7 octobre 2026 avec une nouvelle puce MediaTek et toujours un stylet S Pen toujours fourni dans la boîte, à la différence du rival historique Apple.
Samsung accompagne ses nouvelles tablettes d’une évolution de son traqueur Bluetooth : le Galaxy SmartTag 3. La mauvaise nouvelle est qu’il faudra probablement attendre 2027 pour l’acheter en France.
Samsung met à jour ses tablettes haut de gamme avec toujours une taille record de 14,6 pouces
Sur le papier, la Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra évolue peu. Elle a le même écran AMOLED de 14,6 pouces que la Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra, la même épaisseur de 5,1 mm, le même poids de 692 grammes et la même batterie de 11 600 mAh. Le principal changement est à l’intérieur : la puce MediaTek Dimensity 9500, gravée en 3 nm, remplace la MediaTek Dimensity 9400+. On aurait pu espérer une puce Snapdragon comme sur les smartphones Galaxy, mais Samsung reste fidèle à MediaTek pour ses tablettes. Samsung annonce un meilleur refroidissement avec une chambre à vapeur 3D, des meilleurs haut-parleurs et préinstalle Photoshop sur la tablette, pour adresser une cible créative.
En plus de la Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra, Samsung lance une Galaxy Tab S12+. La marque n’avait pas sorti de Tab S11+ l’année dernière, il s’agit donc d’une vraie nouveauté. Ce modèle a la même puce que l’Ultra, mais avec un écran de 12,6 pouces.
Côté prix, la facture grimpe. En France, la Galaxy Tab S12+ démarre à 1 319 euros et la Tab S12 Ultra à 1 539 euros. À ce tarif, Samsung se place au niveau des iPad Pro : Apple vend sa tablette en version 11 pouces à partir de 1 319 euros. Samsung a néanmoins deux avantages : sa tablette commence à 12,6 pouces et le stylet est inclus.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Écran | 12,6 pouces AMOLED, 2 800 x 1 752 pixels | 14,6 pouces AMOLED, 2 960 x 1 848 pixels | 11 pouces OLED tandem, 2 420 x 1 668 pixels | 13 pouces OLED tandem, 2 752 x 2 064 pixels | 
| Luminosité maximale | 1 600 nits | 1 600 nits | 1 600 nits | 1 600 nits |

articles.title: Microsoft to block Entra ID script injection attacks starting October
articles.text:
Microsoft has reminded customers that the Entra ID identity and access management (IAM) solution will get better protection against external script injection attacks starting next month.
The company first revealed plans to secure Entra ID sign-ins from script injection attacks in a November 2025 announcement.
According to a Monday message center update seen by BleepingComputer, Microsoft will begin enforcing additional Content Security Policy (CSP) defenses that will only allow scripts from trusted Microsoft content delivery network (CDN) domains during Entra ID sign-ins.
The rollout should end by late October 2026, after which all users will be protected from various sign-in security risks, including cross-site scripting attacks in which malicious code is injected into websites to steal credentials.
"Microsoft Entra ID will enhance sign-in security by enforcing a Content Security Policy blocking external script injection starting mid-October 2026," the company said. "This change helps protect users from threats such as cross-site scripting (XSS) by allowing only trusted Microsoft-hosted scripts to run during authentication and blocking unauthorized or externally injected code."
Microsoft advised enterprise customers to stop using browser extensions and tools that inject code or scripts into sign-in pages before the new CSP changes take effect.
It also urged them to test sign-in scenarios before the next month's deadline to identify and address any dependency issues on code-injection tools. IT administrators can identify potential impact by reviewing sign-in flows in the browser developer console and looking for violations that appear in red text with details about the blocked scripts.
"Users will continue to be able to sign in even if unsupported script injection tools no longer function. This change is enabled by default as part of the service update and does not require tenant configuration," the company added.
"Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) and API-based authentication flows are not affected because CSP enforcement applies only to browser-based sign-in experiences using login.microsoftonline.com."
This change is part of Microsoft's Secure Future Initiative (SFI), announced after Chinese hackers breached the Exchange Online mailboxes of dozens of organizations and hundreds of individuals worldwide in May and June 2023.
As part of the same initiative, Microsoft also disabled all ActiveX controls in Windows versions of Microsoft 365 and Office 2024 apps, and it updated Microsoft 365 security defaults to block access to Office, SharePoint, and OneDrive files via legacy authentication protocols.

articles.title: Anthropic Flags AI Agent Liability Risks as OpenAI Faces Hacking Lawsuit
articles.text:
Anthropic has warned prospective investors that it could face claims from customers and users over the actions of rogue AI agents. The warning comes as OpenAI is being sued over agents that hacked Hugging Face during internal testing.
Anthropic says the law on AI agents is unsettled
Anthropic’s disclosure appears in the prospectus for the AI giant’s stock market debut, which Reuters reviewed.
Anthropic’s agentic technology is built to work inside customers’ systems with broad access and to operate without supervision for days. The company acknowledged the risks that come with this level of autonomy.
“These autonomous capabilities could increase the potential for harm, as errors, misalignment, or security exploits may result in real-world consequences,” Anthropic said in the prospectus.
The company pointed to irreversible actions, such as data deletion or financial transactions, as examples. It also warned that the liability limits in its contracts may not be enforceable or adequate against claims over the actions of autonomous agents.
How existing laws apply to AI agents is still an open matter, and many questions “are unsettled and could expose us to significant and unpredictable legal claims,” the company said.
One such question is whether agent actions will be classified as products, services, or something else. Another is whether, and under what circumstances, an agent’s actions can be legally binding on the user who deployed it. Anthropic also said it is unclear whether agent actions would trigger strict liability or negligence.
The FTC’s chairman has also weighed in. Speaking last week at the Reuters Momentum AI event in Austin, Andrew Ferguson rejected the idea of anthropomorphized AI agents that “break loose.” He suggested that the developers or users who instruct agents would be liable for any harm.
“Obviously, there will be new questions that arise when someone uses the tool and it acts in an unexpected, unpredictable way,” Ferguson said. “Ought liability to lie with the person who innocently used the tool and achieved an unexpected result? Ought it to lie with the toolmaker?”
A nonprofit tests California’s anti-hacking law against OpenAI
A public interest law nonprofit sued OpenAI in California, seeking to hold the company responsible for unauthorized access carried out by its agents.
Legal Advocates for Safe Science & Technology (LASST) filed the lawsuit, targeting OpenAI Group PBC and the OpenAI Foundation in San Francisco Superior Court.
The complaint is brought under California’s Unfair Competition Law (UCL) and alleges violations of the state’s Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act (CDAFA). CDAFA prohibits knowingly accessing, or causing to be accessed, computer systems without authorization.
LASST also points to a California provision that rules out autonomy as a defense. Under the state’s Civil Code, it is not a defense “that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm.”
The suit centers on cybersecurity evaluations that OpenAI ran earlier this year and mentions the Hugging Face hack (including how AI agents created a makeshift message board for planning), the RubyGems attack, and the targeting of an Australian government website.
LASST says OpenAI employees saw the agents’ communications before the attack and were advised that stopping the evaluation was “not required.” According to LASST, the agents’ own chain-of-thought reasoning shows that one of them described the plan as “clearly infrastructure hacking.”
LASST is not seeking monetary damages. Instead, it wants a court order barring OpenAI’s agents from accessing third-party systems without authorization and stopping the company from using unsafe AI development practices.
An OpenAI spokesperson told AFP that the Hugging Face incident was serious and that the company has taken several measures in response. However, the spokesperson said the lawsuit is completely without merit.
Senate Democrats introduce AI security bill
Democratic Senators Mark Warner, Brian Schatz, and Andy Kim on Tuesday sought unanimous consent to pass the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026.
The bill would set up a permanent AI Safety Board within the Department of Commerce. The board would bring together representatives from Commerce, NIST, CISA, the NSA, and the Treasury Department, along with independent experts. Developers of frontier models would have to give the board access to their models at least 45 days before public release.
The board would write enforceable standards for testing frontier models and for securing the environments in which they are tested. This would include safeguards and monitoring procedures for models that can find and exploit software vulnerabilities without direct human prompting. Developers that violate the standards would face civil penalties of up to $250,000 per violation, per day.
Senator Ted Cruz, who chairs the Senate Commerce Committee, objected, blocking passage by unanimous consent. He raised concerns that the proposal would give the executive branch too much power over private AI companies.
Experts say accountability should rest with those behind the agents
Aaron Beardslee, manager of threat research at Securonix, compared the liability question to self-driving cars.
“It will be interesting to see how the courts will lean one way or the other. This is similar to a self-driving car: is the car held liable or is the driver held liable? I would argue the person behind the wheel is responsible for whatever the vehicle does,” Beardslee said.
“If you’re building a tool that does cool things and makes cool things, you need to make sure it doesn’t run around and do cyber crime on its own because it had a good idea. AI agents don’t have a moral compass, just programmed rules,” he added.
Jacob Krell, senior director of secure AI solutions and cybersecurity at Suzu Labs, said OpenAI’s response falls short.
“If I accidentally hacked one organization, let alone multiple organizations, I would not expect to get by with a promise to do better. I would expect an investigation. Criminal charges should follow if investigators determine that offenses occurred,” Krell said.
“A pause without a clear timeline, independent testing, release criteria or mandatory reporting requirements is little more than a platitude,” he added. “I view it as an attempt to deflect attention from potential criminal liability and turn what should be a legal and security investigation into a public-relations exercise. Training pauses do not fix the underlying oversight, access-control and accountability failures.”

articles.title: Asha Sharma promet qu'Xbox n'est pas à vendre, après avoir supprimé 20 % des effectifs — Frandroid
articles.text:
Asha Sharma dirige Xbox depuis février, sans avoir jamais travaillé dans le jeu vidéo auparavant. Dans un long portrait publié ce mercredi 30 septembre par The New York Times, la CEO, née en 1989, a répondu à la question d’une revente de la division : « Xbox n’est pas à vendre ». Elle a enchaîné en expliquant que Microsoft regarderait « les bons partenariats, le bon modèle opérationnel et tout ce qui est nécessaire » pour faire réussir la division. Beaucoup d’options restent en effet sur la table, sauf une vente pure et simple.
Si la question se pose, c’est qu’Xbox reste un éternel trou dans les finances de Microsoft. Le groupe mise désormais sur les infrastructures de données et l’intelligence artificielle. Asha Sharma vient justement de là : avant Xbox, elle était présidente produit de la division CoreAI de Microsoft.
« Notre activité n’est pas en bonne santé aujourd’hui », a d’ailleurs reconnu Asha Sharma en juillet, dans une lettre aux employés. Xbox a vendu beaucoup moins de consoles que Nintendo et Sony sur cette génération. Ses licences historiques, comme Halo et Gears of War, comptent aussi de moins en moins pour les joueurs.
Un été de coupes, puis un discours sur le long terme
Microsoft a annoncé cet été la suppression d’environ 3 200 postes chez Xbox, dont 1 600 immédiatement, soit 20 % des effectifs de la division. Microsoft s’est aussi séparé de plusieurs studios : Double Fine et Compulsion Games sont redevenus indépendants, Undead Labs a changé de propriétaire, et Ninja Theory, dont la vente a échoué, est menacé de fermeture.
Les coupes continuent. Le 22 septembre, Xbox a annoncé la suppression de 268 postes, qui font partie des 3 200 annoncés en juillet. Microsoft estime avoir bouclé environ 75 % de ce plan, étalé jusqu’à fin juin 2027. Halo Studios est particulièrement touché, et le prochain Halo sera développé par une nouvelle équipe d’Activision.
Asha Sharma défend pourtant une vision de long terme. « Nous avons encore beaucoup de chemin à faire avec Microsoft », a-t-elle assuré au New York Times, en mettant en avant les 500 millions de joueurs mensuels revendiqués par Xbox « malgré la remise à zéro » en cours. Elle répète aussi volontiers que « la clarté, c’est de la bienveillance », et vise un milliard de joueurs par jour, notamment grâce au jeu en streaming en Afrique, en Amérique latine et en Asie du Sud.
Côté Microsoft, les dirigeants rappellent que des rumeurs de vente d’Xbox circulent depuis toujours, sans jamais s’être concrétisées.
Ces rumeurs ne sortent pourtant pas de nulle part. Plus tôt cette année, le média spécialisé The Information a rapporté que la direction de Microsoft avait discuté en interne d’une scission d’Xbox.
Pourquoi les analystes parient sur un spin-off
De nombreux analystes prédisent bien un spin-off, c’est-à-dire la sortie d’Xbox du groupe sous forme d’entreprise indépendante. Xbox pourrait alors signer un partenariat stratégique avec Microsoft pour garder l’accès à ses technologies, sans plus peser sur ses comptes. Un tel montage respecterait à la lettre la promesse d’Asha Sharma, puisqu’il ne s’agirait pas d’une vente à proprement parler.
Dans ce scénario, Microsoft resterait l’actionnaire majoritaire de la nouvelle entreprise Xbox, qui pourrait ouvrir son capital à d’autres investisseurs.
Depuis le lancement de la première Xbox en 2001, les actionnaires de Microsoft s’interrogent sur l’intérêt de cette division. Aujourd’hui, les priorités de Microsoft sont très éloignées du grand public. Le groupe a abandonné Windows Phone et son service Groove Music, et a nettement ralenti le développement de ses produits Surface. Face aux particuliers et dans les rayons, il ne reste que Xbox, si l’on met de côté l’éternel Windows sur PC. Microsoft a-t-il encore besoin d’Xbox, et Xbox pourrait-il survivre sans Microsoft ?
Microsoft a pourtant beaucoup dépensé pour Xbox. Le groupe a acheté Mojang, le studio de Minecraft, pour 2,5 milliards de dollars (environ 2,2 milliards d’euros) en 2014. Près de dix ans plus tard, il a racheté Activision Blizzard, l’éditeur de Call of Duty, pour 75,4 milliards de dollars (environ 65 milliards d’euros), sans oublier ZeniMax Media, la maison mère de Bethesda, achetée 7,5 milliards de dollars (environ 6,5 milliards d’euros) en 2021. Ces achats ont rapporté de maigres profits.
Le Game Pass n’a pas non plus tenu ses promesses. Cet abonnement donne accès à des centaines de jeux, mais il a plafonné à 34 millions d’abonnés avant de reculer. Phil Spencer, le prédécesseur d’Asha Sharma, en visait pourtant 100 millions.
Satya Nadella, CEO de Microsoft, a refusé de répondre au New York Times.
Le patron de Microsoft s’est toutefois exprimé ces derniers jours sur le sujet. Il estime qu’Xbox doit trouver « le bon modèle économique durable » et renouer avec la croissance dès cet exercice fiscal.

articles.title: Criptomonedas: cuál es el valor de Bitcoin este miércoles
articles.text:
El bitcoin, la primera moneda virtual lanzada al mercado, fue creado por Satoshi Nakamoto (pseudónimo) en 2008 tras la crisis financiera que afectó al mundo; esta divisa digital tenía como base un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales.
Conocido en el mundo de los mercados bajo las siglas BTC, el bitcoin utiliza la criptografía para garantizar que su gestión sea descentralizada, es decir, que no pueda ser regulado por ninguna institución u organismo bancario, lo que a su vez hace que las criptomonedas sean volátiles.
PUBLICIDAD
Pese al avance y alcance que ha tenido el Bitcoin y otros activos digitales de gran talla como Ethereum, organismos como el Banco Mundial, el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) aún se muestran dudosos sobre los "pros" de este tipo de criptomonedas.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
PUBLICIDAD
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
La cotización de bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 84552.95 dólares, lo que significa que la criptomoneda sufrió un cambio de 0.21% en las últimas 24 horas.
Por otro lado, registró un cambio de 0.0% con respecto a su valor hace una hora. En cuanto a su popularidad, se ubica en la posición #1.
PUBLICIDAD
Bitcoin alcanza un nuevo récord y lidera el auge en el mercado de las criptomonedas
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
PUBLICIDAD
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: Tenemos que dar el premio a mejor móvil calidad-precio 2026. Posiblemente sea el año más complicado de la historia para hacerlo
articles.text:
Cuando llega el momento de dar nuestra opinión y voto en los Premios Xataka, hay categorías que suelen provocar debates internos. La de mejor smartphone en relación calidad-precio es, sin duda, una de ellas. ¿Por qué? Tradicionalmente, nuestro galardón era un escaparate donde coronábamos al campeón popular: ese móvil que podíamos recomendar con los ojos cerrados a amigos, familiares y por supuesto, a vosotros, xatakeros. Nos viene a la memoria el ya mítico Pocophone F1, por ejemplo.
Por apenas unos 300 euros nos llevábamos una experiencia solvente para tres o cuatro años sin apenas renuncias. Hablo en pasado porque plantear la previa de este premio este año nos ha situado frente a un contexto insólito. La tormenta que atraviesa la industria —ejem, crisis de las memorias— sumada a la inflación que acompaña al mundo ha hecho saltar por los aires los márgenes de los fabricantes. Y con ellos, los precios que vemos tanto en los escaparates como en las tiendas online. El "móvil chollo" tal y como lo conocíamos ha desaparecido, debemos asumirlo.
Este año, la gama media se ha bifurcado: por un lado, móviles económicos que se ven obligados a reciclar componentes de hace un par de generaciones y a recortar en memorias. Otros aspirantes con vocación más premium que, a cambio de subir el nivel general, coquetean sin miedo con los 500 y 600 euros. La cuestión es que elegir al más equilibrado nunca nos había exigido sopesar tanto.
El fin de la ganga y de la elección fácil
Para entender por qué este año es tan complicado emitir un veredicto, conviene mirar el tablero. Hasta hace no demasiado, bastaba con que un fabricante montara el chip más potente de Qualcomm o MediaTek, un panel AMOLED correcto y una cámara solvente para ganarse el favor de todos.
Llegando al último trimestre de 2026, la categoría —si puede llamarse así— se ha retorcido. Mucho. La demanda de silicio por parte de la IA ha disparado los precios de las memorias de consumo, por ende también la de los smartphones. Y en esas, las decisiones han sido drásticas: o recortar en memoria, con consecuencias como unas velocidades menores o unas capacidades peores que hace un año, o bien asumir que la factura subirá.
Y es que, al mismo tiempo, los móviles que se enmarcan en ella han vivido saltos importantes (la llamada 'premiuminizacion') que antes eran impensables fuera de las cuatro cifras que exige la gama alta y premium. La popularización de las baterías de silicio-carbono que han roto la psicológica barrera de los 5.000 mAh, o los teleobjetivos dedicados, han comenzado a desplazar especificaciones austeras como el típico macro de 2 MP.
En este contexto, medir la "calidad-precio" ya no consiste en buscar quién da más potencia por menos euros, también pide evaluar quién ha gestionado con mayor inteligencia sus renuncias para entregar un producto lo más redondo posible. Y claro, es algo mucho más complicado.
Destellos de gama alta: autonomía y el zoom óptico
En parte por una paradoja: en un momento de precios cuesta arriba, los teléfonos que aspiran a ser esa compra acertada han incorporado avances que hasta hace poco se reservaban para los más top. Hay que decir: no lo han hecho de forma homogénea. Al no haber margen para integrarlo todo, los fabricantes se han visto obligados a jugar la carta de la especialización.
¿Qué queremos decir con esto? Que han debido elegir cuidadosamente dónde concentrar el poderío. Por un lado, hemos visto a marcas apostar por una revolución en autonomía gracias a las baterías de silicio-carbono. Así han sobrepasado los 6.000 e incluso 7.000 mAh sin que se conviertan en rugerizados.
Por otro lado, quienes no han apostado por estas baterías pueden haberlo hecho por teleobjetivos periscópicos. Eso es un alivio cuando se trata de dar relevo a los tristes sensores de 2, 5 y 8 MP tanto macro como ultra gran angular.
Eso sí, no implica que todos los aspirantes que seleccionemos vayan a tener una autonomía de tres días o un telefoto avanzado; la virtud reside en cómo esa cualidad diferencial —siendo otra— compensa otros apartados donde han contenido el presupuesto.
La letra pequeña del equilibrio: sacrificios bajo el capó frente a años de soporte
Porque esa gestión de los recursos por parte del fabricante nos lleva a mirar todo el mercado. Para que un móvil mantenga un precio atractivo y "justo" luciendo una pantalla o cámaras sobresalientes, la tijera aparece en algún punto.
En varios casos, el peaje se ha pagado en el rendimiento, por ejemplo recuperando chips de la anterior hornada u optando por memorias de almacenamiento o RAM más lentas, algo que deteriora el rendimiento y la fluidez. Por ende, su puntuación en el apartado de rendimiento (sí, hay matices como la optimización del software).
Hay quienes recortan en el chip, pero también hay otros que han decidido que el valor reside en el tiempo. El tiempo que duran las políticas de actualizaciones de software, por suerte, de hasta seis o siete años: tener la garantía de que no quedará abandonado a los dos años, es un lujo, tanto para disfrutar de nuevas funciones como para ir a la última en parches de seguridad.
Qué definirá al ganador (y candidatos)
Cuando nos sentemos a deliberar sobre los candidatos, el choque de filosofías será inevitable, porque hoy cada propuesta está más separada. Y por tanto, tenemos que dar respuesta a muchas preguntas:
- ¿Pesa más el mérito de quien mantiene un smartphone potente pero exige que limpiemos de bloatware al encenderlo o que salgan anuncios?
- ¿O la madurez de quien ofrece un diseño exquisito y un zoom óptico asumiendo que el ticket debe subir de escalón?
- ¿Debemos premiar las grandes baterías de silicio-carbono?
- ¿O la tranquilidad de saber que nuestro móvil se actualizará como mínimo seis años?
No hay una respuesta sencilla porque nuestras prioridades han dejado de ser uniformes como antaño sí eran. Lo que sí tenemos claro en Xataka es que este año la etiqueta de calidad-precio va a estar complicada: quien se alce con el galardón habrá tenido que sudar cada punto en nuestras pruebas para demostrar que, en uno de los años más difíciles de la década, todavía es posible construir un teléfono competente sin exigir un desembolso desorbitado.
Sea cuales sean esos candidatos, seguro que merecen la pena: habrá un artículo dedicado para que depositéis vuestro voto. Y por suerte, adelantamos que nuestro premio no se extinguirá, porque sí, siguen existiendo buenos móviles en la categoría de relación calidad-precio.
Sigue con nosotros el Camino a los Premios Xataka 2026
En noviembre celebraremos en Madrid la gala presencial de los Premios Xataka 2026, donde reconocemos los mejores dispositivos tecnológicos del año. Una de las categorías, el Premio de la Comunidad, la decidís solo vosotros.
Este es solo uno de los artículos con los que estamos repasando el estado de cada categoría antes de la gala. Puedes ver todos los artículos de la serie aquí.
¿Qué móvil crees que debe ganar en la categoría de mejor calidad-precio? Déjanos tu candidato en comentarios, comparte este artículo si te ha gustado y estate atento: pronto anunciaremos las votaciones oficiales, además de la fecha, lugar y cómo conseguir entradas.

articles.title: Honor Magic9 Pro Max: Everything to know before you buy
articles.text:
Honor launched the Magic9 Pro Max in Beijing on September 28, 2026, with sales in China starting the same day at CNY 6,499 (about $969).
The phone is the flagship of the new Magic9 series, with two 200MP cameras developed with ARRI, the German cinema-camera maker. It also packs an 8,800mAh battery and Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chip.
Honor styles the name as “Magic9 Pro Max.” The lineup also includes the smaller Magic9 and the Magic9 Super Edition, which puts more emphasis on battery capacity.
For buyers in Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, and Kenya, the bigger questions are when the phone will arrive and how much it will cost. Honor says it will expand to more markets soon, but has not announced local launch dates or prices.
Here’s what you need to know about the Honor Magic9 Pro Max before you buy or import one.
Honor Magic 9 Pro Max price
The Honor Magic 9 Pro Max comes in four RAM and storage versions. These are the China launch prices:
| RAM and storage | China price | About (US$) | 
|---|---|---|
| 12GB + 256GB | CNY 6,499 | $969 | 
| 12GB + 512GB | CNY 6,999 | $1,044 | 
| 16GB + 512GB | CNY 7,499 | $1,118 | 
| 16GB + 1TB | CNY 8,499 | $1,267 | 
Source: Honor launch announcement. Dollar figures use Wise’s rate of about $0.149 per yuan on September 30, 2026. Rates change daily.
Honor also sells a Master Photographer Package for CNY 10,999 (about $1,639), according to Gizmochina. This bundle adds camera accessories to the phone.
How much is the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max in Nigeria?
Honor has not announced a Nigerian price. At about ₦198 per yuan, the CNY 6,499 starting price comes to roughly ₦1.29 million.
Treat that figure as a plain currency conversion. Shipping and customs duty will raise the shop price. The naira also moves often, so check the rate again on the day you buy.
If you plan to buy from an importer, do two things first:
- Ask for the full price, including shipping and customs charges.
- Get the return terms in writing before you pay.
Pick your storage based on how you use your phone. If you shoot long videos and keep them on the device, look at the 512GB or 1TB versions. If you back up most files to the cloud, the 256GB model saves you money.
Honor Magic 9 Pro Max release date and availability
Honor launched the phone in Beijing on September 28, 2026, and sales in China started that same day.
Honor’s global announcement says details for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Southeast Asia and other regions will come later. Honor’s UK site already has a Magic9 series page where you can sign up for news, but it shows no final price or delivery date.
Here is where things stand in key markets:
| Market | What Honor has confirmed | 
|---|---|
| China | On sale since September 28 | 
| Nigeria | No sale date or official price yet | 
| South Africa | No sale date or official price yet | 
| Kenya | No sale date or official price yet | 
Imported units often reach local shops before an official launch. If you see one, ask which market the phone was made for and who will repair it if something goes wrong.
Detailed specs
The table below covers the China model. Scroll down for what each part means for you.
| Feature | Honor Magic 9 Pro Max | 
|---|---|
| Display | 6.8-inch LTPO OLED, 1,320 x 2,868 pixels, 1Hz to 120Hz | 
| Chip | Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 | 
| RAM | 12GB or 16GB | 
| Storage | 256GB up to 1TB | 
| Main camera | 200MP, f/1.57, OIS | 
| Telephoto camera | 200MP, f/2.6, OIS, 3.5x optical zoom | 
| Ultrawide camera | 50MP, f/2.0, autofocus | 
| Front camera | 55MP square sensor with 3D depth sensing | 
| Battery | 8,800mAh | 
| Charging | 100W wired, 80W wireless | 
| Software | MagicOS 11 on Android 17 | 
| Protection | IP68 and IP69/IP69K | 
| Weight | 233g (per PhoneArena) | 
| Colours | Moss Green; also Shadow Black and Glacier Silver | 
Sources: Honor launch materials. Resolution per PhoneDroid and Latestly; weight per PhoneArena.
1. Display
The Pro Max has a 6.8-inch screen. Its refresh rate drops as low as 1Hz when the screen stays still and climbs to 120Hz when you scroll. This keeps motion smooth and saves battery.
Honor claims a peak brightness of 10,000 nits and adds an anti-glare coating. That peak number applies only to small bright spots in special conditions, so expect a lower figure across the full screen in daily use.
The big screen gives you room to frame shots and review video. Try the phone in your hand before you buy, since it is a large device.
2. Performance
The phone runs on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, a 2nm chip. Gizmochina reports CPU speeds of up to 5GHz. Qualcomm pairs its Oryon CPU cores with a Hexagon AI engine for on-device AI tasks.
Qualcomm also offers AI-assisted game graphics through a feature called Adreno Neural Fusion. Each game must support it for you to see the benefit.
Raw chip speed tells you only part of the story. Wait for reviews that test long gaming sessions and 4K recording, since heat can slow any phone down.
3. Cameras
The Pro Max has three rear cameras and one front camera:
- Main: 200MP with a large 1/1.28-inch sensor and optical stabilisation to steady your shots.
- Telephoto: 200MP with 3.5x optical zoom and up to 200x digital zoom.
- Ultrawide: 50MP with autofocus, so it also handles close-up shots.
- Front: 55MP square sensor that lets you crop tall or wide photos, plus 3D depth sensing for face unlock.
Optical zoom keeps detail. Digital zoom crops the photo, so image quality drops at high levels. Check sample photos before you judge the 200x zoom.
4. Battery and charging
The Honor Magic 9 Pro Max packs an 8,800mAh battery, one of the largest in any flagship phone. It supports 100W wired charging and 80W wireless charging.
To get top wired speeds, you need Honor’s original charger and cable. For top wireless speeds, you need a compatible Honor wireless charger, which you buy separately.
Battery life depends on your screen brightness and the apps you use. Wait for independent tests before you count on a set number of days per charge.
5. Software and updates
The phone ships with MagicOS 11, based on Android 17. Honor’s YOYO assistant saves useful information for you and handles some tasks on your behalf. MagicOS also connects with devices from other brands.
Honor promises seven years of Android and security updates for its Magic flagships, starting in EU markets. That promise may not cover a China import. Ask the seller which update plan applies to your unit.
6. Build and durability
Honor builds the Pro Max with an all-metal unibody frame. Moss Green is the launch colour. Honor also sells it in Shadow Black and Glacier Silver.
The phone carries IP68 and IP69/IP69K ratings, so it resists dust and water, including high-pressure jets, in lab tests. Honor’s own notes say this protection weakens with wear, and the warranty excludes water damage.
For security, you get 3D face unlock and an ultrasonic fingerprint reader. Set both up and keep a strong passcode as a backup.
ARRI camera features explained
ARRI makes cinema cameras for Hollywood films. On the Pro Max, ARRI helps with how the phone records colour and how you edit the footage later.
What ARRI adds
- ARRI LogC3: A flat-looking video format that keeps more detail in bright and dark areas for editing.
- ARRI Wide Gamut 3: A wide colour range that works with LogC3 during editing.
- ARRI Looks: Colour styles you can preview while you shoot. You get 14 built in, with 87 in the full library.
- APV 10-bit 4:2:2 recording: A video format that saves more colour data for editing.
Log footage looks dull until you edit it. Plan time for colour work and learn the settings before a paid shoot.
Video tools you get
ARRI CINEMA Mode records up to 4K at 60 frames per second. Two pro tools help you get the shot right:
- Focus peaking marks the sharp parts of your frame in colour.
- False colour shows which areas look too bright or too dark.
The phone also uses directional microphones to capture sound from the direction you point it. Test them where you usually record before you rely on them for paid work.
Zoom and teleconverter lenses
Honor sells two clip-on teleconverter lenses. The G200 gives you a 200mm view and weighs just 88g, according to Huawei Central. The G500 stretches that to 500mm for far-off subjects like wildlife or stage shows.
Make sure you buy the version made for the Magic 9 Pro Max. These lenses may also launch in different markets at different times.
Accessory prices
| Accessory | China price | 
|---|---|
| G200 teleconverter | CNY 999 | 
| G200 teleconverter with photography grip | CNY 1,499 | 
| G500 teleconverter | CNY 1,999 | 
| G500 teleconverter with photography grip | CNY 2,499 | 
| SmallRig professional video kit | CNY 1,699 | 
Source: Honor China launch announcement.
How the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max compares with other Magic9 phones
Each Magic9 model suits a different buyer. The standard Magic9 fits two 200MP cameras into a smaller body. The Super Edition prioritises battery size and active cooling.
| Feature | Magic9 Pro Max | Magic9 | Magic9 Super Edition | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Starting price | CNY 6,499 | CNY 4,999 | CNY 4,499 | 
| Screen size | 6.8 inches | 6.37 inches | 6.81 inches | 
| Chip | Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 | Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 | Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 | 
| Main camera | 200MP | 200MP | 200MP | 
| Telephoto | 200MP | 200MP | 50MP | 
| Ultrawide | 50MP | 50MP | 12MP | 
| Battery | 8,800mAh | 8,000mAh | 11,000mAh | 
| Best for | Video creators | Smaller hands and pockets | Battery life and gaming | 
Sources: Honor China launch announcement and Magic9 product page.
Pick the phone that matches how you use it. If you want a smaller phone, the Magic9 gives you nearly the same main cameras for CNY 1,500 less. If you play long games, check reviews of the Super Edition’s cooling before you pay extra for the Pro Max.
What to check before you import the China version
Get clear answers from the seller before you pay:
- Exact model: Confirm the model number and the market it was made for.
- Apps and language: Ask the seller to show Google Play working, then test your banking apps and notifications. Check that English is available.
- Network support: Compare the phone’s network bands with what your mobile operator uses. Confirm calls and mobile data work.
- Warranty and returns: Get written terms on who fixes faults and who pays for return shipping.
Honor gives China buyers a one-year warranty under its local service terms. An overseas seller may offer different coverage, so ask what you get.
A listing that says “global” can mean many things. Ask the seller what it means for your unit.
Should you buy the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max or wait?
Most buyers in Nigeria should wait for official regional pricing and independent reviews. Then you can compare the full cost and warranty with phones you can already buy locally.
The Pro Max makes sense if you shoot video often and want manual recording tools. Watch sample footage in settings that matter to you, like indoor interviews or moving subjects.
If your current phone still does the job, hold on until reviews show the upgrade helps your work. If you need a new phone now, compare it with locally supported options and their total prices.
Experienced importers can buy the China version today. Check the software and network support first, and accept the seller’s repair terms before you pay.
The video tools give you the strongest reason to consider the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max. Its final value depends on how those tools perform and what the phone costs in your market.
