articles.title: Helsinki-based KHOY raises €2 million to take its vacuum-packed sofa beds across Europe and the US | EU-Startups
articles.text:
KHOY Company, a Helsinki-based direct-to-consumer design and furniture company, has raised €2 million in growth funding.
The round was led by Finnish private equity investor Virta Equity, with participation from Innovestor and several angel investors.
“KHOY has solved something the furniture industry has struggled with: how to sell and ship large, bulky products across borders without the cost eating the margin. We back businesses with real, profitable growth behind them, and KHOY has a combination of a defensible product innovation and proven demand across Europe,” said Heikki Kivirinta, CEO and Partner at Virta Equity.
Founded in 2022 by Visa Friström, András Kelemen (Creative Director) and Jukka Salmikukka (COO), KHOY is a Finnish D2C design and furniture company that sells exclusively online. It makes sofa beds that are vacuum-packed into compact cardboard boxes, which expand to full size once opened at home.
The company was previously called KOTA and adopted the KHOY name in 2026, a change it says reflects its international ambitions, with the same team and ownership. Its story began with a brief from its first customer, hospitality brand BobW, which wanted a sofa bed comfortable enough for daily sleep yet practical for apartments across Europe. The resulting design won a Red Dot Design Award in 2026.
KHOY launched its first sofa bed in June 2024 and posted €4.3 million in revenue in 2025, a 13-fold jump on the previous year. It is now growing 166% year-on-year and expects to more than double its revenue this year. Over 80% of sales already come from outside Finland, with Germany and France being its biggest markets in 2025. It also recorded notable sales in the Netherlands, Italy, Belgium, Austria, Ireland, Sweden and Denmark.
“We have proven that there is strong demand for a simpler way to buy furniture online. We have grown quickly while building a profitable business, and this funding allows us to accelerate from a strong position. Our ambition is to build KHOY into a major global online brand, with European quality,” said Friström, co-founder and CEO, KHOY Company.
Its strength lies in the design, which is a departure from traditional sofa bed designs, and vacuum-packing. The KHOY Company uses premium mattresses that unfold from a sofa into a bed. The company says vacuum-packing can cut delivery costs by as much as 95% compared with conventional furniture logistics, which lets it sell directly to consumers across several markets.
The funding will be used to scale its operations across the European Union, Switzerland, and the UK, while accelerating its push into the US, where the company launched operations around two weeks ago. The company will also keep developing its product portfolio, brand and operations.
“Furniture is still an unusually local industry. Large products are expensive to store and transport, which makes international expansion difficult. Vacuum-packing changes that equation. We already know the model works across borders – for us, the next phase is about scale,” added Friström.

articles.title: BMW reveals US 3 series pricing: The EV carries a hefty premium
articles.text:
BMW has opened the US order books for its hotly anticipated new 3 Series sedan. Built on an all-new platform called Neue Klasse, it now offers a fully electric version for the first time, using BMW’s advanced sixth-generation electric powertrain we liked so much in the iX3. And for those not quite ready to make the switch from liquid hydrocarbons to pure electron power, there are also a pair of gasoline-powered variants.
At launch, the only electric version will be the 2027 BMW i3 50 xDrive. It’s an all-wheel drive setup, with a combined 463 hp (345 kW) and 467 lb-ft (633 Nm). And while BMW is still putting the finishing touches on the car’s EPA certification ahead of its showroom arrival in Q1 next year, it expects 446 to 468 miles (718-753 km) of range on a single charge. Contributing to that very impressive range is the new cylindrical cell battery pack, which uses a cell-to-body approach that maximizes energy density, along with the aforementioned new sixth-gen motors.
We’re not sure whether BMW is planning any single-motor, rear-wheel drive i3s for the US market, such as the i4 eDrive40 we liked so much. But later next year, we can expect the i3 M60 xDrive, and then the first completely electric BMW M3, which will increase the motor count to four—one for each wheel.

articles.title: 'There’s a lot to like, just not the price' - why the LG Gram Pro 16 is almost perfect
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The LG Gram Pro 16 is incredibly light, coming in at under three pounds. Yet, it has enough power to play demanding computer games (on scaled-down settings). The battery life is just as impressive. Too bad, the price tag is so high.
Reasons to buy
- +Under three pounds thanks to the use of a new type of material
- +Impressive performance considering the package
- +Long battery life
- +Has some interesting LG specific apps
Reasons to avoid
- -So expensive
- -Comes with McAfee
- -USB-C ports all on the same side
Why you can trust TechRadar
LG Gram Pro 16 review: Two Minute Review
Thin. Light. And a big screen. Say less. Add in a surprising amount of power for this form factor, and you have the LG Gram Pro 16. There’s a lot to like with this laptop, including some interesting LG-specific software and a very impressive battery life. The only thing that might give me pause in recommending it as one of the best laptops out there is its very high price.
Now, I should clarify that there is a version of the LG Gram Pro 16 that skips the Aerominum material of the pricier version (more on that later) and has the most basic integrated graphics instead of the Intel Arc B390 Graphics included on the configuration reviewed here. Even though the Intel Arc B390 Graphics in the review unit are also integrated, it’s surprisingly on par with an Nvidia GeForce RTX 4050.
So that version might be one of the best Ultrabooks out there for someone who wants that thin and light package with a big screen but doesn’t need all the bells and whistles. But that version pales in performance. Of course, the LG Gram Pro 16 reviewed here is much more expensive. I don’t want to tell you to wait for a sale, but its price is its biggest drawback.
LG Gram Pro 16 review: Price & Availability
- How much does it cost? Starting at $2,699.99 (about £2,010/ AU$3,830)
- When is it available? Available now
- Where can you get it? Available in the US
While the LG Gram Pro 16 is available in US, UK, and Australia, the 2026 configuration, which has the model designation of 16Z90U (or 16Z95U for the AMD powered ones), is mostly just available in the US at the time of writing. It most certainly will make it to the UK, and one configuration is sold in Australia with an MSRP of AU$4,199, though it’s already discounted to AU$2,899. This configuration comes with a Intel Core Ultra 7 355 CPU, 32GB RAM, Intel Arc graphics, and 1TB of storage. It also features a 2560x1600 touchscreen.
For the US, there are seven configurations. The cheapest one, not accounting for any slashed prices, goes for $2,699.99, which has an Intel Core Ultra 7 CPU and its integrated graphics, 32GB RAM, 512GB storage, and that same 2560x1600 touch screen. The price starts to creep up with more storage (though some models have a 1TB SSD but 16GB of RAM and are maybe fifty bucks more).
The most expensive model doesn’t have a touchscreen, but does have slightly higher resolution with a 2560x1800 screen. More importantly, it comes with an Intel Core Ultra X7 CPU, integrated Intel Arc graphics B390 Graphics which have the power of an Nvidia Geforce RTX 4050, 32GB of RAM and 1TB of storage.
The Samsung Galaxy Book6 Ultra is a good laptop to compare the LG Gram Pro 16 to. Its price tag of $2,449.99 / £2,999 (around AU$6,000) for a laptop with an Nvidia RTX 5060 GPU and 1TB of storage, similar CPU, and similar screen is also expensive, though less expensive than the LG Gram Pro 16 at its maxed out configuration. Or, if you look at the Dell 2026 XPS 16, you’ll find a very similarly priced and specced laptop that also comes with an OLED screen (again comparing to the max configuration).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
I think there are a few reasons that LG costs more. The first is that they’re using a new material called Aerominum for the chassis, and semi-relatedly, weighs under three pounds, unlike either of the other mentioned laptops. Hopefully as LG keeps using Aerominum, the price will come down.
- Value score: 4 / 5
LG Gram Pro 16 review: specs
The LG Gram Pro 16 has about seven different configurations at the time of writing, all with slightly different combinations of CPU (Intel Core Ultra 7, AMD Ryzen AI 7 450, Intel Core Ultra X7), RAM (16 or 32GB), storage space (512GB, 1TB, or 2TB), and graphics, with the cheapest configuration utilizing the basic integrated Intel Graphics and more substantial configurations using the Ryzen AI 7 450’s integrated AMD Radeon 860M graphics or at the top of the price range, Intel’s integrated but powerful Arc B390 GPU.
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Base | Review / Max | 
|---|---|---|
| Price | $1,399.99 (about £1,040 / AU$1,980) | $3,499.99 (about £2,600 / AU$9,000) | 
| CPU | Intel Core Ultra 7 | Intel Core Ultra X7 | 
| GPU | Intel graphics | Intel Arc B390 Graphics | 
| RAM | 32GB LPDDR5X | 32GB LPDDR5X (Dual Channel, 8533MHz) | 
| Storage | 512GB M.2 SSD | 1TB M.2 SSD | 
| Display | 16-inch diagonal, WQXGA (2560x1600) touch IPS @120Hz | 16-inch diagonal, WQXGA+ (2560x1800) non-touch IPS @120Hz | 
| Ports and Connectivity | USB 3.2 Gen1 (x2), USB 4 Gen3x2 Type C (x2, with Power Delivery, Display Port, Thunderbolt 4), HDMI, Aux out | USB 3.2 Gen1 (x2), USB 4 Gen3x2 Type C (x2, with Power Delivery, Display Port, Thunderbolt 4), HDMI, Aux out | 
| Wireless | Intel Wi-Fi 7 (WiFi7, 2x2, BT Combo) and Bluetooth 6 | Intel Wi-Fi 7 (WiFi7, 2x2, BT Combo) and Bluetooth 6 | 
| Camera | FHD IR Webcam with Dual Mic (Face recognition) | FHD IR Webcam with Dual Mic (Face recognition) | 
| Dimensions | 2.97 lbs (1.35 kg) | 2.64 lbs (1.2 kg) | 
| Weight | 14.1 x 9.9 x 0.49~0.5 inches / 358.1 x 251.5 x 12.4~12.7 mm | 14.1 x 9.9 x 0.49~0.5 inches / 358.1 x 251.5 x 12.4~12.7 mm | 
On the exterior, there are two different screen options. The less powerful models come with a 2560x1600 resolution, some of which have touchscreens including the cheapest configuration. The more powerful ones with either the Ryzen or Intel Arc graphics have a slightly sharper 2560x1800 resolution – none of them touchscreen.
LG Gram Pro 16 review: Design
- Light, thin, but with a big screen!
- Keyboard doesn’t have much travel
- Good ports, but not ideal port placement
First things first, the LG Gram Pro 16 reviewed here is like all the other LG Grams, as it manages to be light and portable while still providing a pretty large screen. Those things are typically mutually exclusive. Yet here, you get a 16-inch screen in a package that weighs under three pounds. And since the bezels are pretty thin, it’s only fourteen inches wide. Plus, it’s half an inch thick.
It’s taken me a while to figure out why the LG Gram Pro 16 comes with such a high price tag. Part of it is the robust components. Part of it is the engineering to get it so light and thin. But part of it is, in my opinion, the use of a proprietary material called Aerominum instead of the usual aluminum alloy or plastic. It feels like plastic but is a little tougher, and the LG Gram Pro 16's chassis is made from it. There is, however, a little bit of give in the bottom shell where the venting is.
Since the LG Gram Pro 16 is so thin, the keyboard doesn’t have much travel. Because of this, I don’t really enjoy typing on it for long periods of time. It’s fine. It’s accurate. And it doesn’t bother me when browsing or more casual use, but it just doesn’t have much cushion. I can feel the keys bottom out on every press. At least, it’s a full size keyboard.
The trackpad, on the other hand, is nice to use. It’s also big, though I have to be careful to not accidentally touch it when typing as it is sensitive, and I’m somewhat lazy with my hand placement. And if you use all the different gestures Windows is capable of, the trackpad will register them.
Lastly, I’m appreciative of the port selection, but less so the port placement. A laptop like this doesn’t need anything beyond the two USB-4 type C, two USB, headphone jack, and an HDMI port that it comes with, but the LG Gram Pro 16 makes the same mistake that many laptops do. If you have two USB-C ports and that’s the only way to power the laptop, put one on each side and not on the same side. The power cable it comes with is not that long, and I’ve created a few tripping hazards trying to charge just because of the port placement.
- Design score: 4.5 / 5
LG Gram Pro 16 review: Performance
- Plenty of power for demanding tasks, though with some adjustments
- Mostly great suite of additional software
- Good audio, camera, and mic performance
3DMark: Solar Bay: 25,811; Steel Nomad: 1,607
Geekbench 7.0: (Single Core) 2,254; (Multi Core) 17,471
Crossmark: Overall: 1,981; Productivity: 1,763; Creativity: 2,334; Responsiveness: 1,716
HandBrake 1.11.1: 4:01
Total War: Warhammer III: Mirrors of Madness (1080p): 61.7fps; (2880x1800) 29.7fps
Cyberpunk 2077: (1080p, Ray Tracing): 18.29fps; (1080p, Ray Tracing off) 50.07fps
Battery Life (PCMark 10): 15:34:02
Between the Intel Core Ultra X7, Intel Arc B390 Graphics, and 32GB or RAM the LG Gram Pro 16 I’m reviewing has, it’s a fairly powerful computer. Despite the fact that the Intel Arc graphics are integrated and not actually a discrete GPU, it compares favorably to an Nvidia Geforce RTX 4050 (which is admittedly entry level for discrete graphics).
That means that I can take this somewhere to do a little work – maybe write this review, for instance – and then switch to a demanding video game like Starfield, South of Midnight or Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 for a bit of fun. While the computer struggles a little at the highest settings for these games, it’s also running at a 120Hz refresh rate.
Now, I assume that many people wanting to read about the LG Gram Pro 16 care about its gaming capabilities, but those are among the more demanding tasks you can ask from a computer. If it can run one of those games, it can handle photo and video editing (we also have benchmarks to show how they would handle those tasks). It can handle recording audio. This is a powerful computer, though, as a gaming computer, it just barely clears the bar of running those more demanding titles.
Now, since LG proudly advertises the AI capabilities of this laptop – if you look on the website, the thumbnail puts “AI” next to the computer’s name as if it’s part of it – it makes sense that AI is all over this thing.
When I open LG’s My Gram app, which is the LG Gram Pro 16’s software interface for fine-tuning its performance, I see things like AI microphone and speaker optimization settings (you can also register your voice so that the laptop only hears / recognizes it), AI cooling for the fan settings, and an AI mode for the battery settings where it adjusts battery usage based on what it’s learned about how one uses their computer and how to allocate battery based on that. The My Gram software can also turn off the screen automatically when you walk away from the laptop.
LG also includes its own LLM tool for interacting with the laptop: AI Gram Chat. Instead of letting you write prompts to generate an image or a short story, it is made as almost an interactive interface for the computer. I can ask it to summarize a document, change settings, or troubleshoot, to name just a few things it's capable of.
The unique software suite on the LG Gram Pro 16 isn’t limited to AI-focused apps. LG Gram Link is an interesting one that’s included, and lets you quickly share files with other compatible devices, like other LG Grams from 2021 and on, LG TVs and smart monitors, and mobile devices. You can download the LG Gram Link for both Android and iOS, so you’re not limited to an LG device.
The last thing worth mentioning on the software front is that, as interesting as those other apps are and as expensive as this computer can be, you’ll still be subjected to dealing with a free McAfee trial. Since I don’t use or like McAfee, it’s an annoyance with its constant pop-ups. And it’s a piece of software that makes you jump through hoops to uninstall. I don’t like it. Minus five points to LG.
For a laptop, the audio here is pretty good. There’s almost no low end to speak of, but that’s the case for most laptops. Content, whether it’s a movie or music, sounds clear without sounding harsh. If you want excellent audio, get some wireless headphones, but if you don’t have any, the speakers on this laptop are good enough.
Those who are stuck on video calls all day will be happy to know that the webcam looks pretty good. There’s some graininess in low light situations, which is to be expected, but the image is clear and smooth. Plus, you can do the auto framing where the camera zooms in on your face like a 70’s Western. The eye contact feature and background effects are also here. Just be aware that there’s no physical shutter to block the camera. And the built-in mic is similarly capable for Zoom and voice calls.
- Performance score: 4.5 / 5
LG Gram Pro 16 review: Battery life
- Very long battery life
- Has some AI features to extend battery life even longer
LG claims that the Gram Pro 16’s 77Wh battery can last for 27 hours when playing back video when using its AI Battery Efficiency feature). And it might just be able to do that. But I like to test battery life without any special features or tricks. I want to get a good sense of what the battery itself is capable of.
During use, it did in fact last quite a while. I was able to actually play computer games unplugged without running the battery completely down in an hour or two, though it did take a hit. And I would use it unplugged multiple days at a time without charging. Running the PCMark 10 battery benchmark for office use with all the settings midway between performance and battery took almost 17 hours. A chore to sit through, but a great indicator of how good the battery life is.
- Battery Life score: 4.5 / 5
Should I buy the LG Gram Pro 16?
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Value | If you compare the LG Gram Pro 16 to similarly specced laptops trying to do the MacBook Pro 16 thing, they’re all at the same somewhat hard-to-stomach price. | 4 / 5 | 
| Design | I might have some issue with a few choices on this laptop, but it’s thin and light while still offering a big screen. That’s hard to find. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Performance | In that thin and light chassis is a pretty powerful computer, able to handle pretty powerful tasks along with its own AI apps. Just beware the McAfee popups. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Battery Life | Even without LG’s battery efficiency, the battery on this laptop lasts a very long time. | 5 / 5 | 
| Final Score | If price is no object, the LG Gram Pro 16 is a very impressive computer. It’s the full packet (but a light one). | 4.5 / 5 | 
Buy it if…
You want thin, light, and powerful
This laptop comes in under three pounds and is half an inch thick, yet you can run a lot of demanding software on it.
You need long battery life
The LG Gram Pro 16 surprised me with its battery life, especially after experiencing its power. I think you’ll be surprised by it too.
You want to drag and drop files between devices
Using LG Gram Link, you can share files between devices. So, if you want to send a couple pictures from your phone to the laptop for editing, the app makes it simple.
Don't buy it if…
You have any budget concerns
The LG Gram Pro 16 is just priced too high. While I hazard to guess that it’s the use of a new type of material, its price tag is just out of reach for most people.
You don’t like McAfee
This is bloatware. Yes, it can be removed, but you get an added inconvenience to counteract the laptop’s actual conveniences like LG Gram Link.
LG Gram Pro 16 review: Also Consider
If our LG Gram Pro 16 review has you considering other options, here are two laptops to consider...
Samsung Galaxy Book6 Ultra
Thin. Light. With a 16-inch screen. Sound familiar? Well, the Samsung Galaxy Book6 Ultra checks those boxes too. Plus, it’s similarly expensive. However, it does come with more powerful graphics (and a bigger issue with heat).
Read our full Samsung Galaxy Book6 Ultra review
Dell XPS 16 (2026)
The Dell XPS 16 is a premium laptop that’s thin and light with a big screen like the LG Gram Pro 16. Plus, it comes with an OLED screen for about the same price. Its port selection is a bit more limited, however, and it’s a pound heavier.
Read our full Dell XPS 16 (2026) review
How I tested the LG Gram Pro 16
- Tested for a couple weeks
- Used it for work, gaming, and streaming
- Messed with its AI capabilities
I used the LG Gram Pro 16 for a couple weeks. I used it for work, including typing up most of this review (along with the requisite online research). I used it to stream video. I even did some serious gaming. I also played around with the AI and first-party software.
After spending time with the LG Gram Pro 16, it’s clear that this is meant for those who want a large screen in a thin, light package without sacrificing power. That might be a big ask, but LG has done it for a price.
I’ve spent the last few years reviewing tech gear for gaming and otherwise, where I’ve gotten a feel for what to look for and how to put a piece of kit through its paces to see whether it’s worth the recommendation.
- First reviewed: August 2026
James Holland loves checking out gadgets of all sorts, whether it's audio equipment, laptops, or vacuums (especially of the robot variety), and does so for a number of Future Publications including TechRadar, Top Ten Reviews, Homes & Gardens, and T3. He's built up an expertise for in-depth reviewing over the last four years. When he's not putting in the work on the latest tech, he loves to travel, play music, and eat questionable food.

articles.title: Former EVGA employee recounts company’s degrading relationship with Nvidia before 2022 blow-up — forced loss-leader Founders Editions, pricing mandates, and forward-looking tech all led to friction
articles.text:
Former EVGA employee recounts company’s degrading relationship with Nvidia before 2022 blow-up — forced loss-leader Founders Editions, pricing mandates, and forward-looking tech all led to friction
Behind-the-scenes account shows how difficult it was for EVGA to maintain its GPU business.
Former EVGA product manager Brendon Ray Hedrick has posted a personal account of his time at the company in which he details the challenges that EVGA encountered near the end of its partnership with Nvidia. When he left the company in 2019, Hedrick predicted that the business relationship between the two companies would eventually implode, which proved to be largely accurate when EVGA exited the GPU market in 2022.
As he tells it, Hedrick's concerns about the relationship between the two companies began when it first released the Founders Edition GPUs in 2016. While EVGA had sold Nvidia reference designs with its own brand on the box before, its primary (and only) GPU supplier was now competing directly against it by selling graphics cards directly to customers, bypassing board partners entirely.
However, the biggest challenge that EVGA faced arose, according to Hedrick, was when Nvidia began requiring its partners to sell a model that would hit the announced MSRP, even if it sold at a loss. Companies that did not comply would get reduced chip allocations, so partners needed to produce a loss leader product to ensure that they would get all of the chips they would need to satisfy demand.
“The models on which we did not lose money had better circuit boards and cooling of our own, but they also carried a substantial premium,” Hedrick writes. “To a customer comparing them with the advertised starting price, it could look as though EVGA was charging an enormous amount just for those additions.”
In Hedrick's view, as Nvidia Founders Edition cards got better with each generation, more expensive AIB offerings started to make less sense for most buyers. This led to loss-leading models constantly being sold out, while customers who chose more premium models started to hold on to their GPUs for an extra generation or more. “For a manufacturer like EVGA, those decisions carried very different consequences. We still had cards to sell and a business to sustain; enough customers sitting out a generation could be financially devastating,” Hedrick wrote.
In reference to Nvidia's introduction of real-time ray tracing tech on its RTX 20-series cards in 2018, Hedrick recounts that “Nvidia could afford a long technological bet. My concern was whether a company as lean as EVGA could comfortably absorb the difficult part of it,” in reference to convincing consumers that the upgrade to the new tech was worth it at a time when only a tiny handful of games featured RT.
When Hedrick left the company, he says he believed that EVGA and Nvidia had about four or five years left before the situation led to a confrontation. This prediction came true a year earlier than Hedrick projected. In 2022, EVGA announced that it would no longer make partner cards with the advent of the RTX 40-series and that it would exit the GPU market once its stock of RTX 30-series GPUs had run out.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
At that time, it was reported that Nvidia GPUs made up 78% of EVGA’s revenue while contributing only a tiny percentage of the company’s overall profit. Other reports also said that while lower-tier products like the RTX 3060 remained profitable, EVGA lost hundreds of dollars for every RTX 3080 and higher GPU model that it sold.
While it’s easy to blame Nvidia's policies for EVGA’s exit from the GPU market, other analyses partially blamed the company for practices like contracting manufacturing to third parties and providing overly generous customer service for its failures. Its focus on North America and Europe also led to the company shipping fewer units compared to its competitors, meaning its fixed costs were further cutting into its already narrow margins. Although EVGA’s customer-centric approach made it one of the most beloved brands in the GPU space, its strategies ultimately left it vulnerable, and we all know how the story ended.

Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.

articles.title: KI-Agenten für KMU: So entlastet Agentic AI den Mittelstand
articles.text:
Warum KI-Agenten für KMU jetzt relevant werden
Der Mittelstand steht unter Druck: knappe Ressourcen, komplexere Lieferketten, mehr Dokumentationspflichten und steigende Erwartungen an Geschwindigkeit. Genau hier können KI-Agenten ansetzen. Sie übernehmen nicht einfach einzelne Textaufgaben, sondern können Informationen bündeln, Daten prüfen und Arbeitsschritte beschleunigen.
Eine aktuelle YouGov-Umfrage im Auftrag von Alibaba.com und dem Bundesverband E-Commerce und Versandhandel (bevh) zeigt: Rund ein Drittel der KMU sieht administrative Überlastung als konkretes Problem. Rund 40 Prozent nennen Auftragsabwicklung und Kundenservice als besonders zeitintensive Bereiche. Mehr als die Hälfte der KMU ab zehn Mitarbeitern sieht zudem das Potenzial, durch KI-Agenten mindestens zehn Prozent operativer Routineaufgaben einzusparen.
Vom Admin-Overload zu mehr Entscheidungsstärke
Der größte Hebel liegt dort, wo Unternehmen heute besonders viel Zeit verlieren: in fragmentierten Informationen, wiederkehrenden Prüfungen und manuellen Abstimmungen. KI-Agenten können Daten aus verschiedenen Quellen zusammenführen, Dokumente vorstrukturieren, Kriterien abgleichen und nächste Schritte vorbereiten oder ausführen.
Das entlastet Teams im Tagesgeschäft und schafft bessere Grundlagen für Entscheidungen. Besonders relevant ist das in Bereichen wie Auftragsabwicklung, Kundenservice, Compliance, Produktrecherche, Angebotsvorbereitung und internationaler Beschaffung.
Jüngere Entscheider treiben die Nutzung voran
Besonders dynamisch ist die Entwicklung bei jüngeren Führungskräften. In der Gruppe der unter 35-Jährigen nutzen mehr als 62 Prozent bereits Agentic AI. Gleichzeitig investiert in dieser Altersgruppe fast jeder Vierte gezielt in KI-Weiterbildung und ein Drittel sieht ohne KI-Agenten mittelfristig Risiken für die eigene Wettbewerbsfähigkeit. Auch beim Vertrauen in KI-gestützte Ergebnisse liegen jüngere Entscheider klar vorn, etwa bei der Prüfung von Produktinformationen, Lieferantenangaben oder der Vorbereitung von Geschäftsdokumenten. Die Entwicklung ist damit weniger ein Hinweis auf Zurückhaltung im Mittelstand als vielmehr ein positives Signal: Eine neue Generation von Entscheidern zeigt, wie schnell KI-Agenten vom Experiment zum produktiven Werkzeug werden können.
Accio: Agentische KI für den B2B-Alltag
Accio zeigt, wie dieser Wandel praktisch aussehen kann. Die Agentic AI-Plattform unterstützt Unternehmen dabei, Produktideen zu entwickeln, Markt- und Trenddaten zu analysieren, Lieferanteninformationen zu vergleichen, Spezifikationen und Zertifikate schneller einzuordnen und Geschäftsprozesse von Anfang bis Ende zu automatisieren.
Damit adressiert Accio zentrale Engpässe im B2B-Alltag: Recherche, Datenabgleich, Dokumentenprüfung, Angebotsvorbereitung und Beschaffungsentscheidungen. Unternehmen gewinnen Zeit, reduzieren Routineaufwand und können sich stärker auf Bewertung, Strategie und Wachstum konzentrieren.
Alibaba.com lädt Unternehmer aus Deutschland und ganz Europa ein, diese technologischen Möglichkeiten durch den CoCreate Pitch Europe in die Praxis umzusetzen. Der Startup-Wettbewerb unterstützt kleine Unternehmen dabei, den nächsten Schritt in der KI-Nutzung zu gehen. In diesem Jahr werden alle Bewerbungen über Accio eingereicht, von der Marktforschung über Produktideen bis hin zur Bewertung geschäftlicher Chancen. Die europäischen Finalrunden finden am 19. und 20. November in London statt. Weitere Informationen finden Sie auf der Event-Seite zum CoCreate Pitch.
Fazit: Die Chance liegt im Jetzt
Für den Mittelstand liegt die Chance nicht in einem radikalen Bruch, sondern in einem pragmatischen Produktivitätsschub. Wachstumsstarke KMU und jüngere Entscheider machen bereits vor, wie KI-Agenten operative Arbeit erleichtern können. Wer jetzt erste Anwendungsfelder identifiziert, kann Effizienzpotenziale heben, bevor aus Vorsprung Nachholbedarf wird.

articles.title: The AI Tamagotchis are coming
articles.text:
While AI has made plenty of inroads on people’s phones and computers, it’s largely failed in dedicated devices. But over the next year, two major AI companies, Meta and OpenAI, will attempt to change that. And they’re apparently betting on a similar path: testing appetites for physical hardware with their cutesy software agents.
The AI Tamagotchis are coming
Personal AI hardware has mostly crashed and burned. OpenAI and Meta are counting on two selling points: It’s useful, and it’s cute.
The AI Tamagotchis are coming
Personal AI hardware has mostly crashed and burned. OpenAI and Meta are counting on two selling points: It’s useful, and it’s cute.
“Hardware is hard” is a tech industry mantra. Dedicated AI devices like the Friend and Humane AI Pin have inspired mainly frustration and backlash, which may only worsen as public anger toward AI grows. Meta and OpenAI, however, are both pushing ahead. OpenAI is working with famed ex-Apple designer Jony Ive and plans to ship no earlier than February 2027, per a public filing. Meta aims to launch a pendant-like device sooner, before this year’s holiday shopping season.
While OpenAI’s hardware didn’t make an appearance at this year’s DevDay, the company debuted a major new AI agent platform called Dots, complete with personalizable colored blobs with eyes. During a Q&A with reporters after the keynote, when asked whether Dots would make their way into a future physical hardware device, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman replied that that “seems like a very reasonable thing to assume we may do someday,” declining to offer further details.
Meta, meanwhile, is more directly tying its hardware to the recently released Muse agent. Compared by CEO Mark Zuckerberg to a keychain, the device is called the Muse Charm, and it bears a screen featuring its cuddly-looking Muse AI agent, giving it the air of a Tamagotchi. “We’ve packed a lot of technology into this little guy,” Zuckerberg said onstage. “So, if you’re not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show it what’s going on around you.”
Both OpenAI and Meta have likely learned from other companies’ failed hardware rollouts, and their resulting strategy seems to be soft-launching AI agents before hard-launching the hardware. Their solution for hacking the hardware problem is to prime the market by getting people used to AI agents, hoping people will spread the word that “yes, they really work now.” Once people find value in — and even get attached to — the cutesy agents, they might want them in a more physical form. Other companies, like Friend, have taken similar software-first strategies, but Friend was positioned mainly as a companion chatbot, not a productivity tool.
When asked during the DevDay press Q&A whether Dots will likely become the primary interface for interacting with ChatGPT, Thibault Sottiaux, OpenAI’s head of core products, said the company would be “evolving ChatGPT in place to be this incredible personal assistant very soon” and that he believes that as people are able to reach their AI agents via email, text, or phone call, the point of interaction is “all going to blur at some point.” It’ll be a “natural part of your life,” Sottiaux said.
Altman is banking on the fact that Dots will be more useful for long-term tasks than previous iterations of agents on the market have been. “This feels like an always-on helper, collaborator … that you can give very large pieces of work to and it gets to know you and helps proactively over time,” he said during the Tuesday press Q&A.
Both companies’ main bet is that, after years of less-than-impressive AI agents, they can finally deliver a useful everyday tool that will break through to a broader public market. But after Muse’s concerning exploits in Facebook Marketplace, and a Dots voice demo that went awry at DevDay, there’s apparently still some work to do.

articles.title: Spider-Man tendrá una nueva serie live-action estilo 'Spider-Noir' con una de las historias más locas de los cómics
articles.text:
Amazon Prime Video canceló la serie de Spider-Noir tras su primera temporada, pero el Universo Spider-Man sigue más vivo que nunca en la plataforma. Y es que la compañía ya tiene en marcha un nuevo proyecto centrado en el superhéroe de Marvel. Esta vez, adaptarán otra historia totalmente diferente de los cómics.
Según ha informado Deadline, Amazon Prime Video está desarrollando una serie live-action de Spider-Man sobre la segunda Saga del Clon de 1990. Concretamente, se centrará en Ben Reilly y Kaine Parker, dos de los clones más famosos de Peter Parker. Ambos fueron creados por el Chacal, pero tuvieron vidas muy distintas.
Ben Reilly era un clon exacto de Peter que, tras años vagando por el país, decidió regresar a Nueva York y eventualmente asumir la identidad de superhéroe de Araña Escarlata. Este clon tomó el nombre del tío Ben y el apellido de soltera de la tía May. Durante un tiempo y por una confusión, incluso llegó apropiarse de la identidad de Spider-Man.
Por su parte, Kaine Parker fue el primer clon de Peter. Era un clon imperfecto, con habilidades mejoradas pero también con un factor degenerativo y la piel totalmente cubierta con una red de cicatrices. Además, era capaz de dejar en superficies y en personas una marca con su mano, llamada la Marca de Kaine. En un primer momento fue un villano, pero con el tiempo también se convirtió en superhéroe, también llamado Araña Escarlata.
Así será la serie de Spider-Man de la Saga del Clon
La Saga del Clon siempre ha sido una de las historias más famosas y alocadas de los cómics de Spider-Man. Por ello, que Amazon Prime Video le vaya a dedicar una serie genera enorme curiosidad. Eso sí, la fuente señala algo que a los más puristas no les va a gustar nada. Y es que, aunque este arco narrativo de las viñetas sea la inspiración del proyecto, se esperan cambios sustanciales.
Por un lado, se sugiere que la serie podría seguir a Ben y Kaine mientras lidian con sus identidades recién descubiertas como clones. Al mismo tiempo, ambos se enfrentarían a otros clones más perversos. Pero, por otro lado, también se deja la puerta abierta a que la serie altere los orígenes de Ben y Kaine como clones, y que podrían adoptar nuevas identidades.
Prueba Amazon Prime Video totalmente gratis durante 30 días y disfruta del catálogo completo de la plataforma sin límites. Solo con darte de alta tendrás acceso instantáneo a las mejores películas y series, además de envíos gratis en Amazon y otras ventajas.
Por el momento se sabe que Kelvin Yu, creador de la (infravalorada) serie American Born Chinese (Chino americano), será el guionista del título. Y Amy Pascal, Phil Lord y Christopher Miller también regresarán como productores ejecutivos. Por ahora, se desconoce la fecha de estreno o el reparto que la protagonizará.

articles.title: Instinct's new product recommendations are giving some users the ick | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The buzzy AI startup Instinct has just revealed a new potential revenue stream: product recommendations. Unfortunately for the company, the rollout is already rubbing some users the wrong way.
Overnight, the AI agent began pushing product suggestions to users as part of a new feature called Instinct Selections, an effort to curate personalized lists for users in areas like dining, travel, and shopping.
Founder Noah Shinn announced the feature’s debut later Tuesday, explaining that the idea is to partner with “local chefs, designers, architects, travel guides,” and others to bring “human taste” to its product.
In other words, instead of only relying on what the AI could suggest based on its training data gathered from the wider web, the company is partnering with people to offer human-curated suggestions, too. (Instinct didn’t share who, exactly, those human partners are.)
“The next time you’re looking for a restaurant, Instinct can pull from a list handpicked by chefs who know the hidden gems in your area,” Shinn wrote on X.
“If you want to find a new trail to explore, Instinct can draw on recommendations from local guides and suggest a few routes that fit your preferences. And if you’re looking to add some color to your home, Instinct will find pieces from independent designers that match your style, space, and budget,” he continued. “Our goal is to deliver world-class recommendations that are differentiated in quality from what you might find on the internet, and from what other chatbots produce,” he said.
But the initial reaction to these seemingly unsolicited product pushes has not been fully positive.
“I didn’t need to buy carry-on luggage, sunglasses, or a brim hat. This feels so disappointing. At least make me a personalized shopping list of things I actually need!!” Shruti Gandhi, a general partner at the AI-focused investing firm Array VC, wrote on X.
Another entrepreneur, Andrew Yeung, confirmed on X that he also received product recommendations that he hadn’t asked for, which can feel off-putting.
A third user, Chat Joglekar, the founder of a business-buying marketplace, wrote, “I had my first ‘ewwww’ moment with an AI assistant when Instinct started to suggest products that I should buy based on what I had in email and upcoming trips.”
The trick to making curated suggestions useful is to make sure they’re something the user is actually asking for, or at least fit naturally within the current conversation. That way, it feels like the assistant is trying to be helpful, not advertising to you.
If the product suggestions are going to arrive at random intervals, as Instinct’s have been, then they need to be highly personalized, excellent picks — otherwise the user will feel like they’ve been spammed.
That’s not likely to endear users to the AI agent at a time when it’s competing with agents from bigger companies, like Meta and now OpenAI, which don’t do this.
Instinct didn’t share whether it’s currently making money from these recommendations or plans to, but the feature seems ripe for some sort of advertising, commerce, or affiliate play.
TechCrunch has asked the company for further comment.
The product suggestions launched shortly after Instinct confirmed its most recent financing, a $1 billion Series C round that values the company at $10 billion. The company has not yet said how many people actually use its product, a figure that would help justify that valuation, but in a recent podcast, Shinn noted that the agent regularly handles transactions for its users.
In that same podcast interview, with investor Patrick O’Shaughnessy, Shinn said the platform is approaching a billion dollars in annual transactions made through the agent and that more than 50% of them are related to travel.

articles.title: Voyeurisme sordide ou science ? La nouvelle série de Netflix choque les spectateurs
articles.text:
En 1971, l’expérience de Stanford, menée avec 24 étudiants tous masculins, devait durer deux semaines. Elle s’était arrêtée au bout de six jours dans un bain de larmes, de maltraitances psychologiques et de sadisme incontrôlé. Un désastre éthique devenu le cas d’école de tout ce qu’il ne faut pas faire en sciences humaines. Plus d’un demi-siècle plus tard, Netflix en a fait une série de six épisodes de 45 minutes.
Prévue pour le 21 octobre 2026, la série Netflix de téléréalité enferme pendant deux semaines 30 volontaires (hommes et femmes, cette fois) dans un vrai pénitencier, filmées 24 heures sur 24 par des caméras télécommandées. La productrice exécutive Jane Lipsitz a beau jurer sur tous les toits que son équipe a prévu des « garde-fous », des psychologues 24/7 et des mots de passe pour abandonner, la ficelle est trop grosse. Présenter ce divertissement comme une « réinvention moderne » de la célèbre étude revient à emballer de la téléréalité trash dans du papier cadeau universitaire.
Une série Netflix qui pose question
Il n’a pas fallu plus de quelques heures après l’annonce de la série, pour que les réseaux sociaux s’enflamment. Sur X, l’incompréhension a très vite laissé place au dégoût et à l’ironie mordante.
Avec une éthique vendue au clic, les internautes s’insurgent contre le cynisme de la plateforme. « Est-ce qu’on fait vraiment ça ou est-ce qu’on fait juste semblant que les comités d’éthique n’existent plus pour le bien de l’algorithme ? », s’interroge une utilisatrice, tandis qu’un autre résume le projet d’une formule assassine : « L’original a été stoppé après six jours et Netflix a répondu : ‘Hold my beer, on va en faire un truc à binger’. »
Plusieurs internautes rappellent que la méthode de 1971 a depuis été démontée. Dans son enquête Histoire d’un mensonge (2018), le chercheur français Thibault Le Texier a montré, archives à l’appui, que les gardiens avaient reçu des consignes de Zimbardo avant l’expérience. « Le pire, c’est que l’expérience d’origine était bidonnée. Les gardes étaient poussés à être violents », rappelle un internaute.
D’autres ironisent sur la différence fondamentale entre une étude de 1971 et une émission de 2026 : « Zimbardo a tout coupé au bout de six jours. Une émission de télé a toutes les raisons du monde de laisser tourner les caméras. »
La critique ne vient pas seulement des internautes. Clay Ramsay, le « prisonnier 416 » de l’expérience originale, qui avait fait une grève de la faim en 1971, a confié à Newsweek qu’il craignait que la série brouille la frontière entre divertissement et science.
Du laboratoire au divertissement de masse
Pour désamorcer la polémique, la production met en avant un casting mixte, des tests psychologiques avant l’entrée en prison et trois experts : Alison Wood Brooks, psychologue comportementale à Harvard, Trymaine Lee, journaliste lauréat du prix Pulitzer, et Michael Cantrell, ancien professionnel de l’administration pénitentiaire fédérale, avec près de trente ans de carrière.
La vraie perversion du projet réside dans le dispositif lui-même. La simulation s’installe dans une vraie prison, au milieu d’authentiques détenus qui servent de décor d’ambiance. En prétendant répondre à la question « le pouvoir corrompt-il ? », Netflix réutilise en réalité la mécanique la plus ancienne du genre : enfermer des cobayes dans un bocal social pour observer jusqu’où la pression les fera craquer. À la différence près qu’ici, on habille le spectacle du vernis respectable de la science comportementale.
La télévision a déjà tenté l’exercice. En 2002, la BBC a diffusé The Experiment, où les psychologues Alex Haslam et Steve Reicher reproduisaient l’étude de Stanford. Un comité d’éthique suivait le tournage sur place, et les chercheurs se contentaient d’observer, alors que Zimbardo dirigeait lui-même sa prison. Les prisonniers ont fini par se serrer les coudes pour obtenir de meilleures conditions, à l’opposé du scénario de 1971.
Il faudra attendre la mise en ligne des six épisodes, le 21 octobre, pour savoir ce que les participants ont vécu pendant ces deux semaines.

articles.title: Wenn Microsoft das Postfach sperrt: Warum die Niederlande ihre Verwaltung auf NixOS umstellen
articles.text:
Wenn Microsoft das Postfach sperrt: Warum die Niederlande ihre Verwaltung auf Linux umstellen
Die Niederlande entwickeln einen eigenen Behördendesktop auf Basis freier Software. Das Projekt trägt den Namen DAWO, kurz für „Digitaal Autonome Werkomgeving Overheid“ – also „digital autonome Arbeitsumgebung der Regierung“. Als Betriebssystem hat sich der Staat für die Linux-Distribution NixOS entschieden. Acht Kommunen in dem Land testen das System bereits in der Praxis, organisiert über den Gemeindeverband VNG. DAWO ist dabei kein fertiges Produkt, sondern eher eine Art Bauplan: Er beschreibt eine komplette Arbeitsumgebung aus austauschbaren Bausteinen für Betriebssystem, Cloudinfrastruktur, Kommunikation, KI und gemeinsames Arbeiten an Dokumenten, wobei es stets um Souveränität geht.
Drei staatliche IT-Dienstleister entwickeln
Im Juli 2026 beauftragte die zuständige „interdepartementale Kommission für den Geschäftsbetrieb des Staatsdienstes“ (ICBR) drei staatliche IT-Dienstleister mit der Umsetzung: SSC-ICT, DICTU und DUO-ICT. Die übergeordnete Blaupause für das Projekt kommt aus dem Ministerium für Inneres. Beim Betriebssystem für die Arbeitsplatzrechner probierte das Projekt zunächst openSUSE und Fedora aus, entschied sich dann aber für NixOS.
Ein zentraler Baustein dabei ist „MijnBureau“, eine von den Behörden selbst betriebene Suite für den Arbeitsplatz. Sie kombiniert Nextcloud für Dateien, Collabora für Office-Aufgaben, Element für die Kommunikation und OpenProject für das Projektmanagement. Hier läuft das Vorhaben auch schon europäisch: Das Team hinter MijnBureau arbeitet mit dem französischen Projekt La Suite zusammen und orientiert sich an openDesk, dem entsprechenden Vorhaben in Deutschland.
US-Sanktionen als Beschleuniger
Den Anstoß für DAWO gab laut dem niederländischen Tech-Portal Tweakers unter anderem die Erfahrung mit US-Sanktionen gegen den Internationalen Strafgerichtshof (ICC) in Den Haag. Microsoft kappte damals das E-Mail-Konto des damaligen Chefanklägers Karim Khan auf Druck der US-Regierung.
Der Fall zeigte, dass der Zugang zu wichtigen digitalen Werkzeugen von politischen Entscheidungen anderer Länder abhängen kann. Dieses Risiko will die niederländische Regierung offenbar nicht länger eingehen.

articles.title: Reddit says it has to cut back access to ‘Old Reddit’ because of AI bots
articles.text:
Reddit is further limiting who can use the “Old Reddit” experience as part of its efforts to combat scraping and automated traffic. Reddit recently started forcing users to log in to be able to use Old Reddit, but in the “next few months,” the company says that you’ll have to be logged in and have used Old Reddit within the last six months from when the change rolls out to be able to continue browsing the platform with the classic experience.
Reddit says it has to cut back access to ‘Old Reddit’ because of AI bots
Viewing the old Reddit UI will get even harder if you’re not a mod, now that it’s only available to accounts that have used it recently.
Reddit says the six-month window covers “the vast majority of all Old Reddit users.” The announcement didn’t go into detail, but it’s clearly aimed at blocking not just new account creation for bots, but also any bots that might access unused or abandoned accounts. As part of the changes, Reddit will stop supporting RSS feeds on November 13th because RSS is “now a common surface for large-scale scraping and automated abuse,” and suggested replacements like Discord Relay for moderation help.
Reddit:
If you use RSS for feeds outside of a community you moderate, there is no replacement. We know RSS has been a beloved part of the open web for a long time, and we’re grateful to everyone who used it to stay connected to Reddit.
The company has been waging war against unsanctioned access to its data for some time, including blocking the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine to prevent AI scraping, suing Anthropic over alleged unauthorized bot access, and striking deals with Google and OpenAI to use Reddit data for training. Reddit knows that Old Reddit is beloved by many users, and in May 2025, CEO Steve Huffman said the company would “keep it online as long as people are using it.” But this past August, Huffman said that Reddit had gotten to a point where “we need to make some changes” because the experience was being used by “everyone who spams, scrapes, or does anything bad on Reddit.”
In its announcement today, Reddit said that the recent login requirement for Old Reddit “helped reduce scraping and automated abuse” but “still allowed any logged-in account to access Old Reddit, including accounts with no prior Old Reddit use.” Logged-in moderators, however, will still be able to use Old Reddit without a recent usage requirement.
Reddit also shared updates for the previously announced transition moving apps and bots that use Reddit’s public data API to the company’s developer platform. Reddit will begin removing API access for users that haven’t registered their apps by January 12th, 2027, and all remaining public API access “will end in March 2027.”

articles.title: FedEx orders 2,000 electric trucks from Harbinger in $300M deal | TechCrunch
articles.text:
FedEx is ordering 2,000 electric trucks from EV startup Harbinger in a deal worth $300 million. Harbinger, which already has trucks in production, plans to deliver all 2,000 by the end of next year, the company told TechCrunch.
It’s the largest bulk order yet for Harbinger, which was founded in 2022 by former employees of Anduril, defunct EV startup Canoo, and QuantumScape. Bloomberg News first reported the new order Wednesday morning. FedEx led a $160 million Series C funding round for Harbinger late last year.
Harbinger’s pitch since its inception has been to make one main product: an electric medium-duty commercial truck chassis. That simplified approach appears to have paid off, as the company is in production and generating revenue despite being just a few years old. It has already delivered 53 trucks to FedEx as part of an order that the shipping giant placed alongside last year’s fundraise.
That said, Harbinger has started to look at other possible revenue lines. The company is getting into hybrid emergency vehicles, acquired an autonomous driving company in February, and is selling the battery packs it developed as energy storage. The company is also getting into defense use cases. All this comes as Axios reported in May that the company is considering an IPO.

articles.title: Avant même sa sortie, l'iPhone Duo s'apprête à chambouler le marché des pliables : les chiffres
articles.text:
Apple débarque tard sur le marché des smartphones pliables, mais les analystes lui promettent déjà une place de choix. Seule ombre au tableau : des usines qui peinent à suivre…
Les précommandes de l’iPhone Duo, présenté en grande pompe par la marque à la pomme le 9 septembre dernier, ouvriront le 16 octobre. Vendu à partir de la maudite somme de 2 339 euros, l’appareil arrive sur un segment encore très modeste, puisque les pliables ne représentent qu’environ 2 % des smartphones vendus dans le monde. Dans ce contexte, combien d’exemplaires Apple peut-elle espérer écouler ?
Un quart du marché dès la première année
Une estimation chiffrée vient en effet de tomber. Selon Counterpoint Research, qui suit trimestre par trimestre les livraisons de tous les grands fabricants de smartphones, Apple devrait livrer environ 6 millions d’iPhone Duo d’ici à la fin de l’année. Petite précision, ce chiffre fait référence aux appareils expédiés aux revendeurs et aux opérateurs, pas encore achetés par les clients.
Mais rapporté au marché, ce volume pèse lourd, explique Bloomberg. Le géant californien s’emparerait ainsi d’environ 25 % des livraisons mondiales de pliables en 2026. De quoi se hisser directement à la deuxième place, derrière Samsung (38 %) mais devant Huawei (22 %). Le tout avec à peine dix semaines de commercialisation.
L’arrivée d’Apple profiterait d’ailleurs à tout le segment. IDC, autre grand nom des études de marché, table sur 22,9 millions de pliables livrés cette année au total, soit une hausse de près de 13 % en glissement annuel. Sans l’iPhone Duo, le marché aurait au contraire reculé de plus de 10 %.
Le défi se joue sur les lignes d’assemblage
Mais ces projections reposent sur une condition essentielle : la production. Car atteindre les 6 millions d’unités dépend de la vitesse à laquelle Apple montera en cadence. Le chiffre fait donc figure de plafond plutôt que de moyenne. Les autres estimations vont dans le même sens, avec 5 millions pour TrendForce et 6 millions pour l’analyste Jeff Pu.
Ces volumes restent modestes à l’échelle d’Apple. Par exemple, un iPhone Pro se vend habituellement à 20 ou 30 millions d’exemplaires sur l’ensemble de sa carrière. Pour le marché des pliables, en revanche, c’est un séisme.
Mais la tâche s’annonce délicate sur les lignes d’assemblage. Chez Foxconn, le principal sous-traitant d’Apple, à peine plus de 60 % des appareils assemblés auraient passé les contrôles qualité à la mi-septembre. De même, les écrans pliables fournis par Samsung Display et la charnière, composée de plus de 100 pièces, auraient aussi pris du retard. Il faudrait encore environ six mois pour tourner à plein régime.

articles.title: Tracing Agent Harness Behavior with NVIDIA NeMo Relay | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
An agent can finish a task and still take an inefficient path. A failed search can trigger another search. A truncated file read can lead to a command fetching the same content again. A correct final answer hides those extra steps, even though they increase latency and consume tokens. Inefficiencies create more chances for failure.
To improve an agent’s behavior, developers must understand whether a task succeeded and how the agent completed it. A success check by itself cannot explain why an agent recovered from a tool error, stopped early, or needed extra model calls.
In this tutorial, you’ll run two Hermes Agent examples with NVIDIA NeMo Relay. You’ll use the resulting traces to inspect model and tool calls, errors, retries, duration, and token use, then compare that evidence with each task’s verification result. A Hermes ToolPerf case study shows how to use the same approach to evaluate harness changes across repeated runs.
This tutorial and video explain how to:
- Set up an isolated Hermes Agent runtime with its native NeMo Relay integration.
- Run a simple terminal tool task and inspect its event stream and trajectory.
- Run a file-and-web research task and explore its OpenTelemetry trace in Arize Phoenix.
- Combine task verification with trace evidence to evaluate a change to an agent harness.
Prerequisites
Before you begin, make sure you have:
- macOS or Linux
- Git and curl
- Docker Desktop or Docker Engine installed and running
- An NVIDIA Build API key for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Open the model page and select Generate API Key.
Next is an overview of the technologies used for this tutorial and how they work together.
How NeMo Relay works with Hermes Agent harness
NeMo Relay gives agent developers a common way to observe and control model and tool execution. The popular agent harness Hermes Agent includes NeMo Relay natively and represents its sessions, turns, model calls, and tool calls in NeMo Relay’s scope hierarchy. NeMo Relay records lifecycle events as work begins and ends, preserving its timing and parent-child relationships.
Understand the trace outputs
NeMo Relay is used for agent observability. You will work with three representations of agent execution:
| Format | What it contains | When to use it | 
|---|---|---|
| Agent Trajectory Observability Format (ATOF) | A JSONL log of scope starts, scope ends, and point-in-time mark, with IDs and timestamps to reconstruct the agent run. | Use ATOF to debug or audit individual events, timing, and parent-child relationships. | 
| Agent Trajectory Interchange Format (ATIF) | A step-by-step JSON record of agent interactions, tool calls, and observations, assembled from lifecycle events. | Use ATIF to review, analyze, or evaluate the agent’s path step by step. | 
| OpenTelemetry with OpenInference | OpenTelemetry records the run as parent-child spans. OpenInference labels agent, LLM, and tool spans and defines their attributes. | Use it in OTEL-compliant tools like Phoenix, to inspect model and tool calls, duration, token use, and errors. | 
An ATIF tool request shows what the model asked to run, but it does not confirm the outcome. To verify what happened, inspect ATOF for the matching tool start and end events and any recorded errors. Their shared uuid pairs the events, while parent_uuid connects the tool call to its parent.
Review traces before sharing them. Depending on your configuration, they can contain prompts, model responses, tool arguments and results, file paths, and other application data.
For agent safety and security governance, NeMo Relay helps provide the evidence layer: structured traces and trajectories that enterprises, evaluators, and security systems can use to investigate agent behavior, evaluate policies, improve controls, or create specialized security plugins that extend Relay.
Let’s get started with the first agent task run.
Experiment #1: Run a simple tool-use task with Hermes Agent
The first example is intentionally small so you can verify the complete setup before adding web search and Phoenix. Hermes uses its terminal tool to run the included Python script inside an isolated Docker container. The script prints: VALUE=42.
That fixed output gives the runner an exact success check. A passing run also confirms that Hermes reached the model, invoked the terminal tool in the sandbox, and produced both Relay trace files.
The container cannot access the network, repository checkout, or NVIDIA API key. Hermes also cannot fall back to running terminal commands on the host.
Run the following commands in order. After copying keys.env, add your NVIDIA API key to that file before continuing.
# Clone the tutorial repository.
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/nemoclaw-community
# Enter the cloned repository.
cd nemoclaw-community/examples/tools/hermes-relay-tracing
# Create the isolated Hermes Agent and NeMo Relay runtime.
./scripts/setup_tutorial_runtime.sh
# Copy the API key template.
cp keys.env.example keys.env
# Add NVIDIA_API_KEY to keys.env before continuing.
# Verify that Docker is running.
docker version
# Build the Docker image for the terminal-tool task.
./scripts/build_tutorial_image.sh
# Run the task and generate the ATOF and ATIF traces.
./scripts/run_tutorial.sh
The Hermes Agent and NeMo Relay processes run from this repository’s local environment. Docker is used separately for the terminal tool sandbox and the local Phoenix service.
The setup script in the repository creates a self-contained environment under .tutorial-runtime/ with all the appropriate dependencies like Python 3.11 and Hermes 0.21.1 with NeMo Relay 0.8.3. It does not modify your existing Python or Hermes installation.
When the task finishes, the runner checks the response and both trace files. A passing run prints the verification result, followed by the ATOF and ATIF summaries.
Review the trace summaries
After Hermes completes the task, the runner verifies the expected result and the generated traces. It checks that the terminal command succeeded, that the ATOF trace contains completed LLM activity with token usage and no tool errors, and that a nonempty ATIF trajectory was created. The following output comes from one verified run. Token counts, identifiers, and file paths can vary between runs.
ATOF summary
events: 74
completed llm scopes: 2
llm scopes with usage: 2
prompt tokens: 7239
completion tokens: 96
total tokens: 7335
tool calls: 1
tool errors: 0
correlated events: 74
ATIF summary
agent: Hermes Agent
model: nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b
steps: 3
llm calls: 2
requested tool calls: 1
Task verified: VALUE=42
Artifacts: .../artifacts/runs/<run-id>
Look for the line with Task verified: VALUE=42, which confirms the expected result. The ATOF summary reports the completed model scopes, token usage, tool calls, and tool errors. The ATIF summary presents the same execution as a three-step trajectory.
The path following Artifacts: identifies the run directory containing the complete ATOF event stream and ATIF trajectory. The companion repository explains how to inspect or summarize either file again.
Experiment #2: Run a multi-tool research task and explore its traces
After verifying the basic setup, this second example uses the same Hermes and NeMo Relay environment for a task that requires several tools. Hermes receives a travel record containing clues about an unnamed machine-learning conference. It must read the record, find a conference matching the subject, dates, and location, confirm the answer on the official website, save the verified information in a report, and return the conference name.
Use NeMo Relay’s OpenInference exporter to send OpenTelemetry spans to Arize Phoenix over OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol). Phoenix displays the run as an interactive trace, where you can inspect model and tool calls, timing, token usage, errors, and available inputs and outputs.
You can send the same OpenTelemetry trace to other OTLP-compatible backends, such as LangSmith, by changing the endpoint and authentication settings. The NeMo Relay observability guide describes other available exporters and configuration options.
The example reuses the NVIDIA Nemotron model and NVIDIA API key from the first example. Hermes uses its built-in keyless web search, and the runner starts Phoenix in a pinned local container. Run the conference search example:
./scripts/run_conference_research_with_phoenix.sh
During the run, NeMo Relay saves the ATOF event stream and ATIF trajectory locally.
Before reporting success, the runner checks that Hermes:
- Identified COLT 2026 as a conference name
- Saved a report containing the expected conference details and official source
- Successfully completed the read_file ,web_search ,web_extract , andwrite_file calls
- Produced a nonempty ATIF trajectory
- Sent model and tool spans with positive token usage to Phoenix
After the checks pass, the terminal output includes a link to the Phoenix project and the local run directory. Open the project in Phoenix to follow the agent run from the initial file read through the web search, source verification, report write, and final response.
Try the task with another model
To see how another model handles the same conference query, follow the model-profile instructions in the companion repository. Keep the query, available tools, execution limits, and verifier unchanged so you can inspect how the execution path differs.
Because the task uses live web search, use these runs to explore behavior rather than rank models. A controlled comparison requires fixed search responses and repeated runs.
Use traces to evaluate an agent harness change
The two examples show how to verify a result and inspect one run. Evaluating a harness change requires the same checks under controlled, repeated conditions.
Steps for agent harness evaluation
- Choose a fixed task with an exact, automated success check.
- Define a baseline and one focused change to the prompt, tool, configuration, or harness.
- Keep everything except that change constant, including the model snapshot, provider, task input, execution budget, and timeout.
- Run the same number of repetitions for the baseline and candidate with NeMo Relay enabled.
- Compare verified task outcomes first. Then use the traces to examine model calls, tool calls, retries, errors, elapsed time, token usage, and cost.
- Repeat the evaluation across the models or workloads that the change is expected to support before generalizing the result.
Call the candidate an improvement only when it produces a repeatable increase in task completion or preserves completion while improving the reliability, latency, or cost measure you intended to change. One faster run or fewer calls can help explain a result, but neither establishes an optimization by itself.
An unchanged result is useful as well. It can show that an apparent improvement depended on a particular model, environment, or sample.
Benchmark case study for evaluating Hermes tool-layer changes
The Hermes ToolPerf benchmark was developed by Nous Research after analyzing production sessions, auditing tool schemas, and mining production session logs for failure classes. Then, NeMo Relay ATOF traces were used for ground-truth turn accounting. By examining nine failure patterns, the results were turned into deterministic benchmark cases and then used to evaluate a batch of Hermes tool-layer fixes.
The August 6 rerun compared the pinned baseline of Hermes and fixed revisions across nine tasks. Each task ran three times per model per arm, giving 108 runs total, with the same prompts, tools, execution limits, and success checks throughout. A task verifier measured completion, and the NeMo Relay ATOF traces captured model calls, tool calls, errors, retries, tool-result data, and timing.
| Model | Arm | Task success | Mean LLM calls | Mean tool calls | Mean tool result data | Mean duration | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Sonnet 4.5 | Baseline | 24/27 (89%) | 2.9 | 2.2 | 17 KB | 16 s | 
| Claude Sonnet 4.5 | Fixes | 23/27 (85%) | 2.8 | 2.1 | 17 KB | 22 s | 
| Qwen3 Coder 30B | Baseline | 19/27 (70%) | 3.8 | 2.8 | 16 KB | 27 s | 
| Qwen3 Coder 30B | Fixes | 22/27 (81%) | 4.9 | 3.9 | 33 KB | 42 s | 
In this run, Sonnet showed no real change. It finished 24 of 27 runs on baseline and 23 of 27 on fixes, a difference of one run. Its turns, tool calls, and result data were the same on both arms.
Qwen Coder is where the fixes did something, and the effect cuts two ways. It completed three more tasks successfully, going from 19 of 27 to 22 of 27. It also worked harder for them: mean LLM calls rose from 3.8 to 4.9, tool calls from 2.8 to 3.9, tool-result data from 16 KB to 33 KB, and duration from 27 s to 42 s. The fixes brought success to tasks the baseline abandoned, and the price was a slower, chattier agent.
The task-level audit shows where those trade-offs come from.
- On the blocked-command task, baseline Qwen died at the parser block and scored 33%, while the recovery recipes took the fixes arm to 100%. That completion is the reason the turn count went up: recovering costs turns that giving up never spends.
- The case-insensitive search task moved the other way. The zero-match probe output pushed Qwen into extra exploratory searches on two of three reps, taking it from 3.3 turns to 9.3, a regression worth its own look.
- The hidden-file search stayed at 0 to 33% on both arms and both models, the same gap the original run found and still open at these SHAs.
The success or failure of tasks alone could not have produced this conclusion. The NeMo Relay traces recorded every model call, tool call, error, retry, result payload, and timing for all 108 runs. Qwen’s extra turns were recoveries rather than flailing, and that one task’s regression traced back to a specific probe output. The traces are checked into the results directory, so anyone can unpack them and regenerate these tables from the raw records.
Get started with evaluating agent traces
NeMo Relay gives you a consistent way to capture evidence for evaluating changes to optimize your agent harnesses. ATOF preserves the ordered lifecycle events, while ATIF presents the same work as a readable trajectory. Pairing these traces with a deterministic verifier enables you to compare harness changes without confusing fewer calls with better results.
The companion repository provides the sample artifacts, including the runnable tasks, verifiers, NeMo Relay configuration, and Phoenix setup used in this post.
Learn more:
- NeMo Relay documentation for installation, concepts, and configuration.
- Hermes Agent documentation for installing and using Hermes.
- Companion tutorial repository for the runnable examples from this post.
- ATOF and ATIF documentation for the event and trajectory formats.
- NeMo Relay observability configuration for configuring exporters and telemetry destinations.
- Supported integrations for using NeMo Relay with other agent frameworks and applications.

articles.title: Amazon brade sa Kindle 2024 à moins de 90 € avant l'arrivée de sa remplaçante
articles.text:
La relève de la Kindle d’entrée de gamme se précise. Le 28 septembre, le site allemand WinFuture a publié des images présentées comme officielles de la 12e génération de la liseuse (les visuels sont détaillés sur Frandroid). On y voit un écran aux coins arrondis, un bouton d’alimentation qui passe du bas de la liseuse au haut de la tranche droite, et quatre coloris : noir, bleu clair, vert et violet. Amazon n’a encore rien confirmé et aucune date de sortie n’a filtré.
En attendant, Amazon fait de la place dans ses rayons. La Kindle 2024 passe à 89,99 € au lieu de 154,99 € dans sa version avec publicités, soit 65 € d’économie. La promotion tombe en pleine rentrée littéraire, au moment où les soirées raccourcissent.
Il faut quand même relativiser ce « prix de référence ». À sa sortie fin 2024, la Kindle 2024 coûtait 109,99 € dans sa version avec publicités. Elle est brièvement passée à 154,99 € début septembre (169,99 € sans publicités). Par rapport à son prix de lancement, la remise est donc de 20 €.
Que vaut la Kindle 2024 ?
La Kindle 2024 est la liseuse la plus simple de la gamme d’Amazon. Elle a un écran de 6 pouces à encre électronique (E Ink), une technologie qui reflète la lumière comme une page imprimée et ne consomme de l’énergie qu’au moment où la page change. Sa résolution de 300 pixels par pouce, la même que sur les modèles plus chers, donne un texte net, sans effet de flou autour des lettres. Un éclairage avant réglable permet de lire dans le noir, et un mode sombre affiche le texte en blanc sur fond noir.
Elle est équipée de 16 Go de stockage, de quoi garder des milliers de livres. Le Bluetooth sert à écouter des livres audio avec un casque ou une enceinte sans fil. Amazon annonce jusqu’à six semaines d’autonomie, sur la base d’une demi-heure de lecture par jour avec le Wi-Fi coupé. La recharge passe par un port USB-C et prend environ deux heures avec un adaptateur secteur de 9 W, vendu à part.
La liseuse pèse 158 g pour 8 mm d’épaisseur, de quoi la glisser dans la poche d’un manteau. Elle a quand même quelques limites. Elle n’est pas étanche, donc on évite la lecture dans le bain. Son éclairage reste en lumière froide, sans réglage de teinte plus chaude pour le soir. Le bouton d’alimentation est placé sur la tranche inférieure, à un endroit peu pratique, et c’est justement ce que la prochaine génération semble corriger. Les fichiers EPUB, enfin, doivent passer par le service d’envoi d’Amazon pour être lus.
À ce prix, la Kindle 2024 est-elle une bonne affaire ?
D’après les images qui ont fuité, la nouvelle génération changerait surtout de look. Elle garderait un écran d’environ 6 pouces, aux coins arrondis et peut-être avec un éclairage un peu plus puissant, selon WinFuture. Son prix reste inconnu. Si vous cherchez avant tout une liseuse pour lire des romans, le modèle actuel en fait déjà l’essentiel.
Rien ne garantit en revanche que cette remise dure jusqu’à l’annonce officielle, ni que les stocks tiennent. Amazon n’a communiqué ni le prix ni la date de sortie de la 12e génération. À 89,99 €, la Kindle 2024 permet de se constituer une première bibliothèque numérique sans l’attendre.
